items.food_status_note: Oily fish, egg yolk and UV-treated mushrooms supply measurable vitamin D, and fortified fat spreads, milk, breakfast cereals and juices add small amounts, so this is a genuine dietary nutrient rather than a manufactured one. The RICH label needs qualifying on two counts: the food base is narrow (oily fish, egg yolk, UV-treated mushrooms), and two of the stronger rows below are not ordinary foods, since cod liver oil behaves as a supplement and fortified orange juice is a manufactured delivery vehicle. Population evidence points the same way, because SACN concluded the 10 µg/day RNI is difficult to achieve from natural food sources and set it as a year-round RNI for everyone aged 4 and over; UK mean intakes from food are around a third of that (the often-quoted NDNS figures of 2.8 µg/day at ages 19 to 65 and 3.3 µg/day in over-65s are carried here as uncorroborated, since the full SACN report could not be retrieved to confirm them).
items.dose_from_food_note: 1,000 IU (25 µg), the low end of ordinary supplement doses, is about 150 g of cooked sockeye salmon every day, or 155 g to 463 g of grilled herring depending on which herring value holds. 4,000 IU (100 µg) is roughly 600 g of sockeye salmon, 621 g to 1.85 kg of herring, about 109 large egg yolks, or about 890 g of UV-treated portabella mushrooms daily. A 50,000 IU (1,250 µg) weekly loading dose has no food equivalent: 7.5 kg of sockeye salmon, or 7.8 to 23.1 kg of grilled herring. One food gets close on mass alone, UV-treated maitake at the top of its measured range, where 178 g would carry 4,000 IU, and that content is unlabelled, spans 0.1 to 56.1 µg/100 g by growing method and is D2 rather than D3. Above roughly 50 degrees north, cutaneous synthesis is effectively zero from October to March, so there is no sunlight to close the winter shortfall.

items.form_caveat: Mushroom vitamin D is D2 (ergocalciferol), a different molecule from the D3 in fish, egg yolk and almost all supplements, and D3 raises serum 25(OH)D more effectively, with the gap widest for intermittent bolus dosing (Tripkovic et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2012;95:1357-64, PMID 22552031, DOI 10.3945/ajcn.111.031070, mean difference 34.10 nmol/L for bolus dosing, P = 0.0002; the advantage is lost with daily dosing, P = 0.10). UV mushroom content is wildly variable and usually unlabelled: USDA measured UV-treated portabella at 3.4 µg/100 g from one producer and 25.6 µg/100 g from another, maitake from 0.1 to 56.1 µg/100 g by growing method, and untreated white mushrooms at 0.1 to 0.2 µg/100 g, so buying ordinary mushrooms because 'mushrooms have vitamin D' gets you essentially nothing. Species and provenance matter as much as the food name: the salmon row is wild sockeye, while farmed Atlantic salmon, which is what most shoppers buy, runs several-fold lower, so 'salmon' on a pack does not deliver the sockeye figure. Cod liver oil is nominally a food but behaves as a supplement and carries 18,000 µg retinol per 100 g (CoFID 17-488, unconfirmed), so a tablespoon delivers about 8,160 IU of preformed vitamin A alongside the D3, which rules it out in pregnancy. Several real UK vehicles are missing from the table for want of a verifiable figure and should not be forgotten: fortified margarine and fat spreads (a statutory UK vitamin D vehicle for decades, and a larger contributor to UK intake than the US fortified orange juice listed), fortified breakfast cereals, kippers and other smoked herring, canned red sockeye (higher than the canned pink listed), herring and cod roe, and sun-dried shiitake for D2. Oily fish delivers D3 inside a fat matrix with EPA/DHA, protein, iodine and selenium; a capsule delivers D3 alone.
items.bioavailability: Vitamin D from both food and capsules is fat-soluble and absorbed better with a meal containing fat, which oily fish and egg yolk supply themselves. Form matters more than source: D2 from mushrooms is less effective per microgram than D3 (PMID 22552031). Egg yolk additionally contains 25-hydroxycholecalciferol, an already-hydroxylated metabolite that supplements do not normally provide. Composition tables bundle 25-OH-D3 into the headline total under the convention total = cholecalciferol + 5 x 25-OH-D3, so a 'vitamin D' number for eggs, trout or canned salmon is not strictly comparable to the D3 in a capsule; the canned pink salmon (12.1 + 5 x 0.30 = 13.6), trout (7.19 + 5 x 0.20 = 8.19) and whole egg (2.30 + 5 x 0.18 = 3.20) totals here all follow it.
items.data_confidence: LOW. The single richest confirmed food (cooked sockeye salmon) and the UV portabella and fortified orange juice values check out, but most rows rest on McCance and Widdowson CoFID 2021 codes and not one CoFID code or value in the submission could be independently confirmed, because the dataset was not retrievable. Where USDA could be checked against CoFID the two diverged badly in this group: egg yolk vitamin D was overstated 2.4x and herring 3x. The maitake, eel and swordfish figures are indicative only, and the NDNS population intake figures could not be traced to the SACN report.

items.supplement: Vitamin E at or above 400 IU/d
items.food_status_note: Alpha-tocopherol is abundant in ordinary foods: seed and nut oils, sunflower seeds, almonds, hazelnuts, paprika and wheatgerm all supply meaningful amounts, and a normal diet covers the 15 mg/day RDA without effort. This is the clearest case in the group where the two questions come apart, because the nutrient is genuinely rich in food while the dose that defines this item is not obtainable from any diet. The original single RICH label sat directly above the entry's own sentence saying the dose 'cannot be reached by eating', which is why the two answers are now separated.
items.dose_from_food_note: 400 IU of natural vitamin E is 268 mg of RRR-alpha-tocopherol. Reaching that every day from food means about 762 g of sunflower seeds (roughly 4,450 kcal), or 1.05 kg of almonds, or 179 g of wheatgerm oil (about 13 tablespoons of neat oil), or 550 g of sunflower oil at the CoFID value and 654 g at USDA's lower one. If the capsule is synthetic all-rac (180 mg for 400 IU), it is still 512 g of sunflower seeds or about 8.9 tablespoons of wheatgerm oil daily. Habitual intakes cluster around 5 to 20 mg/day, so 400 IU sits one to two orders of magnitude above anything eating produces. No dietary pattern gets there.

items.form_caveat: Most 400 IU capsules contain all-rac-alpha-tocopheryl acetate, a synthetic mixture of eight stereoisomers of which only one eighth is the RRR form that human alpha-tocopherol transfer protein preferentially retains. Food contains only RRR, which is exactly why the label conversions differ (1 IU = 0.67 mg natural against 0.45 mg synthetic). Food also never delivers alpha-tocopherol in isolation: sunflower oil carries 48.7 mg alpha with 5.1 mg gamma per 100 g, rapeseed oil carries 18.4 mg alpha with 38.0 mg gamma (CoFID 17-045 and 17-041, both unconfirmed), red palm oil is tocotrienol-rich, and nuts add tocotrienols too. High-dose alpha-tocopherol actively removes part of what food supplies: 400 IU/day of RRR-alpha-tocopheryl acetate cut serum gamma-tocopherol by a median 58% (95% CI 51 to 66%) and reduced detectable delta-tocopherol in a two-month randomised placebo-controlled trial of 184 adult nonsmokers (Huang HY and Appel LJ, J Nutr 2003;133:3137-40, PMID 14519797, all elements confirmed). A 400 IU capsule is therefore something other than a concentrated handful of sunflower seeds; it shifts the balance of vitamin E forms in blood in a direction food never does.
items.bioavailability: Alpha-tocopherol needs dietary fat and bile for absorption, which nuts and oils supply intrinsically, so food forms are absorbed efficiently in ordinary meals. Fractional absorption falls as the single dose rises, and hepatic alpha-TTP selectively retains only the 2R stereoisomers, so the 2S half of a synthetic all-rac dose is largely excreted. The useful fraction of a 400 IU synthetic capsule is therefore well below its stated IU, plasma alpha-tocopherol does not scale linearly with dose, and the displacement of gamma- and delta-tocopherol documented by Huang et al. (PMID 14519797) does.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. Six of the food values were checkable against USDA and have been replaced or ranged, so the corrected list is USDA-anchored where it matters most. The dose arithmetic is the strongest part of the item: the 268 mg and 180 mg conversions and every food requirement recompute exactly, and the conclusion is insensitive to residual uncertainty of a few tens of percent. Against that, the sunflower oil figure is unverifiable, several added foods (hazelnut, almond, safflower and cottonseed oils, paprika, peanuts, corn and soybean oils) rest on single indicative figures from the verification report, and the remaining CoFID rows could not be confirmed.

items.supplement: Preformed vitamin A at or above 10,000 IU
items.food_status_note: Liver is far more concentrated in preformed retinol than the supplement: 10,000 IU is 3,000 µg retinol, and every common liver in the UK tables carries 10,500 to 25,200 µg per 100 g. Hard cheese, butter, fortified fat spreads and egg yolk supply an everyday retinol baseline of tens to about a hundred micrograms per portion on top of that. This is the one item in the group where the food beats the pill, which is why liver carries a public-health warning rather than a recommendation.
items.dose_from_food_note: There is no gap to close. About 12 g of fried calf liver supplies the full 3,000 µg (10,000 IU) of a high-dose retinol capsule, and a normal 100 g portion of any liver delivers 3.5 to 8.4 times that dose in one sitting. A 40 g serving of liver pate is functionally a 10,000 IU tablet at 2,920 µg (9,730 IU). A tablespoon of cod liver oil is 2,448 µg (8,160 IU). Anyone eating liver weekly is already taking supraphysiological preformed vitamin A intermittently, and a 10,000 IU supplement on top compounds a load the body stores rather than clears. For scale, the US tolerable upper intake level for preformed vitamin A is 3,000 µg/day, which is the supplement dose itself, against a UK RNI of 700 µg for men and 600 µg for women.

items.form_caveat: The retinol in liver is the same molecule as the retinyl palmitate or acetate in capsules, absorbed by the same route and stored in the liver the same way, so the usual reassurance that food forms are safer does not apply here. Pregnancy is the sharp edge: UK advice is that people who are pregnant or who might become pregnant should avoid liver and liver products including pate, and should avoid supplements containing vitamin A including fish liver oils, because excess retinol is teratogenic (NHS pregnancy vitamins guidance). Cod liver oil is the common trap, bought for omega-3 or vitamin D and delivering 60,000 IU of retinol per 100 g, and the same trap has sharper versions that are eaten as ordinary food rather than dosed: canned cod liver (Icelandic and Polish tinned), which carries retinol in the cod-liver-oil range, and halibut liver oil, which is more concentrated again and sold in the same aisle. Liver is also eaten unnoticed as liver sausage, liverwurst, haggis, foie gras, and goose and duck liver, all in the same range as the livers tabulated. Outside pregnancy, chronic preformed retinol above the 3,000 µg/day UL is associated with reduced bone mineral density and fracture risk, which is why UK advice is to eat liver no more than once a week. Beta-carotene-rich foods are the safe substitute precisely because their conversion is regulated.
items.bioavailability: Retinyl esters from liver and from supplements are absorbed at high efficiency and, critically, absorption is not down-regulated when stores are full, so intake accumulates in hepatic stellate cells over weeks and months. Carotenoid absorption works the opposite way, feedback-limited through retinoic-acid induction of the intestinal transcription factor ISX and consequent repression of SR-B1 and BCO1 (reviewed in Reboul E, Nutrients 2019;11(4):838, PMID 31013870, DOI 10.3390/nu11040838; the feedback loop itself originates with Lobo et al. and Widjaja-Adhi et al.). Cooking concentrates liver retinol rather than destroying it, through water loss: CoFID shows raw lamb liver at 17,300 µg/100 g rising to 19,700 fried, and raw ox liver at 14,200 rising to 17,300 stewed (codes 18-413, 18-494, 18-415, 18-416, all unconfirmed along with the rest of the CoFID series).
items.data_confidence: LOW. The item's central claim is robust, since the conclusion that food exceeds the supplement dose survives any plausible revision of the numbers, and every IU conversion and dose equivalence recomputes exactly. But the entire liver series, which carries the whole argument, rests on McCance and Widdowson CoFID 2021 codes that could not be retrieved or confirmed, and the two values in this item that were checkable against USDA both came back overstated (butter retinol by 43%, egg yolk by 17%), so the precision quoted for the liver figures is not yet earned. The added cheddar and fortified spread figures are indicative only.

items.food_status_note: Carrots, carrot juice, sweet potato, squash and dark leafy greens are dense, ordinary sources: baked sweet potato flesh carries 11,509 µg beta-carotene per 100 g, carrot juice about 9,300 and raw carrot 8,285. Red palm oil is denser again at roughly 20,000 to 40,000 µg total carotenes per 100 g. By mass the 20 to 30 mg doses used in the intervention trials sit within reach of a few large portions, which makes this the one case where food and supplement look superficially comparable and behave completely differently.
items.dose_from_food_note: By label mass the trial doses are reachable: 20 mg/day is about 241 g of raw carrot (four medium carrots), 174 g of baked sweet potato, or 215 g of carrot juice, and 30 mg/day is about 362 g of raw carrot. Carrot juice is the case that really tests this, because it is the one form anyone actually consumes in the volume required. By absorbed dose the answer flips. The Dietary Reference Intake conversion factors treat 12 µg of food beta-carotene as equivalent to 1 µg retinol activity against 2 µg for supplemental beta-carotene in oil, implying the supplement form is about six times more available (Institute of Medicine, DRIs for Vitamin A and related micronutrients, 2001, DOI 10.17226/10026). Matching the absorbed exposure of a 20 mg capsule therefore takes on the order of 120 mg of food beta-carotene, roughly 1.45 kg of raw carrots daily, which nobody eats and the gut would not absorb anyway. Food matches the label number and does not match the plasma exposure that produced the trial results.

items.form_caveat: This is the clearest food-versus-extract case in the set. Supplement beta-carotene is synthetic all-trans-beta-carotene or algal/fungal beta-carotene, formulated in oil or water-dispersible beadlets specifically to defeat the poor bioavailability of the food form, so it is engineered to do what a carrot cannot. Food never delivers beta-carotene alone: the same carrot supplies 3,477 µg/100 g of alpha-carotene, red palm oil is roughly a third alpha-carotene, and dark greens supply lutein with less beta-carotene. Dietary carotenoids carry none of the supplement harm for three reasons. First, uptake and cleavage are feedback-regulated, since absorbed beta-carotene raises intracellular retinoic acid, which induces ISX, which represses SR-B1 and BCO1 in the enterocyte, so absorption falls as vitamin A status rises (Reboul E, Nutrients 2019;11(4):838, PMID 31013870; the ISX loop itself traces to Lobo et al. and Widjaja-Adhi et al.). A capsule of purified beta-carotene in oil pushes plasma concentrations well past anything food produces, and the IOM 2:1 factor strictly applies to purified beta-carotene in oil, so applying it to beadlet formulations is an approximation. Second, the harm signals came from isolated high doses in high-risk groups: 20 mg/day raised lung cancer incidence by 18% in male smokers (ATBC, N Engl J Med 1994;330:1029-35, PMID 8127329) and 30 mg/day plus 25,000 IU retinyl palmitate produced about 28% more lung cancers, weighted incidence RR 1.36 (95% CI 1.07 to 1.73, P = .01) with mortality RR 1.59, in smokers and asbestos-exposed workers (CARET, Omenn et al., J Natl Cancer Inst 1996;88:1550-9, PMID 8901853). CARET cannot be attributed to beta-carotene alone, since it co-administered a large preformed retinol dose. Third, overloading on carrots produces carotenodermia, a harmless orange discolouration, rather than hypervitaminosis A, because the conversion step is regulated. Eating carrots and taking 20 mg of beta-carotene are two different interventions. Several everyday sources are absent from the table only because no figure was available to tabulate: dried parsley, basil and coriander, paprika, fresh apricots, persimmon, papaya, sweet red pepper, spring greens and collards, watercress, Swiss chard and romaine lettuce, all of which outrank the baby spinach originally chosen as the green exemplar.
items.bioavailability: Beta-carotene in raw carrot and raw spinach is locked in chromoplasts behind intact plant cell walls, so absorption from raw vegetables is low; chopping, pureeing, juicing, cooking and eating with fat all raise it, and cooking does not destroy it. The formal expression of this is the 12:1 food against 2:1 supplement-in-oil conversion factor (IOM 2001, DOI 10.17226/10026). One retention argument from the original entry has to be withdrawn: boiled carrot at 9,616 µg/100 g against raw carrot at 8,285 now compares a CoFID value with a USDA one, so it cannot be read as a within-dataset cooking effect. Conversion efficiency varies substantially between individuals through BCO1 genotype and vitamin A status, which is why plasma responses to the same carrot intake differ several-fold between people (PMID 31013870, a review stretched somewhat to cover the genotype point). Spinach needs its own correction: it is not the weak green the submission made it, since USDA raw spinach at 5,626 µg/100 g is about two thirds of raw carrot rather than under a fifth, and the honest caution about it is the oxalate load for people managing kidney stones.

items.food_status_note: The two menaquinones need separate answers, because one merged label buries the whole point. MK-7 is genuinely rich in food, at 939 µg/100 g in natto, and that richness rests on exactly one food that most of the target population never eats; every other measured MK-7 source is trace, with cheddar at 2.7 and butter at 4.2 µg/100 g. MK-4 is trace in food across the board, at roughly 1 to 22 µg/100 g in chicken, egg yolk, full-fat dairy and meat, with goose liver paste as the one outlier at about 369 µg/100 g, while the 45 mg clinical dose is synthetic-only, since MK-4 supplements are manufactured from menadione because no food is or could be concentrated to 45 mg per dose.
items.dose_from_food_note: MK-7 and MK-4 give opposite answers. MK-7 at supplement and trial doses of 90 to 180 µg/day is fully covered by food: one 50 g pack of natto carries 470 µg, so a pack every second or third day matches a 180 µg capsule. Nothing else comes close, since 180 µg/day from cheddar at 2.7 µg MK-7 per 100 g would take 6.7 kg of cheese daily and from butter about 4.3 kg. MK-4 is the reverse. The Japanese clinical dose, menatetrenone for osteoporosis, is 45 mg/day (45,000 µg), usually 15 mg three times daily. At the richest food value in the composition literature, goose liver paste at about 369 µg/100 g, that is 12.2 kg per day, and at barbecue chicken's 22.1 µg/100 g it is about 204 kg. Even a modest 1.5 mg consumer MK-4 pill needs 407 g of goose liver paste, 6.8 kg of chicken, or 150 kg of whole milk. Measured whole-diet MK-4 intake sits around 17 µg/day (7.3% of a mean total vitamin K intake of about 230 µg/day in Japanese women, Kamao 2007), roughly one 2,600th of the pharmacological dose. MK-4 at supplement strength is unreachable by eating.

items.form_caveat: MK-7 supplements are made by Bacillus subtilis natto fermentation, the same organism that makes natto, or synthesised; the active species is all-trans MK-7, and cis-isomer contamination is a documented quality problem in commercial products that the fermented food does not have. MK-4 supplements are wholly synthetic, derived from menadione, because no food is or could be concentrated to 45 mg per dose. That said, one framing in the original entry was wrong and has to go: goose liver paste at about 369 µg/100 g puts 100 g of food within roughly 2.1 orders of magnitude of the 45 mg dose (1/122 of it), so the claim that no food comes within three orders of magnitude fails, even though the dose stays unreachable at 12.2 kg/day. Natto also brings the fermentation matrix, fibre and nattokinase, and circulating K2 after eating natto is around ten times circulating K1 after eating spinach, a comparison made with 200 g of natto against 400 g of spinach rather than gram for gram (Schurgers LJ, Vermeer C, Haemostasis 2000;30:298-307, PMID 11356998). The 'cheese is a K2 food' claim needs unpicking: cheese total vitamin K is genuinely high, at 282 ± 5.0 µg/100 g for hard cheese, 289 ± 38 for semi-soft, 440 ± 41 for blue and 506 ± 63 for soft, but roughly 90% of it is MK-9, MK-10 and MK-11 from starter bacteria (Fu et al. 2017, PMID 29955705), forms no clinical trial has tested, while the MK-7 fraction is a few µg/100 g. Cheddar is the weak exemplar for that argument, and the long-ripened Dutch and Norwegian cheeses (Gouda, Edam, Jarlsberg) are the canonical MK-9-rich ones that would test it properly; curd cheese and quark appear as K2 sources in the Schurgers and Vermeer paper itself, and tempeh, fermented soy pastes, Korean cheonggukjang, sauerkraut and fermented salami would show whether natto is uniquely high or simply the best measured. None of those could be tabulated for want of a figure. Animal MK-4 also tracks the animal's feed, since menadione is a routine poultry feed additive and Elder et al. attribute poultry MK-4 to alkylation of it, so brand, country and production system shift the numbers, and the chicken hot dog and chicken broth samples in the same study contained no detectable MK-4 at all.
items.bioavailability: MK-4 and MK-7 behave so differently that microgram-for-microgram comparison is meaningless. A single 420 µg dose of MK-7 was well absorbed, peaked at 6 hours and remained detectable in serum for 48 hours, while the identical 420 µg dose of MK-4 was undetectable in the serum of all subjects at every time point, and seven consecutive days at 60 µg/day raised only MK-7 (Sato T et al., Nutr J 2012;11:93, PMID 23140417, DOI 10.1186/1475-2891-11-93, every element confirmed). MK-7's long half-life comes from its extended isoprenoid side chain and tight lipoprotein binding. That is the mechanistic reason MK-4 is dosed in milligrams while MK-7 works in micrograms, and it means the 1 to 22 µg/100 g of MK-4 in butter, egg yolk, cheese and chicken contributes almost nothing to circulating vitamin K2 even though it is real and measurable. All menaquinones need dietary fat for absorption, which is why they sit in and are absorbed from the fat phase of dairy and eggs, and the reduced-fat versions lose most of it, with reduced-fat cheddar at 1.8 µg MK-4 per 100 g against 9.5 µg for full fat (PMID 29955705, whose fat-dependence finding was confirmed).
items.data_confidence: LOW. The literature layer is strong and fully verified: Kamao 2007 (natto 939 µg/100 g, 230 µg/day total K, MK-4 at 7.3%), Fu 2017 (cheese totals and fat dependence), Sato 2012 (420 µg MK-4 undetectable) and Schurgers 2000 all confirmed exactly against PubMed, so the MK-7 side of the item rests on a confirmed number. The food-composition layer does not. Six MK-4 food values come from Elder et al. Table 1 and 2, which is a confirmed citation with paywalled tables that could not be opened, the butter and cheddar MK-7 values come from a paper whose DOI does not resolve and whose calibration the submission itself questions at about 27x the US values, and the goose liver paste figure that now anchors the MK-4 dose gap is a widely cited table value that could not be confirmed from its source.

items.food_status_note_zh: 多脂鱼、蛋黄和经紫外线处理的菇类都能提供可测量的维生素 D，强化脂肪涂抹酱、牛奶、早餐谷物和果汁再补上少量，所以这是一种真正来自膳食的营养素，并非只能靠工业制造。RICH 这个标签需要在两点上加以限定：食物基础很窄（多脂鱼、蛋黄、经紫外线处理的菇类），而且下表中较强的两行并不是普通食物，鱼肝油的行为更接近补充剂，强化橙汁则是工业化的输送载体。人群证据指向同一方向：SACN 认为 10 µg/天 的 RNI 很难仅从天然食物来源达到，并把它定为 4 岁及以上所有人群的全年 RNI；英国来自食物的平均摄入量约为该值的三分之一（常被引用的 NDNS 数字，19 至 65 岁 2.8 µg/天、65 岁以上 3.3 µg/天，此处标为未获证实，因为无法取得完整的 SACN 报告加以确认）。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 1,000 IU（25 µg）属于普通补充剂剂量的低端，相当于每天吃约 150 g 熟红鲑，或 155 g 至 463 g 烤鲱鱼（取决于采用哪个鲱鱼数值）。4,000 IU（100 µg）大致等于每天 600 g 红鲑、621 g 至 1.85 kg 鲱鱼、约 109 个大蛋黄，或约 890 g 经紫外线处理的褐菇。每周 50,000 IU（1,250 µg）的负荷剂量在食物里没有对应物：7.5 kg 红鲑，或 7.8 至 23.1 kg 烤鲱鱼。只有一种食物单看质量能接近，即处于实测范围上限的紫外线处理灰树花，178 g 就能提供 4,000 IU，但这一含量不会标注在包装上，随栽培方式在 0.1 至 56.1 µg/100 g 之间波动，而且它是 D2，不是 D3。在北纬约 50 度以上，10 月至次年 3 月皮肤合成实际为零，冬季缺口没有阳光可以填补。
items.form_caveat_zh: 菇类的维生素 D 是 D2（麦角钙化醇），与鱼类、蛋黄以及几乎所有补充剂中的 D3 是不同的分子，D3 提升血清 25(OH)D 的效率更高，间歇性大剂量给药时差距最大（Tripkovic 等，Am J Clin Nutr 2012;95:1357-64，PMID 22552031，DOI 10.3945/ajcn.111.031070，大剂量给药的平均差值为 34.10 nmol/L，P = 0.0002；每日给药时这一优势消失，P = 0.10）。紫外线处理菇类的含量波动极大，通常也不标注：USDA 测得一家生产商的紫外线处理褐菇为 3.4 µg/100 g，另一家为 25.6 µg/100 g，灰树花随栽培方式在 0.1 至 56.1 µg/100 g 之间，未处理的白蘑菇为 0.1 至 0.2 µg/100 g，所以只因为“菇类含维生素 D”就买普通蘑菇，基本什么都得不到。物种和产地与食物名称同样重要：表中的鲑鱼是野生红鲑，而大多数消费者买到的养殖大西洋鲑要低数倍，包装上写着“鲑鱼”并不能提供红鲑的数值。鱼肝油名义上是食物，行为上更像补充剂，每 100 g 含 18,000 µg 视黄醇（CoFID 17-488，未证实），因此一汤匙除 D3 之外还带来约 8,160 IU 的预制型维生素 A，孕期不宜使用。还有几种英国实际存在的载体因缺少可核实的数据而未列入表中，但不应被忽略：强化人造黄油和脂肪涂抹酱（数十年来英国法定的维生素 D 载体，对英国摄入量的贡献大于表中所列的美国强化橙汁）、强化早餐谷物、烟熏鲱鱼（kippers）及其他熏制鲱鱼、罐装红鲑（高于表中所列的罐装粉红鲑）、鲱鱼籽和鳕鱼籽，以及提供 D2 的晒干香菇。多脂鱼把 D3 放在脂肪基质中一并送来，同时带有 EPA/DHA、蛋白质、碘和硒；胶囊只送来 D3。
items.bioavailability_zh: 食物和胶囊里的维生素 D 都是脂溶性的，随含脂餐一起摄入吸收更好，而多脂鱼和蛋黄本身就自带脂肪。形式比来源更要紧：菇类的 D2 按每微克计算效力低于 D3（PMID 22552031）。蛋黄还额外含有 25-羟基胆钙化醇，这是一种已经羟化的代谢物，补充剂通常不提供。成分表按“总量 = 胆钙化醇 + 5 x 25-OH-D3”的惯例把 25-OH-D3 并入头条总量，所以鸡蛋、鳟鱼或罐装鲑鱼的“维生素 D”数字与胶囊中的 D3 并不严格可比；此处罐装粉红鲑（12.1 + 5 x 0.30 = 13.6）、鳟鱼（7.19 + 5 x 0.20 = 8.19）和全蛋（2.30 + 5 x 0.18 = 3.20）的总量都遵循这一惯例。
items.data_confidence_zh: 低。唯一一个获得证实的最富含食物（熟红鲑）以及紫外线处理褐菇和强化橙汁的数值都能核对通过，但多数行依赖 McCance and Widdowson CoFID 2021 的食物编码，而提交材料中没有任何一个 CoFID 编码或数值能够独立确认，因为该数据集无法取得。本组中凡是能用 USDA 与 CoFID 对照的地方，两者差异都很大：蛋黄维生素 D 被高估 2.4 倍，鲱鱼高估 3 倍。灰树花、鳗鱼和剑鱼的数字仅为指示性，NDNS 的人群摄入量数字也无法追溯到 SACN 报告。

items.supplement: Vitamin E at or above 400 IU/d
items.supplement_zh: 维生素 E，每日 400 IU 及以上
items.food_status_note_zh: α-生育酚在普通食物里很充足：籽油和坚果油、葵花籽、杏仁、榛子、红椒粉和小麦胚芽都能提供可观的量，普通饮食毫不费力就能覆盖 15 mg/天 的 RDA。本组中这一条最清楚地显示出两个问题会分开作答：这种营养素在食物中确实丰富，而定义本条目的那个剂量任何饮食都无法达到。原先单一的 RICH 标签，正好压在该条目自己那句“靠吃达不到”的话上面，因此现在把两个答案分开。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 400 IU 天然维生素 E 等于 268 mg RRR-α-生育酚。每天从食物达到这个量，意味着约 762 g 葵花籽（约 4,450 kcal），或 1.05 kg 杏仁，或 179 g 小麦胚芽油（约 13 汤匙纯油），或按 CoFID 数值 550 g 葵花籽油、按 USDA 较低数值 654 g。如果胶囊是合成的 all-rac 形式（400 IU 对应 180 mg），每天仍需 512 g 葵花籽，或约 8.9 汤匙小麦胚芽油。习惯摄入量集中在 5 至 20 mg/天，400 IU 比吃出来的任何量高出一到两个数量级。没有任何饮食模式能达到。
items.form_caveat_zh: 多数 400 IU 胶囊装的是 all-rac-α-生育酚乙酸酯，这是八种立体异构体的合成混合物，其中只有八分之一是人体 α-生育酚转运蛋白优先保留的 RRR 型。食物中只有 RRR 型，标签换算因此不同（天然型 1 IU = 0.67 mg，合成型 1 IU = 0.45 mg）。食物也从不单独提供 α-生育酚：葵花籽油每 100 g 含 48.7 mg α 和 5.1 mg γ，菜籽油含 18.4 mg α 和 38.0 mg γ（CoFID 17-045 和 17-041，均未证实），红棕油富含生育三烯酚，坚果也会带来生育三烯酚。大剂量 α-生育酚会主动清掉食物提供的一部分东西：在一项为期两个月、纳入 184 名成年非吸烟者的随机安慰剂对照试验中，每天 400 IU 的 RRR-α-生育酚乙酸酯使血清 γ-生育酚中位数下降 58%（95% CI 51 至 66%），并减少可检出的 δ-生育酚（Huang HY 与 Appel LJ，J Nutr 2003;133:3137-40，PMID 14519797，各项要素均已确认）。因此一粒 400 IU 胶囊与一把浓缩的葵花籽是两回事，它把血液中各种维生素 E 形式的比例推向食物从不会推的方向。
items.bioavailability_zh: α-生育酚的吸收需要膳食脂肪和胆汁，坚果和油脂本身就自带这些，所以在普通餐食中食物形式吸收效率不错。单次剂量越大，吸收分数越低；肝脏的 α-TTP 只选择性保留 2R 立体异构体，因此合成 all-rac 剂量中占一半的 2S 部分大体被排出。这就使 400 IU 合成胶囊真正有用的比例远低于其标称 IU，血浆 α-生育酚不随剂量线性上升，而 Huang 等（PMID 14519797）记录的 γ-生育酚和 δ-生育酚被置换的现象确实随剂量上升。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。六个食物数值可以与 USDA 对照，已经替换或改为范围，所以在最要紧的地方，修正后的清单以 USDA 为锚。剂量算术是本条目最扎实的部分：268 mg 和 180 mg 的换算以及每一项食物需求量都能精确重算，几十个百分点的残余不确定性也不影响结论。另一方面，葵花籽油的数值无法核实，几种新增食物（榛子油、杏仁油、红花籽油和棉籽油、红椒粉、花生、玉米油和大豆油）依赖核查报告中的单一指示性数字，其余 CoFID 行也无法确认。

items.supplement: Preformed vitamin A at or above 10,000 IU
items.supplement_zh: 预制型维生素 A，10,000 IU 及以上
items.food_status_note_zh: 肝脏中预制型视黄醇的浓度远高于补充剂：10,000 IU 相当于 3,000 µg 视黄醇，而英国食物成分表里常见的每一种肝脏，每 100 g 都含 10,500 至 25,200 µg。在此之上，硬质奶酪、黄油、强化脂肪涂抹酱和蛋黄还提供每份数十到约一百微克的日常视黄醇基线。本组中只有这一条是食物胜过药片，所以官方对肝脏发出的是公共卫生警告，谈不上推荐。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 这里没有需要填补的缺口。约 12 g 油炸小牛肝就能提供高剂量视黄醇胶囊的全部 3,000 µg（10,000 IU），而任何一种肝脏的常规 100 g 份量，一餐就能送来该剂量的 3.5 至 8.4 倍。40 g 肝酱含 2,920 µg（9,730 IU），功能上等同一片 10,000 IU 的药片。一汤匙鱼肝油是 2,448 µg（8,160 IU）。每周吃肝的人已经在间歇性摄入超生理量的预制型维生素 A，再叠加 10,000 IU 补充剂，只会加重身体倾向储存而非清除的负荷。作为参照，美国预制型维生素 A 的可耐受最高摄入量是 3,000 µg/天，恰好就是这个补充剂剂量本身，而英国 RNI 为男性 700 µg、女性 600 µg。
items.form_caveat_zh: 肝脏里的视黄醇与胶囊里的视黄醇棕榈酸酯或乙酸酯是同一个分子，走同一条吸收途径，在肝脏中以同样方式储存，所以“食物形式更安全”这句常见的安慰话在这里不成立。孕期是最锋利的一处：英国的建议是，怀孕或可能怀孕的人应避免肝脏及包括肝酱在内的肝制品，并避免含维生素 A 的补充剂，包括鱼肝油，因为过量视黄醇有致畸性（NHS 孕期维生素指南）。鱼肝油是常见的陷阱，人们为了 omega-3 或维生素 D 买它，而它每 100 g 提供 60,000 IU 视黄醇；同一个陷阱还有更锋利的版本，那些是当作普通食物吃下去的，不是按剂量服用的：罐装鳕鱼肝（冰岛和波兰的罐头），其视黄醇含量与鱼肝油同一量级；还有大比目鱼肝油，浓度更高，就摆在同一排货架上。肝脏也常在不被注意的情况下被吃下：肝肠、德式肝肠（liverwurst）、苏格兰羊杂布丁（haggis）、鹅肝酱（foie gras），以及鹅肝和鸭肝，含量都与表中所列的肝脏处于同一区间。在孕期之外，长期摄入超过 3,000 µg/天 UL 的预制型视黄醇与骨密度下降和骨折风险相关，这也是英国建议每周吃肝不超过一次的原因。富含 β-胡萝卜素的食物是安全的替代，原因正在于其转化受到调节。
items.bioavailability_zh: 来自肝脏和来自补充剂的视黄酯吸收效率都很高，而且关键在于，储备充足时吸收并不会下调，因此摄入量会在数周到数月间累积于肝星状细胞。类胡萝卜素的吸收方向相反，受反馈限制：视黄酸诱导肠道转录因子 ISX，进而抑制 SR-B1 和 BCO1（综述见 Reboul E，Nutrients 2019;11(4):838，PMID 31013870，DOI 10.3390/nu11040838；该反馈环路本身出自 Lobo 等和 Widjaja-Adhi 等）。烹饪通过失水提高肝脏视黄醇的浓度，并不会破坏它：CoFID 显示生羊肝为 17,300 µg/100 g，油炸后升至 19,700；生牛肝 14,200，炖后升至 17,300（编码 18-413、18-494、18-415、18-416，与 CoFID 系列其余部分一样均未证实）。
items.data_confidence_zh: 低。本条目的核心论断很稳固，食物超过补充剂剂量这一结论在任何合理的数字修订下都成立，而且每一项 IU 换算和剂量等效都能精确重算。但承载全部论证的整个肝脏系列依赖 McCance and Widdowson CoFID 2021 的编码，这些编码既无法取得也无法确认；本条目中两个能与 USDA 对照的数值都被高估（黄油视黄醇高估 43%，蛋黄高估 17%），所以肝脏数字所给出的精度还不配得上。新增的切达奶酪和强化涂抹酱数字仅为指示性。

items.food_status_note_zh: 胡萝卜、胡萝卜汁、红薯、南瓜类和深色叶菜都是含量高的普通来源：烤红薯果肉每 100 g 含 11,509 µg β-胡萝卜素，胡萝卜汁约 9,300，生胡萝卜 8,285。红棕油浓度更高，每 100 g 总类胡萝卜素约 20,000 至 40,000 µg。按质量算，干预试验所用的 20 至 30 mg 剂量，几大份食物就够得着，这使本条成为食物与补充剂表面看来可比、实际行为完全不同的唯一一例。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 按标签质量算，试验剂量是够得着的：20 mg/天 约等于 241 g 生胡萝卜（四根中等大小），或 174 g 烤红薯，或 215 g 胡萝卜汁；30 mg/天 约为 362 g 生胡萝卜。真正检验这一点的是胡萝卜汁，因为它是唯一一种人们确实会按所需体积喝下去的形式。按吸收剂量算，答案就翻转了。膳食参考摄入量的换算系数把 12 µg 食物来源 β-胡萝卜素算作 1 µg 视黄醇活性当量，油溶补充剂形式的 β-胡萝卜素则是 2 µg，意味着补充剂形式的可利用度约高六倍（Institute of Medicine，DRIs for Vitamin A and related micronutrients，2001，DOI 10.17226/10026）。因此要在吸收暴露上匹配一粒 20 mg 胶囊，需要约 120 mg 食物来源 β-胡萝卜素，大致相当于每天 1.45 kg 生胡萝卜，没有人这么吃，肠道也吸收不了。食物能对上标签上的数字，对不上产生试验结果的那个血浆暴露水平。
items.form_caveat_zh: 这是全组中食物与提取物对比最清楚的一例。补充剂里的 β-胡萝卜素是合成的全反式 β-胡萝卜素，或藻类、真菌来源的 β-胡萝卜素，配制成油溶剂型或水分散微丸，目的正是绕过食物形式吸收差的问题，它被设计出来做胡萝卜做不到的事。食物从不单独提供 β-胡萝卜素：同一根胡萝卜还提供 3,477 µg/100 g 的 α-胡萝卜素，红棕油约三分之一是 α-胡萝卜素，深色叶菜提供叶黄素而 β-胡萝卜素较少。膳食类胡萝卜素不带补充剂的那些危害，有三个原因。第一，摄取和裂解受反馈调节：吸收的 β-胡萝卜素提高细胞内视黄酸，视黄酸诱导 ISX，ISX 抑制肠上皮细胞中的 SR-B1 和 BCO1，因此维生素 A 状态升高时吸收下降（Reboul E，Nutrients 2019;11(4):838，PMID 31013870；ISX 环路本身可追溯到 Lobo 等和 Widjaja-Adhi 等）。一粒油溶纯化 β-胡萝卜素胶囊把血浆浓度推到食物远达不到的水平，而 IOM 的 2:1 系数严格来说只适用于油溶纯化 β-胡萝卜素，用在微丸剂型上只是近似。第二，危害信号来自高危人群中的孤立大剂量：每天 20 mg 使男性吸烟者的肺癌发病率上升 18%（ATBC，N Engl J Med 1994;330:1029-35，PMID 8127329）；每天 30 mg 加 25,000 IU 视黄醇棕榈酸酯，在吸烟者和石棉暴露工人中多出约 28% 的肺癌，加权发病率 RR 1.36（95% CI 1.07 至 1.73，P = .01），死亡率 RR 1.59（CARET，Omenn 等，J Natl Cancer Inst 1996;88:1550-9，PMID 8901853）。CARET 的结果不能只归因于 β-胡萝卜素，因为试验同时给了大剂量预制型视黄醇。第三，胡萝卜吃过量产生的是胡萝卜素性皮肤黄染，一种无害的橙色变色，不会造成维生素 A 中毒，因为转化步骤受调节。吃胡萝卜和服用 20 mg β-胡萝卜素是两种不同的干预。还有几种日常来源没有列入表中，仅因为找不到可以填表的数据：干欧芹、干罗勒和干香菜、红椒粉、新鲜杏、柿子、番木瓜、甜红椒、春季甘蓝（spring greens）和宽叶羽衣甘蓝（collards）、西洋菜、瑞士甜菜和罗马生菜，它们都排在最初被选作叶菜代表的嫩菠菜之前。
items.bioavailability_zh: 生胡萝卜和生菠菜中的 β-胡萝卜素被锁在完整植物细胞壁之后的有色体里，所以生蔬菜的吸收率低；切碎、打泥、榨汁、加热以及与脂肪同食都会提高吸收，加热也不会破坏它。这一点的正式表达就是食物 12:1 与油溶补充剂 2:1 的换算系数（IOM 2001，DOI 10.17226/10026）。原条目里有一条关于保留率的论证必须撤回：水煮胡萝卜 9,616 µg/100 g 对生胡萝卜 8,285，如今是拿 CoFID 数值与 USDA 数值相比，因此不能当作同一数据集内的烹饪效应来读。转化效率在个体之间差别很大，取决于 BCO1 基因型和维生素 A 状态，这也是同样的胡萝卜摄入量在不同人身上血浆反应相差数倍的原因（PMID 31013870，该综述用来支撑基因型这一点略有拉伸）。菠菜需要单独更正：提交材料把它写成弱势叶菜，USDA 生菠菜 5,626 µg/100 g 约为生胡萝卜的三分之二，远高于不足五分之一的说法；对它诚实的提醒是草酸负荷，关系到需要控制肾结石的人。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。承重的数值现在以 USDA 为锚：五个食物数字可核对并已替换（生胡萝卜、烤红薯、生菠菜和熟菠菜、杏干、黄油 β-胡萝卜素），两个通过检验的数值（羽衣甘蓝、芒果）与 USDA 相差在 9% 以内。剂量算术和 IOM 换算系数均已确认。压低置信度的是：仍有四行是未证实的 CoFID 编码，其中两行与同一蔬菜的 USDA 数值对不上（水煮红薯约为 USDA 烤制值的一半），羽衣甘蓝已发表数值的范围异常宽，四种新增食物依赖单一指示性数字。

items.supplement_zh: 维生素 K2（MK-7 和 MK-4）
items.food_status_note_zh: 两种甲基萘醌需要分开作答，合成一个标签会把要点全部埋掉。MK-7 在食物中确实丰富，纳豆达 939 µg/100 g，但这份丰富只落在唯一一种食物上，而目标人群多数人从不吃它；其他所有实测的 MK-7 来源都只是痕量，切达奶酪 2.7 µg/100 g，黄油 4.2 µg/100 g。MK-4 在各类食物中普遍只是痕量，鸡肉、蛋黄、全脂乳制品和肉类大致为 1 至 22 µg/100 g，唯一的异常值是鹅肝酱约 369 µg/100 g；而 45 mg 的临床剂量只能来自合成，MK-4 补充剂由甲萘醌制造，因为没有任何食物浓缩到、也不可能浓缩到每剂 45 mg。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: MK-7 和 MK-4 给出相反的答案。MK-7 在 90 至 180 µg/天 的补充剂和试验剂量上完全能由食物覆盖：一盒 50 g 纳豆含 470 µg，每两三天吃一盒就相当于一粒 180 µg 胶囊。别的食物都远远不及，按切达奶酪 2.7 µg MK-7/100 g 计算，每天 180 µg 需要 6.7 kg 奶酪，用黄油则约 4.3 kg。MK-4 的情况相反。日本用于骨质疏松的临床剂量，四烯甲萘醌，为 45 mg/天（45,000 µg），通常一日三次、每次 15 mg。按成分文献中最高的食物数值，鹅肝酱约 369 µg/100 g，这相当于每天 12.2 kg；按烧烤鸡肉 22.1 µg/100 g 计算约为 204 kg。哪怕是一粒普通消费级 1.5 mg 的 MK-4 药片，也需要 407 g 鹅肝酱、6.8 kg 鸡肉，或 150 kg 全脂牛奶。实测整膳食 MK-4 摄入量约为 17 µg/天（日本女性维生素 K 总摄入量约 230 µg/天，MK-4 占 7.3%，Kamao 2007），大约是药理剂量的 1/2,600。补充剂强度的 MK-4 靠吃达不到。
items.form_caveat_zh: MK-7 补充剂由纳豆枯草杆菌（Bacillus subtilis natto）发酵制得，与做纳豆的是同一种菌，也有化学合成的；活性种类是全反式 MK-7，顺式异构体污染是商业产品中有记录的质量问题，发酵食物没有这个问题。MK-4 补充剂完全是合成的，来自甲萘醌，因为没有任何食物浓缩到、也不可能浓缩到每剂 45 mg。不过原条目里有一个说法是错的，必须去掉：鹅肝酱约 369 µg/100 g，使 100 g 食物与 45 mg 剂量之间只差约 2.1 个数量级（为其 1/122），所以“没有食物能进入三个数量级之内”这一断言不成立，尽管 12.2 kg/天 这个剂量依然达不到。纳豆还带来发酵基质、纤维和纳豆激酶，吃纳豆后循环中的 K2 约为吃菠菜后循环中 K1 的十倍，这一比较用的是 200 g 纳豆对 400 g 菠菜，并非等重比较（Schurgers LJ，Vermeer C，Haemostasis 2000;30:298-307，PMID 11356998）。“奶酪是 K2 食物”这个说法需要拆开看：奶酪的维生素 K 总量确实高，硬质奶酪 282 ± 5.0 µg/100 g，半软质 289 ± 38，蓝纹 440 ± 41，软质 506 ± 63，但其中约 90% 是发酵剂细菌产生的 MK-9、MK-10 和 MK-11（Fu 等 2017，PMID 29955705），这些形式没有任何临床试验测试过，而 MK-7 部分只有每 100 g 几 µg。切达奶酪是支撑该论点的弱例子，长期成熟的荷兰和挪威奶酪（高达 Gouda、埃丹 Edam、亚尔斯堡 Jarlsberg）才是典型的富含 MK-9 品种，用它们才能真正检验；凝乳奶酪和夸克（quark）本身就出现在 Schurgers 与 Vermeer 的论文里，被列为 K2 来源；天贝、发酵豆酱、韩国清麴酱（cheonggukjang）、德式酸菜和发酵萨拉米则可以显示纳豆究竟是独一无二地高，还是仅仅测得最充分的一个。这些都因缺少数据而无法列表。动物性 MK-4 还随动物饲料变化，甲萘醌是家禽饲料的常规添加剂，Elder 等把家禽 MK-4 归因于它的烷基化，所以品牌、国家和生产体系都会改变数字；同一研究中的鸡肉热狗和鸡汤样品完全检不出 MK-4。
items.bioavailability_zh: MK-4 和 MK-7 的表现差别之大，按微克对微克比较毫无意义。单次 420 µg 的 MK-7 吸收良好，6 小时达峰，血清中 48 小时仍可检出；同样 420 µg 的 MK-4 在所有受试者的各个时间点血清中都检不出，连续七天每天 60 µg 也只升高 MK-7（Sato T 等，Nutr J 2012;11:93，PMID 23140417，DOI 10.1186/1475-2891-11-93，各项要素均已确认）。MK-7 半衰期长，来自它较长的类异戊二烯侧链和与脂蛋白的紧密结合。这正是 MK-4 以毫克计量而 MK-7 以微克起效的机理原因，也意味着黄油、蛋黄、奶酪和鸡肉中那 1 至 22 µg/100 g 的 MK-4 虽然真实可测，对循环维生素 K2 的贡献几乎为零。所有甲基萘醌的吸收都需要膳食脂肪，因此它们存在于乳制品和鸡蛋的脂肪相中并从那里被吸收，减脂版本会失去其中大部分：减脂切达奶酪每 100 g 含 1.8 µg MK-4，全脂为 9.5 µg（PMID 29955705，其脂肪依赖性发现已确认）。
items.data_confidence_zh: 低。文献层面很扎实且全部经过核验：Kamao 2007（纳豆 939 µg/100 g，维生素 K 总摄入 230 µg/天，MK-4 占 7.3%）、Fu 2017（奶酪总量和脂肪依赖性）、Sato 2012（420 µg MK-4 检不出）和 Schurgers 2000 都与 PubMed 逐项精确核对无误，所以本条目 MK-7 一侧建立在一个已确认的数字上。食物成分层面则不然。六个 MK-4 食物数值出自 Elder 等的表 1 和表 2，引文本身已确认，但表格在付费墙后无法打开；黄油和切达奶酪的 MK-7 数值来自一篇 DOI 无法解析的论文，提交材料自己也质疑其校准，约为美国数值的 27 倍；而现在支撑 MK-4 剂量缺口的鹅肝酱数字，是一个被广泛引用的表格值，无法从其源头确认。

items.food_status_note: Folic acid (pteroylmonoglutamic acid) is manufactured by chemical synthesis, a Waller-type condensation of a triaminopyrimidinone with a three-carbon unit and p-aminobenzoyl-L-glutamic acid, giving a fully oxidised molecule carrying a single glutamate that does not occur in unfortified food. Ordinary food supplies reduced folate polyglutamates instead, chiefly 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, and USDA's component structure keeps 'folic acid' and 'folate, food' as separate entries: beef liver, lentils, spinach, chickpeas, asparagus and boiled broccoli all read folic acid 0 with folate food equal to folate total. Two distinct answers therefore sit inside one word, so they are separated here: the nutrient class folate is rich in ordinary food, while the marketed molecule folic acid enters the food supply only through fortification and enrichment, which is what every food row below is. Enriched pasta and enriched white rice are the other mandated US enrichment vehicles; their contents are label-dependent per product and no verified figure was available, so they get no row.
items.dose_from_food_note: Two routes with different answers. As folic acid, the 400 ug periconceptional dose is reachable in one sitting only from fortified products: one bowl of ready-to-eat cereal fortified to 400 ug folic acid per serving is the entire dose, whereas matching it from yeast extract spread takes about 13 g (a bit over two teaspoons), from instant fortified oatmeal 8.2 packets, and from enriched wheat bread about 69 slices. As natural food folate the equivalent target is 680 ug DFE (400 x 1.7), and this is where the verification pass forced a correction: the submission's cheapest option was 376 g of cooked lentils, but simmered chicken liver at 578 ug food folate per 100 g (FDC 171061) needs only 118 g, under three 44 g livers, which is an ordinary portion, and pan-fried lamb liver at 400 ug DFE per 100 g (FDC 172533) needs 170 g. The plant routes stay awkward: 376 g cooked lentils (1.9 cups), 219 g prepared edamame (1.4 cups), 300 g dried sunflower kernels, 351 g raw spinach (about twelve 30 g cups), 395 g cooked chickpeas, 456 g cooked asparagus (about thirty spears) or 630 g boiled broccoli. So the plain answer is that a person can eat their way to the folate equivalent of the 400 ug dose through liver or through fortified food, and cannot realistically do it through leafy greens; the UK high-risk 5 mg dose (8,500 ug DFE, 1.47 kg of chicken liver or 4.7 kg of cooked lentils every day) is unreachable by any route. Liver carries its own pregnancy restriction on preformed vitamin A grounds, which is why it is rarely offered as the answer to the population that needs the dose.

items.form_caveat: Folic acid is not bioidentical to food folate and the difference cuts both ways. It must be reduced by dihydrofolate reductase before entering one-carbon metabolism, and human DHFR capacity is low: unmetabolised folic acid appears in serum above a threshold of about 266 ug of folic acid per meal (Kelly et al., Am J Clin Nutr 1997;65:1790-5, PMID 9174474), which a 400 ug tablet exceeds. That is why the adult UL of 1,000 ug/day applies to folic acid from supplements and fortified food with no UL on food folate: high folic acid can correct the megaloblastic anaemia of B12 deficiency while neurological damage continues, masking the diagnosis. Food folate has no toxicity ceiling and the synthetic form does. Running the other way, the quantity of food folate is not the only obstacle. Cuskelly, McNulty and Scott randomised 62 women to an extra 400 ug/day as a folic acid supplement, as folic-acid-fortified food, as natural food folate, or as dietary advice: red cell folate rose only in the supplement and fortified-food arms and did not move in the food-folate arms despite documented increases in intake (Lancet 1996;347:657-9, PMID 8596381). The two trials that established the neural-tube-defect effect used synthetic folic acid, 4 mg/day in the MRC Vitamin Study (Lancet 1991;338:131-7, PMID 1677062) and 0.8 mg/day in a multivitamin (Czeizel and Dudas, N Engl J Med 1992;327:1832-5, PMID 1307234). Substituting leafy greens for the tablet before pregnancy has never been tested against that endpoint. On L-5-methyltetrahydrofolate (calcium methylfolate), the marketed 'MTHFR-friendly' alternative: EFSA's 2022 derivation of DFE factors for it judged 5-MTHF more bioavailable than folic acid at supplement doses of 400 ug/day and above (2.0 versus 1.7; PMC9399872), so the case against it is not absorption. It is that no periconceptional trial has been run on it, and the neural-tube-defect evidence base is specifically folic acid (Czeizel, Ann Nutr Metab 2011, PMID 21865678).
items.bioavailability: Food folate is roughly 50% available against about 85% for folic acid eaten with food and close to 100% fasting, which is where the 1.7 and 2.0 DFE multipliers come from (Suitor and Bailey, J Am Diet Assoc 2000;100:88-94, PMID 10646010). Food folate is a polyglutamate that must be deconjugated at the brush border before absorption, and it is chemically fragile. USDA Table of Nutrient Retention Factors Release 6 (2007) gives folate retention of 45% for legumes boiled 45-75 min and drained (code 0521), 30% for legumes boiled 2-2.5 h (code 0541), 60% for greens boiled in water to cover and drained (code 3005) and 90% for potatoes baked in the skin (code 3301). A cup of dried lentils simmered for an hour loses over half its folate, so a composition table value describes the cooked food only when the cooking matches. Folic acid in a fortified food or a tablet is stable and its dose is what the label says.
items.data_confidence: HIGH. Every per-100 g composition value, gram weight and per-portion figure in the food rows and the dose comparison traces to a named USDA FoodData Central record and recomputes exactly, and all six cited PMIDs resolve to the stated journal, volume and pages. Two qualifications: the fortified-cereal row is an indicative label figure rather than a sourced composition record, and one uncited bioavailability claim was removed rather than kept.

items.food_status_note: Rich in animal foods and effectively absent from plant foods, because cobalamin is synthesised only by bacteria and archaea: every reliable source is an animal that accumulated bacterial B12, or a bacterially fermented or fortified product. The single word RICH is population-dependent and hides a reversal, so state it plainly: for an omnivore B12 is one of the easiest nutrients in the food supply, while for someone on an unfortified plant-based diet the same evidence makes it effectively absent, the only credible source being dried purple laver at 2.33 ug per 3 g sheet from a product whose content varies about elevenfold by origin and degrades with toasting and storage. On the contested plant candidates: spirulina is not usable, since 83% of its cobamide is pseudovitamin B12 (adeninylcobamide), inactive in humans, with only 17% real B12, and microbiological assays cannot tell them apart, which is why the labels claim high B12 (Watanabe et al., J Agric Food Chem 1999;47:4736-41, PMID 10552882); nori is usable and is the only credible plant source, carrying five biologically active cobalamin forms with adenosyl- and methylcobalamin about 60% of the total, and it corrected B12 status in deficient rats (Takenaka S et al., Br J Nutr 2001;85:699-703, PMID 11430774); tempeh is unreliable at 0.7-8.0 ug/100 g depending on which bacteria happened to contaminate the Rhizopus fermentation; mushrooms are not usable, with dried shiitake averaging 5.61 ug/100 g dry weight (range 1.3-12.7), black trumpet and golden chanterelle 1.09-2.65 ug/100 g dry weight and most other species about 0.09 ug/100 g or trace; chlorella ranges from zero to several hundred ug/100 g between products and cannot be relied on (all from Watanabe et al., Nutrients 2014;6:1861-73, PMID 24803097). Two further claims in the original submission, that kimchi and fermented vegetables sit below 0.1 ug/100 g and that lion's mane contains the inactive B12[c-lactone] analogue, could not be traced to the cited review and are recorded here as indicative and unsourced.
items.dose_from_food_note: Against the 2.4 ug/day RDA there is no gap for anyone eating animal food: one 3 oz portion of cooked clams is 35 times the RDA, a slice of beef liver 20 times, a can of sardines 3.4 times. Against the supplement dose the gap cannot be closed. Oral B12 products are typically 500-1,000 ug, and 1,000-2,000 ug for treating deficiency. To have 1,000 ug physically present in a meal takes 1.01 kg of cooked clams, 1.17 kg of pan-fried lamb liver, 1.42 kg of braised beef liver, 4.17 kg of cooked blue mussels, 11.2 kg of canned sardines, 35.7 kg of cooked salmon, or 222 kg of whole milk, which is about 216 litres (the submission's '222 litres' confused grams with litres; 1,000/0.0045 = 222,222 g, and at about 1.03 kg/L that is 216 L). No one could eat any of those. The comparison is also the wrong one, because intrinsic-factor-mediated absorption saturates at about 1.5-2.0 ug per meal (Watanabe, Exp Biol Med 2007;232:1266-74, PMID 17959839), so everything above roughly 2 ug in a single sitting is absorbed only by passive diffusion at on the order of 1%. A 1,000 ug tablet works because 1% of 1,000 ug bypasses the receptor route, which no food can imitate and none needs to unless that route is broken. For a strict vegan the picture inverts: nothing reliably supplies even the 2.4 ug RDA except dried nori, and Watanabe puts the requirement at about 4 g/day of dried purple laver, which is about one and a third 3 g sheets every day (the submission said one and a half) from a product varying about elevenfold by origin. Fortified foods or a tablet are the honest answer.

items.form_caveat: Supplements use cyanocobalamin, a form not found in food, where the cyanide ligand is an artefact of the purification step and is removed intracellularly. Food B12 is protein-bound and needs gastric acid and pepsin to release it before intrinsic factor can take it up, so proton pump inhibitors, atrophic gastritis, gastric surgery and metformin knock out food B12 while leaving free crystalline B12 in a tablet or fortified cereal largely usable. Here the supplement is the mechanistically correct choice, and not merely the convenient one. The form risk with algae products runs opposite to the usual concentration worry: a spirulina capsule sold as a B12 source delivers mostly inactive pseudovitamin B12, and the microbiological assay behind the label number could not distinguish it from the real thing, so the label overstates delivered B12 rather than the dose being too strong. Note also that USDA gives yeast extract spread only 0.50 ug B12/100 g (FDC 167717), which is 0.03 ug per 6 g teaspoon: yeast does not make B12, so any yeast product that is a real source has been fortified and the number belongs to the fortification.
items.bioavailability: About 50% of dietary B12 is assumed absorbed from a normal meal, but it varies sharply by food: fish 42%, sheep meat 56-89%, chicken 61-66% and eggs under 9% (Watanabe 2007, PMID 17959839). The egg figure matters because eggs are routinely offered to vegetarians as a B12 food; on absorbed B12 a large egg delivers about 0.04 ug, which is 1.7% of the RDA rather than the 19% the content figure implies. Cooking costs real B12. USDA Table of Nutrient Retention Factors Release 6 (2007) gives 70% for roasted beef (code 0601), 60% for beef braised or simmered without the drippings (0651/0653), 65% for roasted chicken (0805), 60% for liver simmered without drippings (1152), 90% for baked lean finfish (2301), 60% for shellfish boiled in the shell (2701) against 90% steamed (2702), and 30% for milk held at heat for an hour (2153). Keeping the pan juices recovers much of it, which is why the with-drippings factors run exactly 15 points higher. One methodological point earned by the corrected mussel row: where USDA publishes a cooked composition entry, use it, because a hand-applied retention factor ignores the moisture loss that concentrates B12 and in this case halved the figure for the food people actually eat.

items.food_status_note: Vitamin B6 itself is abundant and widely distributed, with fish, organ meat, poultry, potatoes, bananas, seeds, nuts and fortified cereals all carrying useful amounts, and dietary deficiency uncommon in people eating normally. The marketed high-dose object is a different thing: pyridoxine hydrochloride, a manufactured crystalline salt sold at 50, 100 and sometimes 250-500 mg per tablet, which is 40 to 400 times the 1.3 mg adult RDA and has no dietary counterpart at that concentration. Both statements are true at once, which is why the label is split here: the molecule is RICH in food (so RICH stands rather than being reclassified as synthetic), while the product as sold is unreachable by eating, which is what dose_from_food now records. All percentages below use the 1.3 mg RDA for ages 19-50; over 50 the RDA rises to 1.7 mg for men and 1.5 mg for women, so these percentages overstate the contribution for older adults.
items.dose_from_food_note: A 100 mg pyridoxine tablet is 77 times the RDA. Matching it by eating, in one day, takes 7.46 kg of dried sunflower kernels, 8.93 kg of pistachios, 9.80 kg of braised beef liver, 10.7 kg of raw yellowfin tuna, 16.7 kg of roasted chicken breast, or 27.2 kg of banana, about 231 medium bananas. A 50 mg tablet still needs 4.46 kg of pistachios or 116 bananas. Even the regulatory ceiling sits outside dietary reach: EFSA's 2023 tolerable upper intake level of 12 mg/day for adults corresponds to about 1.07 kg of pistachios or 3.27 kg of banana, roughly 28 bananas, every single day. Nobody eats any of that. Ordinary diets deliver a few mg per day, an order of magnitude below the UL and two to three orders below the supplement, and that is the mechanical reason dietary B6 has never produced the sensory neuropathy that supplements produce: no food is concentrated enough to approach the toxic range. The syndrome was described in seven adults taking megadose pyridoxine (Schaumburg H et al., 'Sensory neuropathy from pyridoxine abuse. A new megavitamin syndrome', N Engl J Med 1983;309:445-8, PMID 6308447), all of whom improved after withdrawal; the widely quoted 2-6 g/day range is secondary-literature summary that does not appear in the abstract, so treat it as unconfirmed and source any dose figure to the full text or to EFSA's case tabulation. Cases have since been reported at far lower supplemental doses, and EFSA cut the adult UL from the SCF's 25 mg/day to 12 mg/day on peripheral neuropathy grounds, from a 50 mg/day reference point with an uncertainty factor of 4 (EFSA NDA Panel, EFSA J 2023;21:e08006, PMID 37207271, DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2023.8006). Not one case has been attributed to food B6.

items.form_caveat: This is a genuine case where the food is safe and the concentrated form is not, and the reason is dose plus kinetics rather than any exotic compound. Food B6 arrives as pyridoxal phosphate and pyridoxamine phosphate bound in the matrix, plus glycosylated pyridoxine in plant foods, released and absorbed gradually across a meal. A tablet delivers a bolus of free pyridoxine. The accepted mechanism for the neuropathy is that free pyridoxine at high concentration outruns conversion to pyridoxal 5-phosphate and acts at PLP-dependent sites in the dorsal root ganglion, which lacks a blood-nerve barrier. Pyridoxal-5-phosphate supplements are marketed as the safe alternative on the strength of that mechanism, but the human evidence is thin and EFSA applies its 12 mg/day UL to total B6 regardless of form, so treating P5P as exempt has no support. One practical consequence: because B6 is added to energy drinks, fortified cereals and B-complex products, people accumulate supplemental doses without intending to, and the UL is easy to cross by stacking products while eating a diet that contributes almost nothing to the risk.
items.bioavailability: Roughly 75% of dietary B6 is absorbed. Plant B6 is partly pyridoxine-5'-beta-D-glucoside, which is about half as available as free pyridoxine and can act as a weak antagonist: a diet supplying 27% of its B6 as PNG lowered plasma total B6 and red cell PLP in women, an effect the authors quantified as a 15-18% loss of total B6 intake (Hansen, Leklem and Miller, J Nutr 1996;126:2512-8, PMID 8857512). That is a real discount on high-PNG plant diets and a modest one, so it should not be stretched into a claim that plant-food B6 numbers are broadly unreliable. Cooking removes more. USDA Table of Nutrient Retention Factors Release 6 (2007) gives B6 retention of 50% for roasted beef (code 0601), 35% for beef braised or simmered without the drippings (0651/0653), 45% for liver simmered without drippings (1152), 80% for roasted chicken (0805), 50% for legumes boiled 2-2.5 h (0541), 65% for legumes boiled 45-75 min and drained (0521) and 85% for greens boiled in water to cover (3005). A raw-basis figure such as the 0.933 mg/100 g for raw tuna is not what lands on the plate.

items.food_status_note: Genuinely rich and cheap in ordinary food, and the verification pass challenged this classification and upheld it as the strongest in the set: one 119 g red pepper (152 mg) or one 55 g guava (125 mg) exceeds the 90 mg adult male RDA on its own, with no trace-amount inflation anywhere in the list. Synthetic ascorbic acid is manufactured (Reichstein or two-step fermentation from glucose), but it is the identical molecule, so the synthetic label carries no penalty here. Percentages below are given against both DRI values, since the RDA is 90 mg for men and 75 mg for women and quoting only the male figure understates every food's contribution for women by 20%. Rose hips, camu-camu, chilli peppers, papaya and Brussels sprouts are further rich sources for which no verified figure was available, so they get no row.
items.dose_from_food_note: This is the one item in the set where the supplement dose is physically reachable by eating. A 1,000 mg tablet equals 60 g of raw acerola, about 12 small fruits, or 439 g of guava (8 fruits), or 552 g of blackcurrants, or 781 g of raw red pepper (about 6.6 medium peppers), or 1.07 kg of raw kale, or 1.70 kg of strawberries, or 1.88 kg of orange (14 medium oranges), or 2.0 kg of fresh orange juice, which is about 1.9 litres (the submission's '2.0 litres' confused grams with litres). A 500 mg dose is 3.3 red peppers or 7 oranges. Eccentric for most of that list, and trivially easy through acerola, so a person genuinely could eat this dose. The real gap is that the dose above roughly 200 mg is pointless rather than unreachable. Levine et al. gave 30-2,500 mg/day under depletion-repletion control: bioavailability was complete at a single 200 mg dose and fell off at 500 mg and above with the absorbed excess appearing in urine, while leucocytes saturated at 100 mg/day and plasma at 1,000 mg/day (PNAS 1996;93:3704-9, PMID 8623000, DOI 10.1073/pnas.93.8.3704). Four or five servings of ordinary fruit and vegetables reach the physiologically useful plateau, and the 1,000 mg tablet mostly funds expensive urine. The number that should temper any composition table is what survives handling: see cooking and storage below.

items.form_caveat: Effectively NONE on the molecule. Synthetic and food-derived vitamin C are chemically identical and all steady-state human comparative bioavailability studies show no difference, with some acute pharmacokinetic studies showing minor transient differences of no physiological consequence (Carr and Vissers, Nutrients 2013;5:4284-304, PMID 24169506, DOI 10.3390/nu5114284). That kills the claim that natural vitamin C is better absorbed, and it means acerola, camu-camu and rose hip products carry no absorption advantage; most such products are in any case standardised by adding synthetic ascorbic acid, so the buyer gets the synthetic molecule with fruit powder attached. Note that acerola still earns a food row on content alone, at 1,680 mg/100 g the richest verified source in the database, which is a separate matter from the debunked absorption claim. What the whole food genuinely adds is the rest of the matrix, potassium, folate, carotenoids, flavonoids and fibre, none of which is in the tablet and none of which the vitamin C evidence is about. Where a caveat does bite is the textbook recommendation to eat spinach: its vitamin C is modest at 28.1 mg/100 g, a realistic 30 g cup gives 8.4 mg, and boiling extracts most of what is there, moving 60% of the vitamin C and 50% of the flavonoids of fresh-cut spinach into the cooking water (Gil, Ferreres and Tomas-Barberan, J Agric Food Chem 1999;47:2213-7, PMID 10794612). Recommending boiled spinach for vitamin C comes close to recommending the cooking water. Raw kale at 93.4 mg/100 g is the green that actually delivers, three times the spinach figure.
items.bioavailability: Absorption is near-complete up to about 200 mg per dose via the sodium-dependent transporter SVCT1, declines above 500 mg, and plasma saturates at 1,000 mg/day (PMID 8623000). Absorption is therefore not the variable that matters; retention before eating is. Cooking and storage losses, all from USDA Table of Nutrient Retention Factors Release 6 (2007), ascorbic acid column: greens boiled in water to cover and drained retain 55% (code 3005), greens boiled in a little water and drained 60% (3004), greens stir-fried 85% (3015), greens cooked from frozen and drained 60% (3019); other vegetables boiled in water to cover and drained 75% (3775), steamed 85% (3784); potatoes baked in the skin 80% (3301), boiled pared and drained 75% (3308), and only 25% when boiled after storage and browned (3311); canned fruit 50% (0154) and dried fruit 20% (0158). Steaming beats boiling and draining consistently: in broccoli every method except steaming caused significant loss of vitamin C and chlorophyll (Yuan et al., J Zhejiang Univ Sci B 2009;10:580-8, PMID 19650196, DOI 10.1631/jzus.b0920051). Storage compounds it: 15 days at 4 C across 19 fruits and vegetables lowered vitamin C and cut total phenolics by up to 29.67%, though total anthocyanins showed minimal change in that study despite the title (Galani et al., Antioxidants 2017;6(3):59, PMID 28737734). Practical upshot: a week-old boiled vegetable can deliver a quarter of its table value, so the 27% loss between raw broccoli at 89.2 mg/100 g and boiled broccoli at 64.9 mg/100 g is the optimistic case rather than the worst one.
items.data_confidence: HIGH. All ten original per-100 g values and all gram weights matched named FoodData Central records exactly, including the raw and boiled broccoli split, and every per-portion figure recomputed. All five cited PMIDs resolve to the stated journal, volume and pages with findings matching the abstracts, and eleven retention factors were verified row by row against Release 6. Two smaller qualifications: the acerola and kale figures come from the verification report's own FDC lookups rather than the original submission, and the 100 g kale portion basis is stated by this dataset rather than taken from a USDA household measure.
corrections_applied: Corrected the orange juice unit slip: a 1,000 mg dose is 2.0 kg of fresh juice, about 1.9 litres, not 2.0 litres
Stated the RDA basis and added the female figure to every percentage, since the 90 mg male RDA alone understates each food's contribution for women by 20% (RDA 75 mg)

Corrected the refrigerated storage claim: total phenolics fell by up to 29.67% and vitamin C declined over 15 days at 4 C, but the paper reports minimal change in total anthocyanins, so anthocyanins were dropped from the claim (Galani et al., Antioxidants 2017;6(3):59)
Fixed the misattributed retention code for stir-fried greens: 3015, not 3008, and added the codes for the factors the submission listed by name only (3019, 3775, 3784, 3308, 0154, 0158)

Added raw acerola (1,680 mg/100 g, FDC 171686, 81 mg per 4.8 g fruit), which the submission mentioned only as something being debunked despite it being the richest verified source in the database, and added the 60 g / about 12 fruits figure for a 1,000 mg dose
Added raw kale (93.4 mg/100 g, FDC 168421) and named it in the spinach passage as the green that actually delivers, plus 1.07 kg of kale for a 1,000 mg dose
Split the single availability label into food_status (RICH, challenged and upheld) and dose_from_food (YES), the one item in this group where the two answers agree
Reordered the food rows richest first per realistic portion, which drops acerola to mid-list on its sub-5 g fruit weight and puts blackcurrants first

items.food_status_note_zh: 合成叶酸（folic acid，蝶酰单谷氨酸 pteroylmonoglutamic acid）由化学合成制造，通过 Waller 型缩合反应把三氨基嘧啶酮、一个三碳单元和对氨基苯甲酰-L-谷氨酸缩合起来，得到一个完全氧化、只带单个谷氨酸残基的分子，未强化的食物里并不存在这种形式。普通食物提供的是还原型叶酸多谷氨酸盐，主要是 5-甲基四氢叶酸。USDA 的成分体系把 folic acid 和 folate, food 列为两个独立条目：牛肝、扁豆、菠菜、鹰嘴豆、芦笋和水煮西兰花的 folic acid 全部读作 0，而 folate food 等于 folate total。一个词里装着两个答案，这里把它们分开：作为营养素类别的叶酸在普通食物中含量丰富；作为在售分子的 folic acid 只能通过强化和营养素添加进入食物供应，下面每一行食物都属于这种情况。强化意面和强化白米是美国另外两种法定的营养素添加载体，含量随具体产品的标签而定，没有可核实的数据，因此不单列。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 两条路径给出不同答案。按 folic acid 计，孕前 400 µg 的剂量只有强化产品能一次吃到：一碗按每份 400 µg folic acid 强化的即食谷物就是全部剂量；用酵母提取物涂抹酱要约 13 g（两茶匙多一点），用强化速食燕麦片要 8.2 包，用强化面粉做的小麦面包约 69 片。按天然食物叶酸计，等效目标是 680 µg DFE（400 x 1.7），核查环节正是在这里改出一处错误：原稿最省的选项是 376 g 熟扁豆，但炖鸡肝每 100 g 含食物叶酸 578 µg（FDC 171061），只需 118 g，不到三块 44 g 的鸡肝，属于正常份量；煎羊肝每 100 g 400 µg DFE（FDC 172533），需要 170 g。植物路径依旧别扭：376 g 熟扁豆（1.9 杯）、219 g 处理好的毛豆（1.4 杯）、300 g 干葵花籽仁、351 g 生菠菜（约十二杯，每杯 30 g）、395 g 熟鹰嘴豆、456 g 熟芦笋（约三十根）或 630 g 水煮西兰花。所以直白的结论是：一个人可以靠肝脏或强化食品吃到相当于 400 µg 剂量的叶酸量，靠绿叶菜现实中做不到；英国面向高风险人群的 5 mg 剂量（8,500 µg DFE，相当于每天 1.47 kg 鸡肝或 4.7 kg 熟扁豆）任何路径都达不到。肝脏本身因预成型维生素 A 而在孕期受限，这也是它很少被拿来当作那个最需要该剂量的人群的答案的原因。
items.form_caveat_zh: folic acid 与食物叶酸并非生物等同，差异在两个方向上都成立。它必须先由二氢叶酸还原酶（DHFR）还原才能进入一碳代谢，而人的 DHFR 能力很低：每餐 folic acid 超过约 266 µg 这一阈值后，血清中就会出现未代谢的 folic acid（Kelly 等, Am J Clin Nutr 1997;65:1790-5, PMID 9174474），一片 400 µg 的片剂已经超过。这正是成人每日 1,000 µg 的 UL 只适用于补充剂和强化食品中的 folic acid、而食物叶酸没有 UL 的原因：高剂量 folic acid 可以纠正 B12 缺乏引起的巨幼细胞性贫血，同时神经损害继续进展，掩盖诊断。食物叶酸没有毒性上限，合成形式有。反方向看，食物叶酸的障碍也不止于量。Cuskelly、McNulty 与 Scott 把 62 名女性随机分组，每天额外补 400 µg，分别以 folic acid 补充剂、folic acid 强化食品、天然食物叶酸或饮食指导的形式给予：红细胞叶酸只在补充剂组和强化食品组上升，食物叶酸组尽管摄入量有记录在案的增加却毫无变化（Lancet 1996;347:657-9, PMID 8596381）。确立神经管缺陷预防效果的两项试验用的都是合成 folic acid：MRC Vitamin Study 的 4 mg/天（Lancet 1991;338:131-7, PMID 1677062），以及 Czeizel 与 Dudas 用复合维生素给的 0.8 mg/天（N Engl J Med 1992;327:1832-5, PMID 1307234）。孕前用绿叶菜替代片剂，从未针对这一终点做过检验。关于 L-5-甲基四氢叶酸（甲基叶酸钙），也就是市面上以适合 MTHFR 基因型为卖点的替代品：EFSA 2022 年推导其 DFE 系数时判定，在每天 400 µg 及以上的补充剂量下，5-MTHF 的生物利用度高于 folic acid（2.0 对 1.7；PMC9399872），所以反对它的理由与吸收无关。问题在于至今没有做过孕前使用的试验，而神经管缺陷的证据基础明确是 folic acid（Czeizel, Ann Nutr Metab 2011, PMID 21865678）。
items.bioavailability_zh: 食物叶酸的可利用率大致 50%，与食物一起摄入的 folic acid 约 85%，空腹接近 100%，1.7 和 2.0 两个 DFE 换算系数就是从这里来的（Suitor 与 Bailey, J Am Diet Assoc 2000;100:88-94, PMID 10646010）。食物叶酸是多谷氨酸盐，吸收前必须在刷状缘去结合，而且化学性质脆弱。USDA 营养素保留系数表（Table of Nutrient Retention Factors）第 6 版（2007）给出的叶酸保留率是：豆类煮 45-75 min 后沥干 45%（代码 0521），豆类煮 2-2.5 h 为 30%（代码 0541），绿叶菜加水没过煮后沥干 60%（代码 3005），带皮烤马铃薯 90%（代码 3301）。一杯干扁豆炖一小时会损失一半以上的叶酸，因此成分表数值只有在烹饪方式对得上时才描述熟食的实际含量。强化食品或片剂里的 folic acid 稳定，剂量就是标签写的那个数。
items.data_confidence_zh: 高。食物行和剂量对比中的每一个每 100 g 成分值、克重和每份数值都可追溯到具名的 USDA FoodData Central 记录，重算完全吻合，引用的六个 PMID 全部指向所述期刊、卷号和页码。两点限定：强化谷物那一行是指示性的标签数据，并非有来源的成分记录；另有一条没有引文的生物利用度说法被删除，没有保留。

items.food_status_note_zh: 动物性食物中含量丰富，植物性食物中基本没有，因为钴胺素只由细菌和古菌合成：所有可靠来源都是积累了细菌 B12 的动物，或经细菌发酵、或经强化的产品。RICH 这一个词依人群而定，还藏着一次反转，所以直说：对杂食者，B12 是整个食物供应里最容易获得的营养素之一；对吃未强化植物性饮食的人，同样的证据意味着它基本缺席，唯一可信来源是干紫菜，每张 3 g 的紫菜片含 2.33 µg，而这种产品的含量随产地相差约十一倍，并会因烘烤和储存而降解。关于几种有争议的植物候选来源：螺旋藻不可用，其钴酰胺中 83% 是假维生素 B12（腺嘌呤基钴酰胺），对人无活性，真正的 B12 只占 17%，微生物法测定又无法区分两者，这就是标签上 B12 数值很高的原因（Watanabe 等, J Agric Food Chem 1999;47:4736-41, PMID 10552882）；紫菜可用，是唯一可信的植物来源，含五种有生物活性的钴胺素形式，其中腺苷钴胺素和甲基钴胺素约占总量的 60%，并在缺乏 B12 的大鼠身上纠正了 B12 状态（Takenaka S 等, Br J Nutr 2001;85:699-703, PMID 11430774）；天贝不可靠，0.7-8.0 µg/100 g，取决于根霉发酵过程中恰好污染进去的是哪种细菌；食用菌不可用，干香菇平均 5.61 µg/100 g 干重（范围 1.3-12.7），黑喇叭菌（black trumpet）和金黄鸡油菌 1.09-2.65 µg/100 g 干重，其他多数种类约 0.09 µg/100 g 或仅为痕量；小球藻在不同产品之间从零到几百 µg/100 g 不等，无法依赖（以上均出自 Watanabe 等, Nutrients 2014;6:1861-73, PMID 24803097）。原稿另有两处说法，即泡菜和发酵蔬菜低于 0.1 µg/100 g，以及猴头菇含无活性的 B12[c-lactone] 类似物，无法在所引综述中找到出处，这里记为指示性且无来源。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 对照每日 2.4 µg 的 RDA，吃动物性食物的人不存在缺口：一份 3 oz 熟蛤蜊是 RDA 的 35 倍，一片牛肝 20 倍，一罐沙丁鱼 3.4 倍。对照补充剂剂量，缺口无法弥合。口服 B12 产品通常是 500-1,000 µg，治疗缺乏时 1,000-2,000 µg。要让一餐里实际存在 1,000 µg，需要 1.01 kg 熟蛤蜊、1.17 kg 煎羊肝、1.42 kg 炖牛肝、4.17 kg 熟蓝贻贝、11.2 kg 罐装沙丁鱼、35.7 kg 熟三文鱼，或 222 kg 全脂牛奶，约合 216 升（原稿写的 222 升把克和升搞混了；1,000/0.0045 = 222,222 g，按约 1.03 kg/L 折算是 216 L）。这些没人吃得下。这个对比本身也问错了问题，因为内因子介导的吸收在每餐约 1.5-2.0 µg 处饱和（Watanabe, Exp Biol Med 2007;232:1266-74, PMID 17959839），一次进食中超过约 2 µg 的部分只能靠被动扩散吸收，效率大约 1%。1,000 µg 的片剂之所以有效，是因为 1,000 µg 的 1% 绕开了受体途径，任何食物都模仿不了，而只要该途径没坏，也不需要模仿。对严格素食者，情况反转：除了干紫菜，没有任何食物能可靠提供哪怕 2.4 µg 的 RDA，Watanabe 把需要量定在每天约 4 g 干紫菜，相当于每天约一又三分之一张 3 g 的紫菜片（原稿说的是一张半），而这种产品的含量随产地相差约十一倍。强化食品或片剂才是诚实的答案。
items.form_caveat_zh: 补充剂用的是氰钴胺，食物中不存在这种形式，其中的氰基是提纯步骤留下的产物，进入细胞后会被去除。食物中的 B12 与蛋白结合，需要胃酸和胃蛋白酶先把它释放出来，内因子才能摄取，所以质子泵抑制剂、萎缩性胃炎、胃部手术和二甲双胍会废掉食物 B12，而片剂或强化谷物里游离的结晶 B12 大体仍可利用。在这一项上，补充剂是机制上正确的选择，不只是图方便。藻类产品的形式风险与通常担心的浓度问题方向相反：作为 B12 来源出售的螺旋藻胶囊，交付的主要是无活性的假维生素 B12，而标签数字背后的微生物法测定无法把它和真货区分开，所以标签高估了实际提供的 B12，这里的风险与剂量过强无关。另外注意，USDA 给酵母提取物涂抹酱的 B12 只有 0.50 µg/100 g（FDC 167717），每 6 g 一茶匙合 0.03 µg：酵母不产生 B12，所以任何真能算作来源的酵母产品都经过强化，那个数字属于强化本身。
items.bioavailability_zh: 一般假定正常膳食中约 50% 的 B12 被吸收，但按食物差别很大：鱼 42%，羊肉 56-89%，鸡肉 61-66%，鸡蛋不到 9%（Watanabe 2007, PMID 17959839）。鸡蛋这个数字要紧，因为素食者常被推荐把鸡蛋当作 B12 食物来源；按实际吸收量算，一个大鸡蛋提供约 0.04 µg，占 RDA 的 1.7%，而含量数字给人的印象是 19%。烹饪会真实损失 B12。USDA 营养素保留系数表（Table of Nutrient Retention Factors）第 6 版（2007）给出：烤牛肉 70%（代码 0601），牛肉炖或煮且不计肉汁 60%（0651/0653），烤鸡 65%（0805），肝脏煮制不计肉汁 60%（1152），瘦身有鳍鱼烤制 90%（2301），带壳水煮贝类 60%（2701）而蒸制 90%（2702），牛奶持续加热一小时 30%（2153）。留住锅里的汤汁能收回很大一部分，这也是带肉汁的系数正好高 15 个百分点的原因。修正后的贻贝那一行还带出一个方法学要点：USDA 只要发布了熟食成分条目就该用它，因为手工套用保留系数会忽略水分流失对 B12 的浓缩作用，本例中这样做把人们真正吃到的那种食物的数值砍掉了一半。
items.data_confidence_zh: 动物性食物各行为高：每一个每 100 g 数值和克重都可追溯到具名的 FoodData Central 记录，每个每份数值和百分比都能重算得出，Watanabe 和 Takenaka 的引文也都指向所述期刊、卷号和页码。有两处较低，并且是明说而非隐藏：紫菜数据和整个纯素饮食结论都依赖单一份汇编综述（Watanabe 2014），该综述自身的产品含量跨度约十一倍；泡菜和猴头菇两条说法无法追溯到任何引用来源，已标为指示性。羊肝和太平洋牡蛎的 3 oz 份量基准由本数据集给出，并非取自 USDA 的家庭常用量。

foods_zh.food_zh: 强化营养酵母、强化植物奶和强化早餐谷物

items.food_status_note_zh: 维生素 B6 本身分布广泛、含量充足，鱼、内脏、禽肉、马铃薯、香蕉、种子、坚果和强化谷物都带有可观的量，正常饮食的人很少出现膳食性缺乏。市面上的大剂量产品是另一回事：盐酸吡哆醇，一种人工制造的结晶盐，以每片 50、100、有时 250-500 mg 出售，相当于成人 RDA 1.3 mg 的 40 到 400 倍，膳食中没有任何东西达到这个浓度。两句话同时成立，所以这里把标签拆开：这个分子在食物中确实丰富（因此保留 RICH，不改判为合成），而以在售形态出现的产品靠吃达不到，这就是 dose_from_food 现在记录的内容。下面所有百分比都按 19-50 岁的 1.3 mg RDA 计算；50 岁以上 RDA 升至男性 1.7 mg、女性 1.5 mg，所以这些百分比高估了对年长成年人的贡献。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 一片 100 mg 的吡哆醇是 RDA 的 77 倍。要在一天之内靠吃达到同样的量，需要 7.46 kg 干葵花籽仁、8.93 kg 开心果、9.80 kg 炖牛肝、10.7 kg 生黄鳍金枪鱼、16.7 kg 烤鸡胸肉，或 27.2 kg 香蕉，约 231 根中等大小的香蕉。50 mg 的片剂也仍需 4.46 kg 开心果或 116 根香蕉。连监管上限都在膳食可及范围之外：EFSA 2023 年为成人定的可耐受最高摄入量 12 mg/天，相当于每天约 1.07 kg 开心果或 3.27 kg 香蕉，约 28 根香蕉。这些没有人会吃。普通饮食每天提供几 mg，比 UL 低一个数量级，比补充剂低两到三个数量级，这就是膳食 B6 从未造成补充剂那种感觉神经病变的机械原因：没有食物浓到能接近中毒范围。该综合征最初描述于 7 名服用超大剂量吡哆醇的成年人（Schaumburg H 等, Sensory neuropathy from pyridoxine abuse. A new megavitamin syndrome, N Engl J Med 1983;309:445-8, PMID 6308447），停用后全部好转；被广泛引用的 2-6 g/天这个区间出自二手文献的概述，摘要里并没有，因此按未确认处理，任何剂量数字都应回到全文或 EFSA 的病例汇总去核对。此后在低得多的补充剂量下也有病例报告，EFSA 以周围神经病变为依据，把成人 UL 从 SCF 的 25 mg/天下调到 12 mg/天，参考点为 50 mg/天，不确定系数取 4（EFSA NDA Panel, EFSA J 2023;21:e08006, PMID 37207271, DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2023.8006）。没有一例被归因于食物中的 B6。
items.form_caveat_zh: 这是食物安全而浓缩形态不安全的一个真实案例，原因是剂量加动力学，与什么特殊化合物无关。食物中的 B6 以磷酸吡哆醛和磷酸吡哆胺的形式结合在食物基质里，植物性食物中还有糖苷化的吡哆醇，在一餐中被逐步释放和吸收。片剂送进去的是一次性的游离吡哆醇冲击量。公认的神经病变机制是：高浓度的游离吡哆醇超出了转化为 5-磷酸吡哆醛（PLP）的能力，并在背根神经节的 PLP 依赖位点上产生作用，而背根神经节没有血神经屏障。5-磷酸吡哆醛补充剂正是凭这套机制被当成安全替代品来卖，但人体证据薄弱，而且 EFSA 把 12 mg/天的 UL 用于各种形式的 B6 总量，所以把 P5P 当成例外没有依据。一个现实后果：由于能量饮料、强化谷物和复合 B 族产品里都加了 B6，人们会在无意中累积到补充剂级别的剂量，叠加几种产品就很容易越过 UL，而饮食对这个风险几乎没有贡献。
items.bioavailability_zh: 膳食 B6 约 75% 被吸收。植物中的 B6 有一部分是吡哆醇-5'-β-D-葡萄糖苷（PNG），可利用率约为游离吡哆醇的一半，还能起弱拮抗作用：一份 27% 的 B6 以 PNG 形式提供的饮食，降低了女性的血浆总 B6 和红细胞 PLP，作者把这一效应量化为总 B6 摄入量损失 15-18%（Hansen、Leklem 与 Miller, J Nutr 1996;126:2512-8, PMID 8857512）。对 PNG 比例高的植物性饮食，这是一个真实而幅度有限的折扣，不应被放大成植物性食物 B6 数据普遍不可靠。烹饪损失更多。USDA 营养素保留系数表（Table of Nutrient Retention Factors）第 6 版（2007）给出的 B6 保留率：烤牛肉 50%（代码 0601），牛肉炖或煮且不计肉汁 35%（0651/0653），肝脏煮制不计肉汁 45%（1152），烤鸡 80%（0805），豆类煮 2-2.5 h 为 50%（0541），豆类煮 45-75 min 后沥干 65%（0521），绿叶菜加水没过煮 85%（3005）。像生金枪鱼 0.933 mg/100 g 这样的生品数值，与最终上桌的量不是一回事。
items.data_confidence_zh: 高。九个成分值和所有克重都已对照具名的 FoodData Central 记录核实，包括开心果的 13 个数据点及其 0.484-1.80 分析范围，每一项剂量差距的用量都逐行重算过。EFSA 2023 意见、其 12 mg/天 UL、50 mg 参考点和不确定系数 4 全部核对无误。唯一的薄弱环节已就地标注：附在 Schaumburg 1983 上的 2-6 g/天出自二手文献概述，摘要中没有，因此以未确认的形式呈现。

items.food_status_note_zh: 在普通食物里真正丰富而且便宜。核查环节对这一分类提出质疑并予以确认，认定它是整组里最扎实的一项：一个 119 g 的红甜椒（152 mg）或一个 55 g 的番石榴（125 mg）单独就超过成人男性 90 mg 的 RDA，整份清单里没有任何靠痕量堆数字的地方。合成抗坏血酸是制造出来的（Reichstein 法，或以葡萄糖为原料的两步发酵法），但它是完全相同的分子，所以合成这个标签在这里不带任何折扣。下面的百分比同时给出两个 DRI 数值，因为 RDA 男性为 90 mg、女性为 75 mg，只引男性数字会把每种食物对女性的贡献低估 20%。玫瑰果、卡姆果（camu-camu）、辣椒、木瓜和抱子甘蓝也是富含来源，但没有可核实的数据，因此不单列。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 这是整组里唯一一个靠吃就能在物理上达到补充剂剂量的项目。1,000 mg 的片剂等于 60 g 生针叶樱桃，约 12 颗小果，或 439 g 番石榴（8 个），或 552 g 黑加仑，或 781 g 生红甜椒（约 6.6 个中等大小），或 1.07 kg 生羽衣甘蓝，或 1.70 kg 草莓，或 1.88 kg 橙子（14 个中等大小），或 2.0 kg 鲜榨橙汁，约合 1.9 升（原稿写的 2.0 升把克和升搞混了）。500 mg 的剂量是 3.3 个红甜椒或 7 个橙子。这份清单上大多数选项都很古怪，通过针叶樱桃则轻而易举，所以一个人确实吃得到这个剂量。真正的问题在别处：超过约 200 mg 的剂量吃得到，只是没有意义。Levine 等在耗竭-补足的对照条件下给予 30-2,500 mg/天：单次 200 mg 剂量的生物利用度是完全的，500 mg 及以上开始下降，吸收后多余的部分出现在尿中；白细胞在 100 mg/天饱和，血浆在 1,000 mg/天饱和（PNAS 1996;93:3704-9, PMID 8623000, DOI 10.1073/pnas.93.8.3704）。四到五份普通蔬果就能达到生理上有用的平台，1,000 mg 的片剂多半只是在为昂贵的尿液付钱。该给成分表打折的那个数字是经过处理后还剩下多少，见下面的烹饪与储存部分。
items.form_caveat_zh: 就分子本身而言基本没有。合成与来自食物的维生素 C 化学上完全相同，所有稳态条件下的人体比较生物利用度研究都显示没有差别，部分急性药代动力学研究显示的轻微短暂差异没有生理意义（Carr 与 Vissers, Nutrients 2013;5:4284-304, PMID 24169506, DOI 10.3390/nu5114284）。这否掉了天然维生素 C 吸收更好的说法，也意味着针叶樱桃、卡姆果和玫瑰果产品在吸收上没有优势；这类产品本来大多靠添加合成抗坏血酸来做标准化，买家拿到的是带着果粉的合成分子。要注意针叶樱桃仍然凭含量单独占一行，1,680 mg/100 g 是数据库中已核实的最富来源，这与被否掉的吸收说法是两件事。整个食物真正多给的是基质里的其余成分，钾、叶酸、类胡萝卜素、类黄酮和膳食纤维，片剂里都没有，而维生素 C 的证据讲的也不是这些。真正需要警告的是教科书式的吃菠菜补维生素 C 这条建议：菠菜的维生素 C 含量一般，28.1 mg/100 g，现实中一杯 30 g 只给 8.4 mg，而水煮会把里面的大部分萃取出去，鲜切菠菜有 60% 的维生素 C 和 50% 的类黄酮进了煮菜的水里（Gil、Ferreres 与 Tomas-Barberan, J Agric Food Chem 1999;47:2213-7, PMID 10794612）。推荐用水煮菠菜补维生素 C，差不多等于推荐那锅水。生羽衣甘蓝 93.4 mg/100 g 才是真正管用的绿叶菜，是菠菜数字的三倍。
items.bioavailability_zh: 每次剂量约 200 mg 以内，经钠依赖性转运体 SVCT1 的吸收接近完全，超过 500 mg 后下降，血浆在 1,000 mg/天饱和（PMID 8623000）。决定实际摄入的是入口前还能保留多少，吸收本身不构成变量。烹饪与储存损失全部出自 USDA 营养素保留系数表（Table of Nutrient Retention Factors）第 6 版（2007）的抗坏血酸一栏：绿叶菜加水没过煮后沥干保留 55%（代码 3005），加少量水煮后沥干 60%（3004），快炒 85%（3015），从冷冻直接烹制后沥干 60%（3019）；其他蔬菜加水没过煮后沥干 75%（3775），蒸 85%（3784）；带皮烤马铃薯 80%（3301），削皮水煮沥干 75%（3308），储存后再水煮并褐变的只有 25%（3311）；罐装水果 50%（0154），干制水果 20%（0158）。蒸一贯优于水煮后沥干：在西兰花上，除蒸制以外的每一种方法都造成维生素 C 和叶绿素的显著损失（Yuan 等, J Zhejiang Univ Sci B 2009;10:580-8, PMID 19650196, DOI 10.1631/jzus.b0920051）。储存会叠加：19 种蔬果在 4 C 下放 15 天，维生素 C 下降，总酚类最多减少 29.67%，不过该研究中总花青素变化很小，与标题给人的印象不同（Galani 等, Antioxidants 2017;6(3):59, PMID 28737734）。实际结论：放了一周又水煮过的蔬菜可能只剩成分表数值的四分之一，所以生西兰花 89.2 mg/100 g 到水煮西兰花 64.9 mg/100 g 之间那 27% 的损失属于乐观情形，最坏的情况比这更糟。
items.data_confidence_zh: 高。原稿的十个每 100 g 数值和所有克重都与具名的 FoodData Central 记录完全吻合，包括生西兰花与水煮西兰花的拆分，每个每份数值都能重算得出。引用的五个 PMID 全部指向所述期刊、卷号和页码，结论与摘要一致，十一个保留系数逐行对照第 6 版核实。两点较小的限定：针叶樱桃和羽衣甘蓝的数据来自核查环节自行查询的 FDC 记录，并非原稿提供；羽衣甘蓝 100 g 的份量基准由本数据集给出，并非取自 USDA 的家庭常用量。

items.food_status_note: Iron is genuinely abundant in ordinary food, in two chemically distinct forms that behave differently. Haem iron (offal, red meat, shellfish, blood sausage) is absorbed by a dedicated transporter and is largely indifferent to the rest of the plate; non-haem iron (legumes, seeds, greens, fortified flour) is the bulk of most people's intake and is absorbed at a fraction of the rate, heavily modified by vitamin C, polyphenols, phytate and calcium. Haem accounts for 77 percent of total iron in raw lean beef, 81 percent in lamb, 88 percent in pork and 74 percent in chicken (PMID 26433293), higher than the 40 percent assumed in the older Monsen equation; those fractions were measured in raw lean meat, so the haem share of a braised product is probably slightly lower than the calculations below imply. Reference point used in the table: EFSA PRI 16 mg/d for premenopausal women, 11 mg/d for men (EFSA, Dietary Reference Values for nutrients Summary report, approved 4 December 2017, doi 10.2903/sp.efsa.2017.e15121, Tables 5 and 7; underlying opinion EFSA Journal 2015;13(10):4254).
items.dose_from_food_note: Two supplement doses need two answers. A nutritional dose (14 to 18 mg elemental iron, the EU labelling reference level) is comfortably reachable by eating: 1 cup of boiled lentils (6.6 mg) plus 85 g of braised lamb's liver (7.0 mg) plus 1 oz of pumpkin seeds (2.3 mg) is 15.9 mg in one day, and a single 85 g portion of braised pig's liver is 15.2 mg on its own. A therapeutic dose is out of reach. The absorption and treatment trials gave 60 mg and 120 mg of elemental iron as labelled ferrous sulfate, which is a salt weight of about 325 mg for 65 mg of iron (PMID 29032957). Matching 65 mg of iron by total content takes roughly 363 g of braised pig's liver, 785 g of lamb's liver, 3.3 kg of sirloin steak, 1.95 kg (about 10 cups) of boiled lentils, or 2.4 kg (about 80 cups) of raw spinach in a single day. By absorbed iron the food burden is about 1.6 times larger than the submission claimed, because the trial it cites measured cumulative fractional absorption of 16.3 percent on consecutive days and 21.8 percent on alternate days at 60 mg/d, and 11.8 percent for a single 120 mg dose, rather than the 10 percent assumed. At the source's own 16.3 percent a 65 mg dose delivers about 10.6 mg absorbed. Absorbing 10.6 mg as haem iron at 25 percent requires 42.4 mg of haem iron, about 1.94 kg of braised lean lamb shoulder (2.7 mg total iron per 100 g, 81 percent haem in raw lean; FDC 174331 and PMID 26433293). Absorbing the same 10.6 mg from non-haem food at 5 percent requires 212 mg of non-haem iron, about 6.4 kg of cooked lentils per day. Correcting a diagnosed deficiency cannot be done with food; preventing one can.

items.form_caveat: Three traps, and the first is narrower than usually stated. (1) The retinol hazard belongs to liver, not to offal as a class. Braised lamb liver carries 7,490 ug retinol activity equivalents per 100 g, which is 6,367 ug in an 85 g portion, and braised beef liver 9,440 ug RAE per 100 g (raw beef liver 4,970 ug RAE; FDC 172532, 168626, 169451). That is why liver is contraindicated in pregnancy in most national guidance. The hazard separates cleanly by organ: braised lamb kidney is 12.4 mg iron with 137 ug RAE (FDC 174355) and braised pork kidney 5.29 mg iron with 78 ug RAE (FDC 167860), so kidney beats every muscle-meat row on iron without the vitamin A problem. The earlier claim that the iron benefit and the vitamin A hazard travel together and cannot be separated is withdrawn. (2) Liver's iron is largely ferritin and haemosiderin iron, so its headline 8.28 mg is less absorbable than the haem fraction of plain muscle meat implies, and muscle meat with a smaller number can deliver more absorbed iron. (3) Supplement iron behaves unlike food iron: a 60 mg dose raises hepcidin and suppresses absorption of the next dose, which is why alternate-day dosing absorbed 21.8 percent against 16.3 percent on consecutive days (PMID 29032957). Food iron arriving in small amounts across the day never triggers that. On spinach, the correction runs both ways. Isotope work found that potassium oxalate added to a low-oxalate kale meal did not change non-haem iron absorption (11.5 percent against 10.7 percent, P=0.86), so the textbook oxalate explanation does not survive testing. But the spinach meal in the same study absorbed 24 percent less than the matched kale meal without reaching significance (P>0.16), and although the paper reports spinach as significantly higher in calcium and polyphenols it does not attribute the absorption difference to them. The honest reading is that spinach iron was numerically lower in a single small study, the oxalate mechanism is refuted, and no replacement mechanism is established. Either way a 30 g bowl of raw spinach leaves contains 0.81 mg of iron and yields a rounding error.
items.bioavailability: Haem iron is absorbed at roughly 15 to 35 percent and non-haem at 2 to 20 percent, with iron status the dominant variable. Across whole diets rather than single meals, bioavailability is 14 to 18 percent for mixed diets and 5 to 12 percent for vegetarian diets in people with no iron stores, and the authors note that iron status generally has a greater effect than diet composition (PMID 20200263). Vitamin C: the source concludes that about 50 mg of ascorbic acid in each main meal is desirable for optimum effect, with the most pronounced effects in meals high in inhibitory ligands such as phytates and tannins (PMID 3700141). The '25 mg' lower bound and the 'several-fold' multiplier claimed earlier are not in that source and have been dropped. When the same amount of ascorbic acid is given across a complete diet over days, the facilitating effect is far less pronounced (PMID 11124756): squeezing lemon on your lentils helps, and it does not turn plant iron into meat iron. Tea and coffee inhibition, with numbers: a cup of coffee cut non-haem absorption from a hamburger meal by 39 percent and tea by 64 percent; instant coffee at double strength drove absorption from 5.88 percent to 0.53 percent; coffee one hour before the meal did no harm, while coffee one hour after inhibited as much as coffee with the meal (PMID 6402915). Black tea inhibited non-haem absorption by 79 to 94 percent, peppermint tea by 84 percent, cocoa by 71 percent and chamomile by 47 percent, dose-dependently on total polyphenols, and adding milk made no difference (PMID 10999016). That is polyphenol inhibition; phytate is a separate inhibitor sitting inside the wholegrains and legumes themselves. Practical consequence: the highest-yield single change for someone with low iron stores is moving tea and coffee to between meals rather than with or after them.
