items.food_status_note: Iodine occurs in ordinary food, and the answer rests on a narrow set of foods: dairy, white fish, eggs, shellfish and, where a country iodises it, table salt. Nothing else contributes meaningfully. The RICH classification carries a jurisdictional qualifier: for a UK reader it rests on dairy, white fish and eggs alone, because the UK has no salt iodisation programme, so the US iodised salt row below is not transferable and is marked as such. Iodine in milk is not intrinsic to the cow, it arrives from fortified cattle feed and iodophor teat disinfectants, which is why it is seasonal (higher in winter housing) and why organic milk is lower. Reference point used in the table: EFSA AI 150 ug/d for adults, 200 ug/d in pregnancy and lactation (EFSA, Dietary Reference Values for nutrients Summary report, approved 4 December 2017, doi 10.2903/sp.efsa.2017.e15121, Tables 5 and 7; underlying opinion EFSA Journal 2014;12(5):3660).
items.dose_from_food_note: There is essentially no gap. A standard iodine supplement or prenatal multivitamin supplies 150 ug, exactly the EFSA adult AI. A single 120 g UK haddock fillet delivers 390 ug, two and a half times the dose. One 115 g cod fillet delivers 131 ug. About 400 ml of milk delivers roughly 156 ug at milk density (412 g); the 151 ug figure quoted previously is what 1.6 USDA cups (398 g) gives, and the two should not be equated. Six large eggs deliver 147 ug. Half a teaspoon of iodised salt (3 g) delivers 152 ug where salt is iodised. Iodine belongs in the small category of supplements a normal eater does not need. The gap opens the moment those specific foods leave the diet, and the UK numbers are stark. Substituting three dairy portions a day (milk, yoghurt, cheese) with plant alternatives cuts the iodine those portions supply from 124 ug to 2.6 ug, a 97.9 percent loss, taking the contribution to the 150 ug recommendation from 83 percent down to 1.8 percent (PMID 35373723). The same market survey identified 146 milk alternatives and 76 yoghurt alternatives, excluded 48 organic products, and found 29 milk alternatives and 4 yoghurt alternatives iodine-fortified; that is 28 percent and 6 percent of the non-organic subset, or 19.9 percent and 5.3 percent of all products identified. The 28 and 6 percent figures quoted earlier against the full denominators were wrong. Against those, 88 percent and 73 percent were fortified with calcium; no cheese alternative and no fish alternative was iodine-fortified; and organic plant alternatives cannot legally be fortified. This shows up in real people: in NDNS years 7 to 9, adults and children consuming milk alternatives exclusively had an iodine intake of 94 ug/d against 129 ug/d for cows' milk consumers, and a median urinary iodine concentration of 79 ug/l against 132 ug/l, which classifies the milk-alternative group as iodine deficient by the WHO criterion while the milk drinkers were sufficient (PMID 32993817). Unfortified milk-alternative concentrations were a median 7.3 ug/kg, 1.7 percent of winter conventional cows' milk; the three fortified products found in 2015 sat at 266 to 287 ug/kg (PMID 28946925).

items.form_caveat: Kelp is the dangerous answer, and the danger is dosing variability rather than iodine itself. Across 12 species of commercially sold edible seaweed, iodine ranged from 16 ug/g in nori to over 8,165 ug/g in processed kelp granules from Laminaria digitata sold as a salt substitute, a 510-fold spread, and within a single species it varied with preharvest conditions (514 ug/g in sun-bleached blades, 6,571 ug/g in fresh juvenile blades) (PMID 15588380). One gram of those granules is 54 times the adult AI. A 2021 survey of 96 commercial macroalgae products found 128 to 62,400 ug of iodine per portion in wholefood kelp products and 5 to 5,600 ug per supplement dose, that for 54 of the 96 products a single serving or dose would exceed the tolerable upper intake level, and that species labelling and declared iodine content were frequently inadequate or inaccurate (PMID 33889064). A kelp tablet is therefore an unlabelled dose of a potent thyroid-active substance, and excess iodine causes both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism. If iodine is the goal, potassium iodide at a known 150 ug, or milk, fish and eggs, are the correct answers and kelp is not. Second, milk: iodine there comes from feed and dairy hygiene, so it moves with farming practice. Organic milk was 42.1 percent lower in iodine than conventional in a 172-sample UK retail survey (median 144.5 against 249.5 ng/g; PMID 21781365), and winter milk runs higher than summer. Someone switching to organic milk has quietly cut their main iodine source by nearly half without changing anything visible. Third, iodised salt: the USDA entry in the table is a US product, the UK has no iodisation programme, and that is precisely why the Bath group repeatedly identify milk, dairy and fish as the main UK iodine sources. Fourth, the plant drinks in the table are fortified products, with calcium and vitamin A, that skip iodine. That is the mechanism behind the 97.9 percent substitution loss rather than an absence of fortification technology.
items.bioavailability: Iodine bioavailability is the simple case. Iodide from milk, iodised salt and potassium iodide supplements is almost completely absorbed, and urinary iodine excretion is used directly as the intake biomarker on the standard assumption that about 90 percent of ingested iodine is excreted in urine (PMID 25274294). There is no meaningful absorption advantage to any form and no matrix effect worth chasing: 150 ug from a fillet of cod, a pot of yoghurt or a tablet are close to interchangeable systemically. The one real form difference sits at the top end. Organically bound iodine in seaweed is released variably during digestion and cooking, and boiling kelp leaches a large fraction of its iodine into the water, so a seaweed dose is uncertain in both directions. Two further practical points: iodine and selenium interact, because the deiodinase enzymes that convert thyroxine to the active hormone are selenoproteins, so iodine repletion in a selenium-poor person behaves differently; and goitrogens in raw brassicas and cassava compete with iodide uptake, which matters only when iodine intake is already marginal.

items.food_status_note: Two separate questions share a mineral name here, and they get different answers. Zinc the nutrient is abundant in ordinary food: oysters are the outlier of the entire composition table, red meat and offal follow, and wheat germ, seeds and legumes carry useful amounts, so on the question of whether the substance is in food the answer is RICH. Zinc lozenges are not a nutritional product: the trials used more than 75 mg/day of elemental zinc, most commonly 80 to 92 mg/day and in two trials 192 to 207 mg/day, delivered as slowly dissolving zinc acetate or gluconate lozenges taken roughly every two hours while awake (PMID 28515951), and the mechanism depends on free zinc ions released in the mouth and throat over 20 to 30 minutes in contact with the pharyngeal mucosa. Food zinc is swallowed and absorbed in the small intestine, so no amount of it reproduces the intended local effect, which is why dose_from_food is NO while food_status is RICH. Reference point used in the table: EFSA PRI 7.5 mg/d for adult women and 9.4 mg/d for adult men at a phytate intake of 300 mg/d (EFSA, Dietary Reference Values for nutrients Summary report, approved 4 December 2017, doi 10.2903/sp.efsa.2017.e15121, Tables 5 and 7; underlying opinion EFSA Journal 2014;12(10):3844).
items.dose_from_food_note: The lozenge dose fails on arithmetic and then fails again on route. Arithmetically, hitting the 80 mg/day of elemental zinc used in the trials (PMID 28515951) every day for the duration of a cold takes 204 g of raw oyster meat, roughly 14 to 15 medium oysters; or 102 g of cooked oysters; or 88 g of canned oysters, about 11 of them; or 479 g of toasted wheat-germ cereal; or 989 g of braised lean beef chuck; or 1.10 kg of braised lamb shoulder; or 1.05 kg of pumpkin seed kernels; or 5.23 kg of boiled chickpeas; or 6.30 kg of boiled lentils. Only oysters make it look even arithmetically plausible, and 14 raw oysters a day for a week is a Vibrio and norovirus decision rather than a nutrition one. Closing the arithmetic would still not reproduce the product, because the lozenge trials work through free Zn2+ released in the oropharynx and held against the mucosa, and swallowed zinc from food or from a capsule bypasses that route entirely. On scale, 80 to 92 mg/day is roughly 11 to 12 times the EFSA female PRI of 7.5 mg/d (10.7 and 12.3 times); the 'eight times' figure quoted earlier corresponds to the male PRI of 9.4 mg/d, not the female one named in the sentence. Separately, and this is the part food answers easily, the nutritional dose is trivially reachable: 85 g of braised lean beef chuck (6.9 mg) or 6 medium raw oysters (33.4 mg) meets or vastly exceeds the 7.5 to 9.4 mg PRI in one portion.

items.form_caveat: Zinc gluconate lozenges shortened colds by 28 percent and zinc acetate lozenges by 40 percent, a 12-point difference that was not statistically significant (95% CI -12 to +36), and there is no evidence that doses above 100 mg/day do better than 80 to 92 mg/day (PMID 28515951). The salt matters less than people claim and the lozenge format matters more. Zinc capsules, tablets, syrups and food are not substitutes in this indication, because the local contact is the point. Two safety notes follow from the numbers: 80 to 92 mg/day is roughly 11 to 12 times the EFSA female PRI and well above nutritional upper levels, defensible only for a few days because sustained high zinc antagonises copper absorption; and this is a short pharmacological course with an actual end date, unlike a nutrient. One earlier claim about the oyster records has to be withdrawn. Cooking does concentrate oyster zinc by moisture loss (raw 89.0 g water, cooked 78.2 g; dry matter 11.0 g against 21.8 g, so solids exactly double and zinc exactly doubles from 39.3 to 78.6 mg per 100 g). Canning does not work that way: canned oysters hold 85.1 g water and 14.9 g dry matter, only 1.35 times the raw solids, yet 2.3 times the zinc at 91.0 mg, which is 1.7 times richer per gram of solids (611 mg zinc per 100 g dry matter against 357 raw and 361 cooked). The canned entry reflects different material or different analyses rather than moisture loss. Per-100 g comparisons across preparation states remain misleading either way unless the yield is tracked.
items.bioavailability: Oysters are the outlier of the entire food composition table. At 39.3 mg/100 g raw and up to 91.0 mg/100 g canned they carry four to twelve times the zinc of red meat, which is itself the next best category, and they are why oysters answer every zinc question. Beyond oysters, absorption efficiency does most of the work and phytate is the variable. Human whole-body-retention studies of matched cereal meals found fractional zinc absorption of 26.8 percent from a rye bread meal containing 100 umol of phytic acid, falling to 8.4 percent from oatmeal porridge containing 600 umol, a threefold loss driven by phytate alone (PMID 2824731). Fractional absorption is not the whole story, and the earlier version of this section had the direction of the bread comparison backwards. A related study found that a lower absolute amount of zinc was absorbed from white bread than from the same amount of wholemeal bread, because wholemeal supplies more zinc and the phytate penalty on fractional absorption did not overturn that content advantage; white bread only won once both breads were enriched with zinc chloride. Adding milk products did improve zinc absorption from the wholemeal meal (PMID 7361691). Replacing 25 percent of the beef protein in a composite meal with defatted soy flour lowered both the zinc content and the zinc absorbed, while the same substitution in a chicken meal changed neither (PMID 6893252). EFSA builds phytate straight into the requirement: the adult male PRI rises from 9.4 mg/d at 300 mg phytate/day to 11.7, 14.0 and 16.3 mg/d at 600, 900 and 1,200 mg, and the female PRI from 7.5 to 9.3, 11.0 and 12.7 mg/d across the same range, ratios of 1.73 and 1.69. A high-legume, high-wholegrain diet therefore needs about 70 percent more zinc on the label to deliver the same absorbed zinc. On mitigations, the evidence is narrower than previously claimed: the cited review covers added Aspergillus niger phytase (12 iron studies, 5 zinc studies) and states that for zinc not enough information is available to determine optimal activities (PMID 24050000), so added phytase is supported while soaking, sprouting and sourdough fermentation need a fermentation-specific source. Animal protein and milk in the same meal do raise absorption, and vegetarians consequently sit at the top of the EFSA PRI range rather than the bottom (PMID 12936958).

The six added rows use conventional portion sizes rather than USDA measure-table entries, so their per-portion figures are derived and are flagged as such in place.

Corrected the dose scale: 80 to 92 mg/day is roughly 11 to 12 times the EFSA female PRI of 7.5 mg/d (10.7 and 12.3 times), not eight to twelve times. Eight times corresponds to the male PRI of 9.4 mg/d.

The previous version stated the opposite and was doing argumentative work.

Cooking concentrates oyster zinc by moisture loss (dry matter 11.0 to 21.8 g, zinc 39.3 to 78.6 mg), but canned oysters hold only 1.35 times the raw dry matter (14.9 g) against 2.3 times the zinc, giving 611 mg zinc per 100 g dry matter against 357 raw and 361 cooked. items.food_status_note: Selenium is genuinely abundant in ordinary food, and offal and marine fish carry it most reliably: braised pork kidney is 312 ug per 100 g, braised lamb kidney 219 ug, cooked yellowfin tuna 108 ug and braised lamb's liver 111 ug. Brazil nuts are the richest known food source at a USDA average of 1,920 ug/100 g, about 96 ug in a single 5 g kernel, which makes them the one food where a supplement dose is met by two nuts, and that is a hazard rather than a reassurance because their selenium is set by the soil the tree grew in and varies more than thirty-fold between Amazon regions. Reference points used in the table: EFSA AI 70 ug/d for adults, and the EFSA tolerable upper intake level of 255 ug/d for adult men and women including pregnancy and lactation, set from alopecia as the critical endpoint with a LOAEL of 330 ug/d taken from the SELECT trial and an uncertainty factor of 1.3 (EFSA Journal 2023;21(1):e07704, DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2023.7704; AI from EFSA, Dietary Reference Values for nutrients Summary report, doi 10.2903/sp.efsa.2017.e15121, Tables 5 and 7). The 200 ug/d dose comes from two landmark trials: selenised yeast in the Nutritional Prevention of Cancer trial and 200 ug/d L-selenomethionine in SELECT.
items.dose_from_food_note: There is almost no gap, and that is the finding. 200 ug/d is met by 2.1 average Brazil nuts (10 g), or 64 g of braised pork kidney, or 91 g of braised lamb kidney, or 185 g of cooked yellowfin tuna, or 180 g of braised lamb's liver, or 223 g of cooked blue mussels, or 243 g of simmered chicken liver, or 263 g of canned light tuna in oil, or 532 g of cooked cod, or 4 tins of sardines, or 13 eggs. Kidney and Brazil nuts overshoot in one normal portion: an 85 g portion of braised pork kidney is 265 ug, already 133 percent of the supplement dose and above the EFSA upper level on its own, and an 85 g portion of braised lamb kidney is 186 ug, 93 percent of the dose. Because the dose is so easy to reach, the useful calculation runs the other way. The EFSA AI is 70 ug/d and the EFSA upper level is 255 ug/d, a working margin of about 185 ug. A person on a 200 ug/d supplement plus an ordinary diet is at roughly 270 ug and already over the upper level; add two average Brazil nuts and they are at about 462 ug. The UL derives from alopecia observed in SELECT at a LOAEL of 330 ug/d, so this is an observed human effect at achievable intakes rather than a theoretical ceiling (DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2023.7704). Selenium is the case where food easily matches the supplement, and the honest advice is to pick one route.

items.form_caveat: Brazil nuts are the textbook answer and a genuinely bad way to dose selenium deliberately, because the dose is unknowable at the point of eating. Median selenium varied from 2.07 mg/kg in Mato Grosso state to 68.15 mg/kg in Amazonas, which the authors attribute to soil selenium, soil pH and texture, location and genotype (PMID 28923728). On the 5 g kernel used throughout this item's table, one nut therefore supplies about 15 percent to about 490 percent of the 70 ug adult AI. The paper's own '11 percent to 288 percent' phrasing implies a 3.0 to 3.7 g kernel and cannot stand alongside a 5 g table, so the figures have been put on one basis. Nuts from the two extremes are visually identical, are not labelled by state of origin, and are routinely blended, so 'two Brazil nuts a day' is a dose ranging from about 20 ug to about 680 ug depending on a fact the eater cannot access, spanning deficient to well over the upper level. On form equivalence, selenium is unusual in a helpful way: the dominant species in Brazil nuts and cereals is selenomethionine, the same species used as the supplement in SELECT, so food and that supplement are pharmacologically comparable (PMID 18346307). But 200 ug of selenium is not one thing. The selenised yeast used in the earlier NPC trial was a poorly speciated mixture whose delivered selenium was variable, and the two trials produced opposite results, so the number 200 ug carries no single meaning across the literature (PMID 18346308, PMID 18346307). Finally, the case for supplementing collapses in a selenium-replete person: SELECT tested 200 ug/d L-selenomethionine in selenium-replete men, found no protection against prostate or other major cancers, and produced the alopecia signal that now defines the UL.
items.bioavailability: Selenium bioavailability depends on chemical species more than on food matrix. Selenomethionine, the form in Brazil nuts, cereals and meat, is absorbed almost completely and is incorporated non-specifically into body proteins as a storage pool, which is why it raises plasma selenium readily and why its kinetics differ from inorganic selenite and selenate (PMID 18346307, PMID 28412747). That has a practical consequence the composition tables hide: the selenium content of any plant food is a proxy for the soil it grew in rather than a property of the species. The USDA wholemeal bread figure of 25.7 ug/100 g and the wheat germ figure of 79.2 ug/100 g both reflect North American wheat grown on selenium-rich soils. European and UK wheat grows on selenium-poor soils, so the same bread and the same wheat germ cannot be assumed to deliver the same selenium, and the wide between-country variation in intake driven by exactly this mechanism is the central theme of the food-chain intake review (PMID 18346308). Animal foods hold their values better across countries, because livestock feed is commonly selenium-supplemented, which is why kidney, liver, tuna, mussels and eggs travel better than bread or nuts do. Ranking for a reader who wants reliable selenium without a variable dose: kidney and liver first, then marine fish and shellfish including canned tuna and mussels, eggs as a steady background contributor, and Brazil nuts last precisely because they are the richest source.
items.data_confidence: HIGH. Every original per-100 g figure matched FoodData Central to the digit (312, 1,920, 108, 111, 37.6, 52.7, 36.1, 31.1, 25.7, 19.7), the Brazil nut state medians were confirmed verbatim from PMID 28923728, and the EFSA UL derivation was confirmed word for word: alopecia as critical endpoint, LOAEL 330 ug/d from SELECT, uncertainty factor 1.3, UL 255 ug/d including pregnancy and lactation. EFSA itself notes that consumers are unlikely to exceed the UL except regular users of food supplements or regular consumers of Brazil nuts. The seven added rows use conventional portion sizes rather than USDA measure-table entries, so their per-portion figures are derived and flagged in place.

items.food_status_note_zh: 铁在普通食物中确实丰富，并以两种化学性质不同、吸收表现也不同的形式存在。血红素铁（内脏、红肉、贝类、血肠）由专门的转运体吸收，基本不受同一餐其他食物影响；非血红素铁（豆类、种子、绿叶菜、强化面粉）构成多数人摄入量的主体，吸收率只有前者的一小部分，并明显受维生素 C、多酚、植酸和钙的影响。血红素铁占生瘦牛肉总铁的 77%，羊肉 81%，猪肉 88%，鸡肉 74%（PMID 26433293），高于较早的 Monsen 方程所假定的 40%；这些比例是在生瘦肉中测得的，因此炖煮产品中血红素铁的占比很可能略低于下文计算所暗示的水平。表中使用的参考值：EFSA PRI 绝经前女性 16 mg/d，男性 11 mg/d（EFSA，Dietary Reference Values for nutrients Summary report，2017 年 12 月 4 日通过，doi 10.2903/sp.efsa.2017.e15121，表 5 和表 7；基础意见书 EFSA Journal 2015;13(10):4254）。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 两种补充剂剂量需要两个答案。营养剂量（14 至 18 mg 元素铁，欧盟标签参考量）靠吃就能轻松达到：1 杯煮扁豆（6.6 mg）加 85 g 炖羊肝（7.0 mg）加 1 oz 南瓜子（2.3 mg），一天合计 15.9 mg；单独一份 85 g 炖猪肝本身就有 15.2 mg。治疗剂量则达不到。吸收和治疗试验给的是以硫酸亚铁形式标示的 60 mg 和 120 mg 元素铁，65 mg 铁对应的盐重约为 325 mg（PMID 29032957）。若按总含量匹配 65 mg 铁，一天大约需要 363 g 炖猪肝、785 g 羊肝、3.3 kg 西冷牛排、1.95 kg（约 10 杯）煮扁豆，或 2.4 kg（约 80 杯）生菠菜。若按吸收铁计算，食物负担约为原稿所称的 1.6 倍，因为它引用的那项试验测得，在 60 mg/d 下连续每日给药的累积分数吸收率为 16.3%，隔日给药为 21.8%，单次 120 mg 剂量为 11.8%，原稿假定的 10% 低于这些实测值。按该来源自己的 16.3% 计算，65 mg 剂量提供约 10.6 mg 吸收铁。以 25% 的吸收率通过血红素铁吸收 10.6 mg，需要 42.4 mg 血红素铁，约合 1.94 kg 炖瘦羊肩肉（每 100 g 总铁 2.7 mg，生瘦肉中 81% 为血红素铁；FDC 174331 与 PMID 26433293）。以 5% 的吸收率从非血红素食物吸收同样的 10.6 mg，需要 212 mg 非血红素铁，约合每天 6.4 kg 熟扁豆。已确诊的缺铁无法靠食物纠正，预防缺铁可以。
items.form_caveat_zh: 三个陷阱，其中第一个的适用范围比通常所说的更窄。(1) 视黄醇危害属于肝脏，并不适用于内脏这一整类。炖羊肝每 100 g 含 7,490 ug 视黄醇活性当量，85 g 一份即 6,367 ug；炖牛肝每 100 g 含 9,440 ug RAE（生牛肝 4,970 ug RAE；FDC 172532、168626、169451）。这正是多数国家指南在孕期禁食肝脏的原因。危害按器官清晰分开：炖羊肾每 100 g 含铁 12.4 mg、视黄醇 137 ug RAE（FDC 174355），炖猪肾含铁 5.29 mg、78 ug RAE（FDC 167860），所以肾脏在含铁量上胜过表中所有肌肉肉类，同时没有维生素 A 问题。此前关于铁的益处与维生素 A 危害必然同行、无法分开的说法予以撤回。(2) 肝脏中的铁大部分是铁蛋白铁和血铁黄素铁，因此 8.28 mg 这个表面数值的可吸收性低于普通肌肉肉中血红素铁比例所暗示的水平，数字更小的肌肉肉反而能提供更多吸收铁。(3) 补充剂铁的行为与食物铁不同：60 mg 的剂量会升高铁调素并抑制下一次剂量的吸收，这就是隔日给药吸收 21.8%、而连续每日给药为 16.3% 的原因（PMID 29032957）。食物铁在一天之内小量陆续到达，从不触发这一机制。关于菠菜，纠正是双向的。同位素研究发现，向低草酸的羽衣甘蓝餐中加入草酸钾并未改变非血红素铁吸收（11.5% 对 10.7%，P=0.86），教科书式的草酸解释经不起检验。但同一研究中菠菜餐的吸收比配对的羽衣甘蓝餐低 24%，未达显著（P>0.16）；论文虽报告菠菜的钙和多酚显著更高，却没有把吸收差异归因于它们。诚实的解读是：在一项小样本研究中菠菜铁的吸收数值偏低，草酸机制已被否定，替代机制尚未确立。无论如何，一碗 30 g 生菠菜叶含铁 0.81 mg，得到的只是一个舍入误差。
items.bioavailability_zh: 血红素铁的吸收率大约为 15% 至 35%，非血红素铁为 2% 至 20%，铁营养状况是主导变量。若看整体膳食而非单餐，无铁储备者混合膳食的生物利用度为 14% 至 18%，素食膳食为 5% 至 12%，作者指出铁营养状况的影响通常大于膳食组成（PMID 20200263）。维生素 C：该来源的结论是每一主餐中约 50 mg 抗坏血酸有利于取得最佳效果，在植酸、鞣质等抑制性配体含量高的餐食中效果最明显（PMID 3700141）。此前声称的 25 mg 下限和数倍增幅并不见于该来源，已删除。当同样剂量的抗坏血酸在数天内随完整膳食给予时，促进作用要弱得多（PMID 11124756）：在扁豆上挤点柠檬有帮助，但不会把植物铁变成肉类铁。茶与咖啡的抑制作用，附上数字：一杯咖啡使汉堡餐的非血红素铁吸收下降 39%，茶下降 64%；双倍浓度的速溶咖啡把吸收率从 5.88% 压到 0.53%；餐前 1 小时喝咖啡无害，餐后 1 小时喝咖啡的抑制程度与随餐喝相当（PMID 6402915）。红茶使非血红素铁吸收降低 79% 至 94%，薄荷茶 84%，可可 71%，洋甘菊 47%，抑制程度随总多酚量呈剂量依赖，加奶没有区别（PMID 10999016）。这是多酚的抑制作用；植酸是另一种抑制因素，本身就存在于全谷物和豆类之中。实际后果：对铁储备偏低的人，收益最高的单一改变是把茶和咖啡移到两餐之间，避免随餐或餐后饮用。
items.data_confidence_zh: 高。从原稿沿用的每一个每 100 g 数值在独立检索时都与 FoodData Central 逐位一致，所引用的全部 PMID 和 DOI 都能查到对应论文，内容与引用说法相符。两处置信度较低的地方已在相应行标出：血肠条目是美国替代数据，其英国对应值无法确认；新增的十一行使用常规份量而非 USDA 自己的计量表，因此其每份数值是推算的，并非表中列出的。

items.food_status_note_zh: 碘存在于普通食物中，答案落在一小组食物上：乳制品、白肉鱼、蛋、贝类，以及在实行食盐加碘的国家里的食用盐。其他食物的贡献都不明显。RICH（丰富）这一分类带有辖区限定：对英国读者而言，它只依靠乳制品、白肉鱼和蛋，因为英国没有食盐加碘计划，所以下表中的美国加碘盐一行不可套用，并已如此标注。牛奶中的碘来自强化饲料和碘伏乳头消毒剂，并非奶牛自身产生，这也是它随季节波动（冬季圈养期更高）以及有机牛奶含量更低的原因。表中使用的参考值：EFSA AI 成人 150 ug/d，孕期和哺乳期 200 ug/d（EFSA，Dietary Reference Values for nutrients Summary report，2017 年 12 月 4 日通过，doi 10.2903/sp.efsa.2017.e15121，表 5 和表 7；基础意见书 EFSA Journal 2014;12(5):3660）。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 基本上没有缺口。标准的碘补充剂或孕期复合维生素提供 150 ug，正好等于 EFSA 成人 AI。单块 120 g 的英国黑线鳕鱼柳提供 390 ug，是该剂量的两倍半。一块 115 g 鳕鱼柳提供 131 ug。约 400 ml 牛奶按牛奶密度（412 g）计算提供约 156 ug；此前引用的 151 ug 是 1.6 个 USDA 杯（398 g）的量，两者不应等同。六个大号鸡蛋提供 147 ug。在实行加碘的地区，半茶匙加碘盐（3 g）提供 152 ug。碘属于正常饮食者不需要补充的那一小类。一旦这些特定食物离开饮食，缺口立刻出现，英国的数据很直白。把一天三份乳制品（牛奶、酸奶、奶酪）换成植物替代品，这些份量提供的碘从 124 ug 降到 2.6 ug，损失 97.9%，对 150 ug 推荐量的贡献从 83% 降到 1.8%（PMID 35373723）。同一项市场调查识别出 146 种牛奶替代品和 76 种酸奶替代品，排除了 48 种有机产品，发现 29 种牛奶替代品和 4 种酸奶替代品做了碘强化；这相当于非有机子集的 28% 和 6%，或全部已识别产品的 19.9% 和 5.3%。此前按全部分母引用的 28% 和 6% 是错的。相比之下，88% 和 73% 做了钙强化；没有任何奶酪替代品和鱼类替代品做碘强化；有机植物替代品在法律上不能强化。这在真实人群中有体现：在 NDNS 第 7 至 9 年，只饮用植物奶的成人和儿童碘摄入量为 94 ug/d，饮用牛奶者为 129 ug/d，尿碘浓度中位数分别为 79 ug/l 和 132 ug/l，按 WHO 标准前一组属于碘缺乏，而牛奶饮用者充足（PMID 32993817）。未强化植物饮品的碘浓度中位数为 7.3 ug/kg，只有冬季常规牛奶的 1.7%；2015 年发现的三种强化产品在 266 至 287 ug/kg 之间（PMID 28946925）。
items.form_caveat_zh: 海带是那个危险的答案，危险之处在于剂量的不可预期，碘本身并非问题。在 12 种商售可食海藻中，碘含量从海苔的 16 ug/g 到作为盐替代品出售的指状海带（Laminaria digitata）加工海带颗粒的 8,165 ug/g 以上，相差 510 倍；同一物种内部也随采收前条件而变（日晒漂白的叶片 514 ug/g，新鲜幼叶 6,571 ug/g）（PMID 15588380）。一克这种颗粒相当于成人 AI 的 54 倍。2021 年对 96 种商售大型藻类产品的调查发现，整食型海带产品每份含碘 128 至 62,400 ug，补充剂每次剂量 5 至 5,600 ug；96 种产品中有 54 种，一次食用或一次剂量就会超过可耐受最高摄入量；物种标注和申报的碘含量常常不充分或不准确（PMID 33889064）。因此一片海带片剂就是一剂未标明用量的强效甲状腺活性物质，而碘过量既可导致甲减也可导致甲亢。若目标是补碘，正确答案是剂量已知为 150 ug 的碘化钾，或牛奶、鱼和蛋，海带不在其中。其次是牛奶：其中的碘来自饲料和乳品卫生措施，因此会随养殖方式变化。在一项 172 份英国零售样品的调查中，有机牛奶的碘含量比常规牛奶低 42.1%（中位数 144.5 对 249.5 ng/g；PMID 21781365），冬季牛奶高于夏季。换成有机牛奶的人，在没有任何可见改变的情况下已经把主要碘来源砍掉近一半。第三是加碘盐：表中的 USDA 条目是美国产品，英国没有加碘计划，这正是 Bath 研究组反复把牛奶、乳制品和鱼列为英国主要碘来源的原因。第四，表中的植物饮品是强化产品，强化了钙和维生素 A，却跳过了碘。这就是 97.9% 替代损失背后的机制，问题并不在于缺少强化技术。
items.bioavailability_zh: 碘的生物利用度属于简单情形。来自牛奶、加碘盐和碘化钾补充剂的碘化物几乎完全被吸收，尿碘排出量被直接用作摄入量的生物标志物，其标准假设是摄入碘约 90% 经尿排出（PMID 25274294）。任何形式都没有值得追求的吸收优势，也没有值得计较的基质效应：来自一块鳕鱼柳、一小杯酸奶或一片药片的 150 ug，在体内几乎可以互换。唯一真实的形式差异出现在高端。海藻中有机结合的碘在消化和烹调过程中的释放量不稳定，煮海带会把其中很大一部分碘浸出到水里，因此海藻的剂量在两个方向上都不确定。另有两个实用要点：碘和硒相互作用，因为把甲状腺素转化为活性激素的脱碘酶属于硒蛋白，所以硒不足的人补碘的表现会不同；生十字花科蔬菜和木薯中的致甲状腺肿物质会与碘化物摄取竞争，这只在碘摄入本已处于边缘水平时才重要。
items.data_confidence_zh: 高，就该条目的核心而言。所有 USDA 数值与 FoodData Central 逐位一致，Bath 研究组和 Nicol 的 PMID 均经逐字核实，包括 97.9% 的损失、NDNS 中 94 对 129 ug/d 的摄入量、79 对 132 ug/l 的尿碘浓度、438 和 324 ug/kg 的牛奶中位数以及 42.1% 的有机牛奶差距。两行较弱并已就地标注：黑线鳕和挪威海螯虾的数值来自一份英国二次汇编表（BDA Iodine Food Fact Sheet），而非一手分析，只作参考。

items.food_status_note_zh: 这里有两个不同的问题共用一个矿物名称，它们得到不同的答案。作为营养素的锌在普通食物中很丰富：牡蛎是整张成分表的极端值，红肉和内脏其次，小麦胚芽、种子和豆类也提供可用的量，所以就这种物质是否存在于食物中而言，答案是 RICH。锌含片并非营养产品：试验使用的是每天超过 75 mg 元素锌，最常见为每天 80 至 92 mg，两项试验为每天 192 至 207 mg，以缓慢溶解的醋酸锌或葡萄糖酸锌含片给药，清醒时约每两小时一次（PMID 28515951），其机制依赖在口腔和咽部释放的游离锌离子在 20 至 30 分钟内与咽部黏膜保持接触。食物中的锌被吞下并在小肠吸收，任何量都无法复制这种预期的局部作用，这就是 dose_from_food 为 NO 而 food_status 为 RICH 的原因。表中使用的参考值：在植酸摄入 300 mg/d 的条件下，EFSA PRI 成年女性 7.5 mg/d、成年男性 9.4 mg/d（EFSA，Dietary Reference Values for nutrients Summary report，2017 年 12 月 4 日通过，doi 10.2903/sp.efsa.2017.e15121，表 5 和表 7；基础意见书 EFSA Journal 2014;12(10):3844）。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 含片剂量先在算术上不成立，接着在给药途径上再次不成立。就算术而言，要在感冒期间每天达到试验所用的 80 mg 元素锌（PMID 28515951），需要 204 g 生牡蛎肉，约 14 至 15 个中等大小牡蛎；或 102 g 熟牡蛎；或 88 g 罐装牡蛎，约 11 个；或 479 g 焙烤小麦胚芽谷物；或 989 g 炖瘦牛肩肉；或 1.10 kg 炖羊肩肉；或 1.05 kg 南瓜子仁；或 5.23 kg 煮鹰嘴豆；或 6.30 kg 煮扁豆。只有牡蛎在算术上看起来还有些可能，而连续一周每天吃 14 个生牡蛎，要权衡的是弧菌和诺如病毒的风险，与营养无关。即便把算术凑齐，也复制不出这个产品，因为含片试验的作用依赖在口咽部释放并停留在黏膜上的游离 Zn2+，而来自食物或胶囊的锌被吞下后完全绕过这条途径。在量级上，每天 80 至 92 mg 约为 EFSA 女性 PRI 7.5 mg/d 的 11 至 12 倍（10.7 倍和 12.3 倍）；此前引用的八倍对应的是男性 PRI 9.4 mg/d，并非句中提到的女性值。另外一点是食物能轻松回答的：营养剂量非常容易达到，85 g 炖瘦牛肩肉（6.9 mg）或 6 个中等大小生牡蛎（33.4 mg），一份就达到或远超 7.5 至 9.4 mg 的 PRI。
items.form_caveat_zh: 葡萄糖酸锌含片使感冒病程缩短 28%，醋酸锌含片缩短 40%，两者相差 12 个百分点，未达统计显著（95% CI -12 至 +36）；也没有证据表明每天超过 100 mg 的剂量优于 80 至 92 mg（PMID 28515951）。盐型的重要性低于人们所说，含片这一剂型的重要性更高。在这一适应症下，锌胶囊、片剂、糖浆和食物都不能替代含片，局部接触才是关键。从这些数字引出两条安全提示：每天 80 至 92 mg 约为 EFSA 女性 PRI 的 11 至 12 倍，远高于营养性上限，只有在数天之内才站得住脚，因为长期高锌会拮抗铜的吸收；这是一个有明确终点的短期药理疗程，与长期摄入的营养素不同。此前关于牡蛎数据条目的一个说法必须撤回。烹熟确实通过失水提高了牡蛎的锌浓度（生品含水 89.0 g，熟品 78.2 g；干物质 11.0 g 对 21.8 g，固形物正好翻倍，锌也正好从每 100 g 39.3 mg 翻倍到 78.6 mg）。罐装不是这样：罐装牡蛎含水 85.1 g、干物质 14.9 g，只有生品固形物的 1.35 倍，锌却是 2.3 倍，达到 91.0 mg，按固形物计算浓 1.7 倍（每 100 g 干物质含锌 611 mg，生品 357 mg，熟品 361 mg）。罐装条目反映的是不同原料或不同分析，与失水无关。无论哪种情形，除非同时追踪出品率，跨加工状态的每 100 g 比较仍然会误导。
items.bioavailability_zh: 牡蛎是整张食物成分表的极端值。生品每 100 g 39.3 mg，罐装最高每 100 g 91.0 mg，是红肉的四到十二倍，而红肉本身已是次优类别，这也是牡蛎能回答所有锌相关问题的原因。牡蛎之外，吸收效率承担了大部分工作，植酸是那个变量。对配对谷物餐的人体全身滞留研究发现，含 100 umol 植酸的黑麦面包餐锌分数吸收率为 26.8%，含 600 umol 的燕麦粥降到 8.4%，仅由植酸造成三倍的差距（PMID 2824731）。分数吸收率不是全部，本节此前的版本把面包比较的方向弄反了。一项相关研究发现，从白面包吸收的锌绝对量低于同等量的全麦面包，因为全麦提供更多锌，植酸对分数吸收率的惩罚没有抵消这一含量优势；只有当两种面包都用氯化锌强化后，白面包才占优。在全麦餐中加入乳制品确实改善了锌的吸收（PMID 7361691）。在一份复合餐中用脱脂大豆粉替代 25% 的牛肉蛋白，锌含量和吸收的锌都下降，而在鸡肉餐中做同样替代则两者都没有变化（PMID 6893252）。EFSA 把植酸直接纳入需要量：成年男性 PRI 从植酸 300 mg/d 时的 9.4 mg/d，在 600、900 和 1,200 mg 时升至 11.7、14.0 和 16.3 mg/d；女性 PRI 在同一区间从 7.5 升至 9.3、11.0 和 12.7 mg/d，比值分别为 1.73 和 1.69。因此高豆类、高全谷物的膳食需要标签上多出约 70% 的锌，才能提供同样的吸收锌。关于缓解措施，证据比此前所称更窄：所引综述涵盖的是添加黑曲霉（Aspergillus niger）植酸酶（12 项铁研究、5 项锌研究），并指出就锌而言现有信息不足以确定最佳酶活（PMID 24050000），所以添加植酸酶有支持，而浸泡、发芽和酸面团发酵需要专门针对发酵的来源。同餐中的动物蛋白和牛奶确实提高吸收，素食者因此落在 EFSA PRI 区间的上端（PMID 12936958）。
items.data_confidence_zh: 高。原稿全部十一个每 100 g 数值都与 FoodData Central 逐位核实一致，Hemila 的含片荟萃分析在每一项参数上都得到确认（剂量阈值、每天 80 至 92 mg 和 192 至 207 mg 两个区间、按盐型 40% 对 28%、每天超过 100 mg 无额外益处），EFSA 按植酸分级的 PRI 表与来源文本一致。新增的六行使用常规份量而非 USDA 计量表条目，因此其每份数值是推算的，并已就地标注。

items.food_status_note_zh: 硒在普通食物中确实丰富，内脏和海鱼提供得最稳定：炖猪肾每 100 g 含 312 ug，炖羊肾 219 ug，熟黄鳍金枪鱼 108 ug，炖羊肝 111 ug。巴西坚果是已知最富硒的食物，USDA 平均值为每 100 g 1,920 ug，单个 5 g 果仁约 96 ug，这使它成为唯一两颗就能达到补充剂剂量的食物，而这一点值得警惕，谈不上让人放心，因为其硒含量由树木生长的土壤决定，在亚马逊各地区之间相差三十多倍。表中使用的参考值：EFSA 成人 AI 70 ug/d；EFSA 可耐受最高摄入量为成年男性和女性 255 ug/d，包括孕期和哺乳期，以脱发为关键终点，取自 SELECT 试验的 LOAEL 330 ug/d 并使用 1.3 的不确定系数（EFSA Journal 2023;21(1):e07704，DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2023.7704；AI 来自 EFSA，Dietary Reference Values for nutrients Summary report，doi 10.2903/sp.efsa.2017.e15121，表 5 和表 7）。200 ug/d 这一剂量来自两项标志性试验：Nutritional Prevention of Cancer 试验中的富硒酵母，以及 SELECT 中的 200 ug/d L-硒代甲硫氨酸。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 几乎没有缺口，这本身就是结论。200 ug/d 可由 2.1 颗平均水平的巴西坚果（10 g）达到，或 64 g 炖猪肾、91 g 炖羊肾、185 g 熟黄鳍金枪鱼、180 g 炖羊肝、223 g 熟蓝贻贝、243 g 文火煮鸡肝、263 g 油浸罐装淡金枪鱼、532 g 熟鳕鱼、4 罐沙丁鱼，或 13 个鸡蛋。肾脏和巴西坚果在一份正常份量里就会超出：85 g 一份炖猪肾含 265 ug，已是补充剂剂量的 133%，单独就超过 EFSA 上限；85 g 一份炖羊肾含 186 ug，为该剂量的 93%。由于这个剂量太容易达到，有用的计算要反过来做。EFSA AI 为 70 ug/d，EFSA 上限为 255 ug/d，可用余量约 185 ug。一个每天服用 200 ug 补充剂并保持普通饮食的人，大约在 270 ug，已经超过上限；再加两颗平均水平的巴西坚果，就到约 462 ug。该上限源自 SELECT 中在 LOAEL 330 ug/d 观察到的脱发，这是在可达到的摄入量下观察到的人体效应，并非理论推算的天花板（DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2023.7704）。硒是食物可以轻松匹配补充剂的例子，诚实的建议是两条路只选一条。
items.form_caveat_zh: 巴西坚果是教科书答案，也确实是刻意补硒的糟糕方式，因为吃下去的那一刻剂量无从知道。硒的中位数从马托格罗索州的 2.07 mg/kg 到亚马逊州的 68.15 mg/kg，作者将其归因于土壤硒、土壤 pH 与质地、地点和基因型（PMID 28923728）。按本条目表中通用的 5 g 果仁计算，一颗坚果因此提供成人 AI 70 ug 的约 15% 到约 490%。论文自己的 11% 至 288% 的表述隐含的是 3.0 至 3.7 g 的果仁，无法与 5 g 的表格并存，因此这些数字已统一到同一基准。两个极端产地的坚果外观完全相同，不按产州标注，并且常规混装，所以每天两颗巴西坚果对应的剂量在约 20 ug 到约 680 ug 之间，取决于食用者无法获知的事实，横跨从缺乏到远超上限的范围。在形式等效性上，硒有一点很有帮助：巴西坚果和谷物中的主要形态是硒代甲硫氨酸，与 SELECT 使用的补充剂形态相同，因此食物与该补充剂在药理上可比（PMID 18346307）。但 200 ug 硒并不是一件事。更早的 NPC 试验使用的富硒酵母是形态不明确的混合物，实际提供的硒含量不稳定，而两项试验得出相反结果，所以 200 ug 这个数字在整个文献里没有单一含义（PMID 18346308，PMID 18346307）。最后，对硒充足的人来说，补充的理由完全崩塌：SELECT 在硒充足的男性中测试了 200 ug/d L-硒代甲硫氨酸，未发现对前列腺癌或其他主要癌症的保护作用，并产生了如今界定 UL 的脱发信号。
items.bioavailability_zh: 硒的生物利用度主要取决于化学形态，食物基质的影响较小。硒代甲硫氨酸是巴西坚果、谷物和肉类中的形态，几乎完全被吸收，并以非特异方式掺入体内蛋白作为储存池，这就是它容易提高血浆硒、而其动力学又与无机的亚硒酸盐和硒酸盐不同的原因（PMID 18346307，PMID 28412747）。这带来一个成分表掩盖了的实际后果：任何植物性食物的硒含量都是其生长土壤的代理指标，物种本身的属性并不决定它。USDA 全麦面包 25.7 ug/100 g 和小麦胚芽 79.2 ug/100 g 这两个数值都来自生长在富硒土壤上的北美小麦。欧洲和英国的小麦长在贫硒土壤上，所以不能假定同样的面包和同样的小麦胚芽能提供同样的硒，各国摄入量差异巨大正是由这一机制驱动，也是那篇食物链摄入综述的核心主题（PMID 18346308）。动物性食物的数值跨国稳定得多，因为畜禽饲料通常补硒，这也是肾、肝、金枪鱼、贻贝和蛋比面包或坚果更经得起地域迁移的原因。对想要稳定补硒又不愿面对波动剂量的读者，排序是：肾和肝居首，其次是海鱼和贝类，包括罐装金枪鱼和贻贝，蛋作为稳定的背景来源，巴西坚果排在最后，恰恰因为它是最富硒的来源。
items.data_confidence_zh: 高。原稿每一个每 100 g 数值都与 FoodData Central 逐位一致（312、1,920、108、111、37.6、52.7、36.1、31.1、25.7、19.7），巴西坚果各州中位数已从 PMID 28923728 逐字确认，EFSA UL 的推导也逐字确认：脱发为关键终点，来自 SELECT 的 LOAEL 330 ug/d，不确定系数 1.3，UL 255 ug/d，包括孕期和哺乳期。EFSA 自己指出，除了经常使用食品补充剂或经常食用巴西坚果的人，消费者不太可能超过 UL。新增的七行使用常规份量而非 USDA 计量表条目，因此其每份数值是推算的，并已就地标注。

items.food_status_note: Magnesium sits in the chlorophyll molecule and in the outer layers of seeds and grains, so every unrefined plant food carries some; nuts, seeds, cocoa, wholegrains, legumes and dark leafy greens are all meaningful contributors, and a mixed diet built on them reaches the adult RDA (420 mg/day men 31+, 320 mg/day women 31+, Institute of Medicine 1997) with no supplement. Refining is what strips it, and the honest like-for-like comparison is CoFID wholemeal bread at 66 mg/100 g against white bread at 22 mg/100 g (11-981 and 11-1145), a three-fold gap. The wheat bran figure of 389 mg/100 g (CoFID 11-906) is a dry milling fraction, so setting it against a roughly 40%-water baked loaf inflates the effect of refining to eighteen-fold and should not be used that way.
items.dose_from_food_note: Supplements are sold at 200 to 400 mg elemental magnesium, which is the whole daily requirement, and ordinary food covers that range easily. A worked day: 1 oz pumpkin seeds (156 mg) plus 1 cup cooked black beans (120 mg) plus 1 oz 70-85% dark chocolate (65 mg) is 341 mg before anything else on the plate is counted. Single-food routes are absurd by comparison: 400 mg from dark chocolate alone means 175 g of bar, roughly 1,000 kcal, and 400 mg from wholemeal bread alone means 533 g, about 17 slices. Nobody needs a single-food route, because the mixed-diet route is three normal portions. The safety asymmetry matters more than the arithmetic: the Institute of Medicine set the 350 mg/day upper limit for supplemental magnesium only, and it explicitly excludes magnesium naturally present in food and water, so 700 mg of magnesium from seeds and beans carries no upper limit while 400 mg from tablets is already over the supplemental ceiling. A comparable 250 mg/day EU limit for magnesium added through supplements or fortified foods is normally attributed to the SCF 2001 opinion; the source text could not be retrieved during verification, so that figure is carried here as indicative and unconfirmed.

items.form_caveat: The difference is dose kinetics rather than chemistry. Food delivers magnesium in small amounts across a day inside a matrix that slows release, so the unabsorbed fraction stays small and osmotic diarrhoea does not happen. A 400 mg bolus of a soluble magnesium salt leaves a large unabsorbed load in the gut lumen, and that load is the mechanism of the laxative effect that set the upper limit in the first place. Magnesium citrate and magnesium hydroxide are marketed as laxatives at doses close to supplement doses. In anyone with reduced renal clearance (CKD stage 4-5, elderly patients on multiple drugs) supplements can cause symptomatic hypermagnesaemia, while food magnesium is handled by renal excretion across the normal intake range. There is no situation where the food form is the risky one.
items.bioavailability: Net absorption of dietary magnesium is 40 to 60% at an intake averaging 380 mg/day, falling to 15-36% at higher daily intakes of 550 to 850 mg (Institute of Medicine DRI report 1997, Chapter 6, NCBI Bookshelf NBK109816). NIH ODS quotes 30-40% for public guidance, so the working figure should be the lower half of the DRI range rather than the 50% midpoint. Phytate is the main food inhibitor and can cut fractional absorption by up to 60% in a dose-dependent way, so the magnesium in bran, seeds and legumes is not fully realised. Oxalate matters much less than the textbook version implies: Bohn et al. (Br J Nutr 2004;91:601-606) measured 26.7% fractional absorption from a spinach meal against 36.5% from kale and concluded the spinach penalty is at least partly counterbalanced by its higher native magnesium content, so a cooked cup of spinach delivers roughly 42 mg absorbed against roughly 11 mg from a cooked cup of kale. Supplement forms differ sharply among themselves: Firoz and Graber (Magnesium Research 2001;14(4):257-262, PMID 11794633) measured fractional absorption of about 4% for magnesium oxide against 9-11% for the lactate, aspartate and chloride forms, and magnesium oxide is the cheapest and most widely sold form. A 400 mg magnesium oxide tablet can therefore deliver less absorbed magnesium than a handful of pumpkin seeds while producing the loose stools.
items.data_confidence: HIGH for composition and arithmetic: verification checked every cited FDC ID against the USDA SR Legacy April 2018 dataset and every CoFID code against CoFID 2021, and found no fabricated identifier, no wrong per-100 g value and no wrong portion weight, with all per-portion multiplications reproducing. Two lower-confidence pockets are flagged in place: the mineral water row carries no sourced figure at all, and the flaxseed, wheat germ, wheat bran and cocoa portion weights are conventions rather than dataset portions. The EU SCF 250 mg/day added-magnesium limit is consistent with the standard figure but was not confirmable from the source text.
corrections_applied: Reversed the spinach magnesium write-down. The original called it nominal-only on oxalate grounds; Bohn 2004 gives spinach 26.7% against kale 36.5% and concludes the penalty is partly offset by spinach's higher native content, so absorbed magnesium is about 42 mg per cooked cup against about 11 mg for kale. Spinach now ranks first and the warning language is removed from both the food row and the bioavailability text.

Replaced 'net absorption about 50%' with the source's own '40 to 60 percent at an intake averaging 380 mg/day', and added the NIH ODS 30-40% public-guidance figure, per the IMPRECISE finding on NBK109816.

Replaced the wheat bran (389 mg/100 g) versus white bread (22 mg/100 g) refining comparison with the like-for-like CoFID pair wholemeal 66 versus white 22, a three-fold gap, because the bran figure is a dry milling fraction being compared against a roughly 40%-water baked good.

Flagged the EU Scientific Committee on Food 250 mg/day limit for added magnesium as indicative and unconfirmed (UNVERIFIABLE in the verification pass; body text of the EFSA compilation not machine-readable).

Added the missing rich sources named in verification, each in rank order: melon seeds 510 mg/100 g (CoFID 14-826), sunflower seed kernels 325 mg/100 g (FDC 170562, CoFID 14-845 390), pine nuts 270 mg/100 g (CoFID 14-839), flaxseed 392 mg/100 g (FDC 169414), wheat bran (CoFID 389, USDA crude 611), wheat germ 239 mg/100 g (FDC 168892), and mineral/hard water.

items.supplement: Calcium supplements on top of an adequate diet
items.food_status_note: Calcium is among the easiest nutrients to get from ordinary food. Dairy, calcium-set tofu, hard cheeses, tinned fish eaten with the bones, whole small fish, fortified plant milks and fortified juice each deliver 200 to 860 mg per normal portion, and low-oxalate brassicas add 150 to 270 mg per cooked cup with fractional absorption in the same band as milk. In the UK, non-wholemeal flour is fortified with calcium carbonate by law, so bread is one of the largest single contributors to national intake at about 50 mg per slice. The adult reference intake of 1,000 mg/day (1,200 mg for women 51+, Institute of Medicine 2011) is reachable in three or four food choices, and this entry concerns adding a supplement to a diet that already meets that target, which is a different question from correcting a real deficit.
items.dose_from_food_note: Calcium supplements are sold at 500 to 600 mg elemental per tablet, and the trials that generated the safety signals gave 1,000 to 1,200 mg/day on top of whatever participants were already eating. Matching 1,000 mg from food takes 3.6 cups of milk, or 141 g of Cheddar, or about 85 g of Parmesan, or one 1/2-cup serving of calcium-set tofu (861 mg) plus one cup of cooked kale (177 mg) for 1,038 mg, or 3.2 pots of low-fat yogurt (about 546 g), or two small cans of sardines plus a glass of fortified soy drink (1,001 mg). The 'three pots of yogurt' route quoted in the original submission is wrong: 3 x 311 mg is 933 mg, 93% of the target and short of it. Every one of the corrected routes is a normal day of eating, so in a person whose diet already provides 1,000 mg a 1,000 mg supplement does not fill a deficit, it doubles the intake and delivers the added half as a single soluble bolus. The supplement is additive rather than corrective, which is the whole point of this entry.

items.form_caveat: The harms recorded in the trials attach to supplements, not to dietary calcium, and the proposed mechanism is the form itself. Food calcium arrives in small amounts inside a matrix across a whole meal and produces no sharp rise in serum calcium; a 500-1,000 mg dose of calcium carbonate or citrate produces a measurable postprandial spike, and that spike is the hypothesised driver of the vascular signal. The specific findings: in the Women's Health Initiative randomised trial, 36,282 postmenopausal women given 1,000 mg calcium carbonate plus 400 IU vitamin D3 daily for a mean 7 years had more clinically diagnosed urinary tract stones, hazard ratio 1.17 (95% CI 1.02-1.34), unrelated to baseline calcium intake (PMID 21525191). Bolland and colleagues' meta-analysis of calcium supplements without co-administered vitamin D reported a 27-31% relative increase in myocardial infarction (BMJ 2010, DOI 10.1136/bmj.c3691). In the 10-year MESA follow-up of 5,448 adults, supplement users had higher incident coronary artery calcification while the highest quintile of dietary calcium was associated with lower risk (Anderson et al., DOI 10.1161/JAHA.116.003815). Observational work in the same populations consistently finds higher dietary calcium associated with fewer kidney stones, the opposite direction to the supplement result. This is contested territory: a 2016 National Osteoporosis Foundation and American Society for Preventive Cardiology review concluded there was no demonstrable cardiovascular harm at total intakes up to 2,000-2,500 mg/day, and the meta-analyses have been criticised for relying on secondary endpoints and self-reported events. The defensible summary is that food calcium has no such signal attached to it in any dataset, so where the diet already reaches the target the supplement carries risk without a corresponding benefit. Two practical form points: calcium carbonate requires gastric acid and must be taken with food, so it is a poor choice for anyone on a proton pump inhibitor or with achlorhydria (calcium citrate does not have this dependency), and doses above about 500 mg saturate absorption, so a single 1,000 mg tablet is worse value than two 500 mg doses.
items.bioavailability: Fractional absorption reorders the raw milligram ranking, though less dramatically than the original submission claimed. From the tabulated studies (Nutrients 2022 review, PMC8746734; Heaney et al., J Food Sci 1993;58:1378-1380), at an identical 83 mg load: kale 52.7%, bok choy leaves 52.0%, bok choy stems 51.9%, broccoli 47.8% and cow milk 46.3%, with the authors stating the differences were absolutely small and statistically insignificant. No vegetable can be called the best-absorbed calcium food, and the superlative attached to bok choy in the original entry is refuted by the experiment it cited. Across loads of 14.7 to 563 mg the milk range is 21.7-66.0%, about 30-32% at a typical 250 mg load, so milk's upper bound exceeds every brassica figure and the claim that brassicas beat milk holds only at matched loads where the difference is not significant. Calcium-set tofu is 39.0-49.3%, Cheddar 37.4%, yogurt 24.2%, calcium carbonate supplement roughly 22-24%, calcium citrate roughly 24%, and spinach 5.1%. Two conclusions survive. Low-oxalate brassicas comfortably beat the supplement forms per milligram consumed and match milk at comparable loads, so a cup of bok choy at 158 mg delivers about as much absorbed calcium as 250 ml of milk (roughly 82 mg against 83 mg). And spinach, rhubarb, beet greens and Swiss chard should be struck off calcium lists entirely, since oxalate precipitates the calcium in the gut and the food is close to useless for this purpose despite good label numbers. On fortified plant milks, the carbonate fortificant performs as well as dairy calcium: Zhao, Martin and Weaver (J Nutr 2005;135(10):2379, PMID 16177199) titled their paper on the finding that calcium-carbonate-fortified soymilk is equivalent to cow milk in young women (21.1% against 21.7% at a 250 mg load), and only the tricalcium phosphate form is genuinely lower at 18.1%. The sedimentation problem is real and separate: the added salt is insoluble and settles to the bottom of the carton, so an unshaken carton delivers a fraction of the label value and the last glass delivers a dose nobody intended.

items.food_status_note: This is a product category rather than a molecule, and almost every nutrient inside it is abundant in ordinary food, which is why the US Preventive Services Task Force concluded in 2022 that the evidence is insufficient to recommend multivitamins for preventing cardiovascular disease or cancer, and recommended against beta-carotene and vitamin E supplements outright. The nutrients are food-abundant while the pill itself is manufactured: folic acid is not a natural food form, and cyanocobalamin occurs in food only in traces, so the accurate statement is that neither is the predominant natural form, and both are present in fortified foods, which this entry treats as a legitimate route for B12. Shortfalls that are real in populations are a short list: the 2020-2025 Dietary Guidelines for Americans name calcium, potassium, vitamin D and dietary fibre as nutrients of public health concern, with iron and folate added in pregnancy, and UK survey data adds magnesium, selenium and iron in younger women, though the specific NDNS below-LRNI percentages carried in the original submission (magnesium 9% of men and 13% of women, selenium 25.8% of males and 50.3% of females, iron about a quarter of younger women) could not be traced to a named survey round, age band or table and are indicative and unconfirmed here.
items.dose_from_food_note: There is no single food equivalent of a multivitamin, because a multivitamin is not a nutrient: one tablet supplies roughly 100% of the reference intake for 20 or more nutrients at once, and the only thing matching that profile is a varied diet, which by definition already supplies them. So the answer has to be given per nutrient, and it splits. For most of the tablet (vitamin C, vitamin A, thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, B6, vitamin E, vitamin K, zinc, selenium, copper, iodine) the food gap for anyone eating a normal mixed diet is zero. Vitamin D is reachable but rarely reached: the original claim that UV-treated mushrooms are the only food to hit 15 ug in one portion is arithmetically false, because 3 oz of canned sockeye salmon gives 17.9 ug (119% of the 15 ug RDA), 3 oz of farmed rainbow trout 16.2 ug (108%), a USDA half-fillet (155 g) of cooked sockeye 25.9 ug (173%), and a teaspoon of cod liver oil 11.3 ug (75%), alongside a cup of UV portabella at 24.4 ug. Reaching 15 ug/day from food needs about 90 g of cooked sockeye every day, or 1.15 litres of fortified milk, or 14 large eggs; the UK 10 ug RNI needs about 60 g of oily fish daily or 770 ml of fortified milk. So the vitamin D case for supplementing is behavioural (few people at temperate latitudes eat oily fish daily through winter) rather than compositional, and it argues for vitamin D alone rather than a 25-ingredient tablet. Periconceptional folic acid is a genuine exception: 400 ug/day is food-achievable in bulk (about 220 g of cooked lentils daily) but the trial evidence for preventing neural tube defects is for supplemental folic acid, and food folate is both less bioavailable and more variable, so food substitution is not supported. B12 on a vegan diet is the second real exception, since there is no reliable unfortified plant source, so a supplement or fortified food is mandatory. Two mismatches run the other way: the potassium in a multivitamin is capped at about 99 mg against a 3,500 mg reference intake, and the calcium is typically 100-200 mg, so the tablet cannot address either of the shortfalls the guidelines name, and fibre, the fourth named shortfall, is absent from every tablet. Iodised salt, the global public-health iodine vehicle, belongs in this list as well; verification named it as a complete omission but supplied no composition figure, so no row is given for it.

items.form_caveat: This category contains the clearest documented case of a whole food being safe while the isolated concentrate is harmful. Carotenoid-rich vegetables are consistently associated with lower lung cancer risk, while beta-carotene as a supplement increased lung cancer incidence in smokers and asbestos-exposed workers in the ATBC and CARET trials, and the USPSTF now recommends against it with moderate certainty that harms exceed benefits. Vitamin E supplements carry the same recommendation against. Preformed vitamin A as retinol in a tablet counts toward the 3,000 ug/day upper limit and is teratogenic at high intake, while beta-carotene in carrots does not convert quickly enough to reach toxicity. Two food rows on this list carry the same warning as the tablet: beef liver at 9,442 ug RAE/100 g and cod liver oil are both concentrated retinol sources, so neither is a free lunch. Folic acid in a tablet can partially mask the haematological signs of B12 deficiency while neurological damage continues, an effect food folate has not been shown to produce. Stacking is the underappreciated risk: a multivitamin alongside fortified breakfast cereal and a fortified plant drink can push folic acid, retinol, niacin and iron past their upper limits in someone who believes they are taking one tablet. Within the tablet itself, iron competes with zinc and copper for shared transporters and calcium interferes with iron uptake, so a combined product delivers less of each than the label states. And no tablet carries the fibre, the food-level potassium, or the polyphenols that account for much of the association between diet quality and outcomes, which is the structural reason a pill is not a diet.
items.bioavailability: Form differences run in both directions, so blanket claims fail here. Iron: haem iron from meat and fish absorbs at roughly 15-35% and is largely insensitive to the rest of the meal, while non-haem iron from plants and from the ferrous salts in tablets ranges from about 2% to 20% depending on phytate, polyphenols, calcium and vitamin C eaten at the same time. Spinach iron sits at the bottom of that range because oxalate binds it, so the textbook answer is the wrong answer. Folate: folic acid from a supplement taken with food is roughly 85% bioavailable against about 50% for naturally occurring food folate, so here the synthetic form genuinely outperforms the food. Vitamin B12: food B12 is protein-bound and needs gastric acid and pepsin to release it, so older adults with atrophic gastritis and long-term proton pump inhibitor or metformin users often absorb crystalline B12 from a tablet better than B12 from a chop. Vitamin D: the D2 in UV-treated mushrooms raises and sustains serum 25(OH)D less efficiently than the D3 in oily fish and most supplements, so 24.4 ug from a cup of portabella is not equivalent to 24.4 ug from salmon, and the mushroom rows should not be read as interchangeable with the fish rows despite ranking near them. Vitamin K: the K1 in leafy greens is poorly released from the plant matrix and cleared fast, while the long-chain MK-7 in natto reaches higher and far longer-lasting serum concentrations, so a portion of natto and a portion of kale are not interchangeable despite sharing the label term. All four fat-soluble vitamins need fat in the same meal, which is why a multivitamin swallowed with black coffee delivers less than the panel claims.

Flagged the NDNS below-LRNI percentages (magnesium 9%/13%, selenium 25.8%/50.3%, iron about a quarter of younger women) as indicative and unconfirmed, and set data_confidence to MEDIUM on that basis.
Flagged the EFSA 600 ug/day adult iodine upper level as consistent with the standard SCF figure but not confirmable from the retrieved compilation.

Added the omitted sources named in verification, each in rank order: cod liver oil 250 ug/100 g (FDC 173577), canned sockeye salmon 21.0 (FDC 173693), salted mackerel 25.2 (FDC 168149), farmed rainbow trout 19.0 (FDC 173718), UV crimini mushrooms 31.9 (FDC 168557), fortified fat spread 17.5 (FDC 171415), grilled haddock 421 ug iodine (CoFID 16-376) and crab brown meat 333 ug (CoFID 16-391).

Added spinach's 146 ug/100 g folate (263 ug per cooked cup, 66% of the 400 ug target) to the spinach row, which the original used only as an iron warning. The iron warning is unchanged, since the oxalate write-down is legitimate for iron.
Named iodised salt, fortified breakfast cereals, chickpeas, asparagus and edamame as genuine omissions without tabulating them, because verification supplied no composition figures for them.
Kept the RICH classification, which verification upheld once the vitamin D claim was corrected, and split the dose answer per nutrient rather than treating a 20-nutrient tablet as one dose.
Added a note that beef liver and cod liver oil carry the same preformed retinol hazard as the tablet, so the two most concentrated new rows are not free of the form caveat.

Left every verified figure untouched, including clams 84.1 ug, liver 48.0/172/4.4, lentils 358 ug, oysters 33.0 mg, Brazil nut 96 ug and the 544 ug six-kernel selenium overshoot, and the vitamin D dose arithmetic (90 g sockeye, 1.15 L fortified milk, 14 eggs; 60 g oily fish and 770 ml milk for the UK 10 ug RNI).

items.food_status_note_zh: 镁存在于叶绿素分子中，也集中在种子和谷物的外层，因此任何未精制的植物性食物都含有一定量；坚果、种子、可可、全谷物、豆类和深色叶菜都是有意义的贡献者，以它们为基础的混合膳食无需补充剂就能达到成人 RDA（31 岁以上男性 420 mg/天，31 岁以上女性 320 mg/天，Institute of Medicine 1997）。真正把镁剥掉的是精制加工，诚实的同类对比是 CoFID 全麦面包 66 mg/100 g 对白面包 22 mg/100 g（11-981 和 11-1145），相差三倍。麦麸的 389 mg/100 g（CoFID 11-906）是干磨组分，把它拿去和含水量约 40% 的烤制面包对比，会把精制的影响夸大到十八倍，不应这样使用。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 补充剂的售卖规格是 200 至 400 mg 元素镁，也就是一整天的需要量，而普通食物很容易覆盖这个区间。一天的实际算法：1 oz 南瓜籽（156 mg）加 1 杯熟黑豆（120 mg）加 1 oz 70-85% 黑巧克力（65 mg），在盘子里其他东西都还没算进来时就已经是 341 mg。相比之下，单一食物路线荒唐得多：只靠黑巧克力吃到 400 mg 意味着 175 g 巧克力，大约 1,000 kcal；只靠全麦面包吃到 400 mg 意味着 533 g，约 17 片。没有人需要单一食物路线，混合膳食路线只是三份正常分量。算术之外，安全性上的不对称影响更大：Institute of Medicine 设定的 350 mg/天 上限只针对补充剂形式的镁，并明确排除食物和水中天然存在的镁，因此来自种子和豆类的 700 mg 镁不受上限约束，而来自片剂的 400 mg 已经超过补充剂的上限。欧盟对通过补充剂或强化食品添加的镁设有相当的 250 mg/天 限值，通常归于 SCF 2001 意见书；核查期间无法获取原文，因此该数字在此仅作参考，未经确认。
items.form_caveat_zh: 差别在于剂量动力学，与化学性质无关。食物在一天之内以小剂量提供镁，并且处在减缓释放的基质里，未被吸收的部分始终很少，不会引起渗透性腹泻。一次 400 mg 可溶性镁盐会在肠腔留下大量未吸收的负荷，这一负荷正是当初设定上限所依据的导泻机制。柠檬酸镁和氢氧化镁本身就以接近补充剂剂量的剂量作为泻药销售。在肾清除率下降的人群中（CKD 4-5 期、同时服用多种药物的老年患者），补充剂可造成有症状的高镁血症，而食物来源的镁在正常摄入范围内由肾排泄处理。不存在食物形式反而更危险的情形。
items.bioavailability_zh: 在平均摄入 380 mg/天 时，膳食镁的净吸收率为 40 至 60%；当日摄入量升到 550 至 850 mg，吸收率降至 15-36%（Institute of Medicine DRI 报告 1997，第 6 章，NCBI Bookshelf NBK109816）。NIH ODS 在公众指导中引用 30-40%，因此实际取值应落在 DRI 区间的下半段，而不取 50% 的中点。植酸是食物中的主要抑制因素，可以按剂量依赖的方式把吸收分数削减最多 60%，所以麦麸、种子和豆类里的镁并没有被完全实现。草酸的影响远小于教科书版本的说法：Bohn 等（Br J Nutr 2004;91:601-606）测得菠菜餐的吸收分数为 26.7%，羽衣甘蓝为 36.5%，并认为菠菜的损失至少部分被其本身较高的镁含量抵消，因此一杯熟菠菜实际提供约 42 mg 吸收量，一杯熟羽衣甘蓝约 11 mg。补充剂各形式之间差别很大：Firoz 和 Graber（Magnesium Research 2001;14(4):257-262，PMID 11794633）测得氧化镁的吸收分数约 4%，乳酸镁、天门冬氨酸镁和氯化镁为 9-11%，而氧化镁恰恰是最便宜、卖得最多的形式。因此一片 400 mg 氧化镁提供的可吸收镁可能少于一小把南瓜籽，同时还带来稀便。
items.data_confidence_zh: 组成与算术为高：核查把每个引用的 FDC ID 对照 USDA SR Legacy 2018 年 4 月数据集、每个 CoFID 代码对照 CoFID 2021 逐一检查，未发现编造的标识符、错误的每 100 g 数值或错误的分量重量，所有按分量的乘算也都能复现。两处置信度较低的地方已就地标注：矿泉水那一行完全没有来源数值；亚麻籽、小麦胚芽、麦麸和可可粉的分量重量属于惯例，并非数据集分量。欧盟 SCF 关于添加镁 250 mg/天 的限值与通行数字一致，但无法从原文确认。

items.supplement: Calcium supplements on top of an adequate diet
items.supplement_zh: 在膳食已充足的基础上加用钙补充剂
items.food_status_note_zh: 钙是最容易从普通食物获得的营养素之一。乳制品、以钙凝固的豆腐、硬质奶酪、连骨一起吃的罐装鱼、整条小鱼、强化植物奶和强化果汁，每份正常分量各提供 200 至 860 mg；低草酸的十字花科蔬菜每杯熟菜再提供 150 至 270 mg，吸收分数与牛奶处在同一区间。在英国，非全麦面粉依法用碳酸钙强化，因此面包是全国钙摄入最大的单一贡献者之一，每片约 50 mg。成人参考摄入量 1,000 mg/天（51 岁以上女性 1,200 mg，Institute of Medicine 2011）靠三四项食物选择就能达到。本条讨论的是在已经达标的膳食之上再加补充剂，这与纠正真实缺乏是两个不同的问题。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 钙补充剂每片售 500 至 600 mg 元素钙，而产生安全性信号的那些试验是在受试者原有饮食之上再给 1,000 至 1,200 mg/天。从食物达到 1,000 mg 需要 3.6 杯牛奶，或 141 g 切达奶酪，或约 85 g 帕玛森奶酪，或一份 1/2 杯以钙凝固的豆腐（861 mg）加一杯熟羽衣甘蓝（177 mg）共 1,038 mg，或 3.2 盒低脂酸奶（约 546 g），或两小罐沙丁鱼加一杯强化豆奶（1,001 mg）。原稿引用的“三盒酸奶”路线是错的：3 × 311 mg 等于 933 mg，只有目标的 93%，达不到。上面每一条修正后的路线都是正常的一天饮食，所以对膳食已提供 1,000 mg 的人来说，1,000 mg 的补充剂并不填补缺口，它把摄入量翻倍，并把多出来的那一半作为单次可溶性剂量送进体内。这里的补充剂只是在原有摄入之上叠加，起不到纠正作用，这正是本条的要点。
items.form_caveat_zh: 试验中记录到的危害出现在补充剂身上，膳食钙没有这类记录，而推测的机制就是形式本身。食物中的钙在一整餐里以小剂量到达，不会造成血钙的急剧上升；500-1,000 mg 的碳酸钙或柠檬酸钙则产生可测量的餐后峰值，这个峰值被假设为血管信号的驱动因素。具体发现如下：在妇女健康倡议（Women's Health Initiative）随机试验中，36,282 名绝经后女性每天服用 1,000 mg 碳酸钙加 400 IU 维生素 D3，平均随访 7 年，临床诊断的尿路结石增多，风险比 1.17（95% CI 1.02-1.34），且与基线钙摄入无关（PMID 21525191）。Bolland 等对未同时给维生素 D 的钙补充剂所做的荟萃分析，报告心肌梗死相对风险增加 27-31%（BMJ 2010，DOI 10.1136/bmj.c3691）。在 5,448 名成人的 MESA 十年随访中，使用补充剂者新发冠状动脉钙化更多，而膳食钙最高五分位与更低风险相关（Anderson 等，DOI 10.1161/JAHA.116.003815）。同一批人群中的观察性研究一致发现膳食钙越高肾结石越少，方向与补充剂的结果相反。这仍是有争议的领域：2016 年美国国家骨质疏松基金会与美国预防心脏病学会的一篇综述认为，总摄入量达到 2,000-2,500 mg/天 时没有可证实的心血管危害，而那些荟萃分析也因依赖次要终点和自报事件受到批评。站得住的结论是：任何数据集中都没有针对食物钙的这类信号，因此在膳食已达标的情况下，补充剂带来风险而没有相应获益。两点实用的形式问题：碳酸钙需要胃酸，必须随餐服用，对服用质子泵抑制剂或胃酸缺乏者是糟糕的选择（柠檬酸钙没有这种依赖）；超过约 500 mg 的剂量会使吸收饱和，所以一片 1,000 mg 不如分两次各 500 mg 划算。
items.bioavailability_zh: 吸收分数会重排毫克数的排名，只是幅度不像原稿声称的那么大。根据表列研究（Nutrients 2022 综述，PMC8746734；Heaney 等，J Food Sci 1993;58:1378-1380），在同样 83 mg 负荷下：羽衣甘蓝 52.7%，小白菜叶 52.0%，小白菜茎 51.9%，西兰花 47.8%，牛奶 46.3%，作者明确指出这些差异在绝对值上很小且统计上不显著。因此没有哪种蔬菜能被称作吸收最好的钙食物，原条目给小白菜加的这个最高级说法，被它自己引用的实验否证。在 14.7 至 563 mg 的负荷范围内，牛奶的区间是 21.7-66.0%，典型 250 mg 负荷下约 30-32%，所以牛奶的上界高于任何一个十字花科数值，“十字花科蔬菜按毫克胜过牛奶”的说法只在负荷匹配、差异并不显著的条件下成立。以钙凝固的豆腐为 39.0-49.3%，切达奶酪 37.4%，酸奶 24.2%，碳酸钙补充剂约 22-24%，柠檬酸钙约 24%，菠菜 5.1%。有两个结论站得住。低草酸的十字花科蔬菜按每毫克摄入量计算明显优于各种补充剂形式，在可比负荷下与牛奶相当，所以一杯 158 mg 的小白菜提供的可吸收钙与 250 ml 牛奶差不多（约 82 mg 对约 83 mg）。另外，菠菜、大黄、甜菜叶和瑞士甜菜应当从钙的清单里彻底划掉，草酸会在肠道内把钙沉淀下来，尽管标签数字不错，这类食物在补钙上接近无用。关于强化植物奶，碳酸钙强化剂的表现与乳钙一样好：Zhao、Martin 和 Weaver（J Nutr 2005;135(10):2379，PMID 16177199）的论文标题就是这一发现，碳酸钙强化豆奶在年轻女性中与牛奶等效（250 mg 负荷下 21.1% 对 21.7%），只有磷酸三钙形式确实较低，为 18.1%。沉降问题是真实存在的另一回事：添加的钙盐不溶，会沉到纸盒底部，没摇过的盒子倒出来只有标签值的一部分，最后一杯的剂量则是谁也没打算给的。
items.data_confidence_zh: 组成与算术为高。核查把每个引用的 FDC ID 追溯到 USDA SR Legacy 2018 年 4 月、每个 CoFID 代码追溯到 CoFID 2021，食物描述、每 100 g 数值和分量重量全部吻合，所有按分量的乘算也都能复现。这里的修正属于推断层面（三处说法与其自身引用的来源不符），外加酸奶路线的一处算术错误。置信度较低的只限已就地标注的项目：银鱼、强化奶粉和强化燕麦谷物的分量重量属于惯例，并非数据集分量；SR Legacy 的羽衣甘蓝数值处在当前数据的高端；嫩豆腐（silken tofu）的对照值来自单一品牌产品。

items.supplement_zh: 复合维生素／复合矿物质
items.food_status_note_zh: 这是一个产品类别，谈不上是单一分子，而其中几乎每一种营养素在普通食物里都很丰富，这也是美国预防服务工作组（USPSTF）在 2022 年得出结论的原因：证据不足以推荐用复合维生素预防心血管疾病或癌症，同时明确不推荐 β-胡萝卜素和维生素 E 补充剂。营养素本身在食物中很丰富，药片则是制造出来的：叶酸（folic acid）不是食物中的天然形式，氰钴胺在食物里只有痕量，因此准确的说法是这两者都不是占主导的天然形式，两者也都存在于强化食品中，本条把强化食品视为获取 B12 的正当途径。人群中真实存在的摄入不足只是一个短名单：2020-2025 年美国膳食指南把钙、钾、维生素 D 和膳食纤维列为公共健康关注营养素，孕期再加铁和叶酸；英国调查数据在年轻女性中补上镁、硒和铁。不过原稿携带的具体 NDNS 低于 LRNI 比例（镁为男性 9%、女性 13%，硒为男性 25.8%、女性 50.3%，铁约为四分之一的年轻女性）无法追溯到具体的调查轮次、年龄组或表格，在此仅作参考，未经确认。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 复合维生素没有单一食物的等价物，因为它本身并不是一种营养素：一片药同时提供 20 种以上营养素各约 100% 的参考摄入量，唯一符合这一构成的东西是多样化的膳食，而多样化膳食按定义已经在提供这些营养素。所以答案必须按营养素分别给出，结论也随之分开。药片里的大部分成分（维生素 C、维生素 A、硫胺素、核黄素、烟酸、B6、维生素 E、维生素 K、锌、硒、铜、碘），对任何吃正常混合膳食的人来说食物缺口为零。维生素 D 可以达到，却很少有人达到：原稿称经紫外线处理的蘑菇是唯一能在一份内达到 15 ug 的食物，这在算术上不成立，因为 3 oz 罐装红鲑给出 17.9 ug（15 ug RDA 的 119%），3 oz 养殖虹鳟 16.2 ug（108%），USDA 的半片（155 g）熟红鲑 25.9 ug（173%），一茶匙鱼肝油 11.3 ug（75%），此外一杯紫外线处理的褐菇为 24.4 ug。要从食物做到 15 ug/天，需要每天约 90 g 熟红鲑，或 1.15 litres 强化牛奶，或 14 个大鸡蛋；英国的 10 ug RNI 需要每天约 60 g 多脂鱼或 770 ml 强化牛奶。所以维生素 D 需要补充的理由在行为层面（温带纬度很少有人整个冬天每天吃多脂鱼），与食物成分无关，据此该补的是单独的维生素 D，一片含 25 种成分的药并无必要。孕前和孕早期的叶酸是真正的例外：400 ug/天 靠食物在数量上做得到（每天约 220 g 熟扁豆），但预防神经管缺陷的试验证据针对的是补充剂形式的叶酸，食物叶酸生物利用度更低且变化更大，因此用食物替代得不到支持。素食者的 B12 是第二个真正的例外，植物性食物中没有可靠的未强化来源，所以补充剂或强化食品是必需的。有两处不匹配方向相反：复合维生素中的钾被限制在约 99 mg，而参考摄入量是 3,500 mg；钙通常只有 100-200 mg，因此药片解决不了指南列出的这两项不足，而纤维这第四项不足在任何药片里都不存在。碘盐作为全球公共卫生的碘载体也属于这个名单；核查指出它被完全遗漏，但没有给出成分数值，因此这里不为它单列一行。
items.form_caveat_zh: 这个类别里有最清楚的记录：完整食物是安全的，分离出来的浓缩物有害。富含类胡萝卜素的蔬菜一贯与更低的肺癌风险相关，而 β-胡萝卜素作为补充剂在 ATBC 和 CARET 试验中增加了吸烟者和石棉暴露工人的肺癌发生率，USPSTF 现在不推荐使用它，并以中等确定性认为危害超过获益。维生素 E 补充剂同样被列为不推荐。药片中以视黄醇形式存在的预成型维生素 A 计入 3,000 ug/天 的上限，高摄入时具有致畸性；胡萝卜里的 β-胡萝卜素转化速度不足以达到中毒水平。本清单里有两行食物带着与药片相同的警告：牛肝为 9,442 ug RAE/100 g，鱼肝油同样是浓缩的视黄醇来源，两者都不是免费的午餐。药片里的叶酸可以部分掩盖 B12 缺乏的血液学表现，而神经损伤仍在继续，食物叶酸尚未显示有这种效应。叠加是被低估的风险：复合维生素加上强化早餐谷物再加强化植物饮料，可以把叶酸、视黄醇、烟酸和铁推过各自的上限，而当事人以为自己只吃了一片药。在药片内部，铁与锌和铜竞争同一批转运体，钙干扰铁的吸收，所以复合产品实际提供的每种成分都少于标签值。另外没有任何药片带来纤维、食物水平的钾或多酚，而这些占了膳食质量与结局之间关联的很大一部分，这是药片顶不上膳食的结构性原因。
items.bioavailability_zh: 形式差异在两个方向上都存在，因此一刀切的说法在这里都不成立。铁：来自肉和鱼的血红素铁吸收率约 15-35%，且基本不受同餐其他成分影响；来自植物以及片剂中亚铁盐的非血红素铁则在约 2% 到 20% 之间，取决于同餐的植酸、多酚、钙和维生素 C。菠菜的铁处在这个区间的底部，因为草酸把它结合住了，所以教科书答案是错误答案。叶酸：随餐服用的补充剂叶酸生物利用度约 85%，天然食物叶酸约 50%，在这里合成形式确实更胜一筹。维生素 B12：食物中的 B12 与蛋白结合，需要胃酸和胃蛋白酶才能释放，因此患萎缩性胃炎的老年人以及长期使用质子泵抑制剂或二甲双胍者，往往从药片里的结晶 B12 吸收得比从一块肉里更好。维生素 D：紫外线处理蘑菇中的 D2 在提升和维持血清 25(OH)D 上不如多脂鱼和多数补充剂中的 D3 有效，所以一杯褐菇的 24.4 ug 不等于来自三文鱼的 24.4 ug，蘑菇那几行虽然排名相近，也不应读作能与鱼类互换。维生素 K：叶菜中的 K1 从植物基质中释放较差且清除很快，纳豆里的长链 MK-7 则达到更高、持续时间长得多的血清浓度，所以一份纳豆和一份羽衣甘蓝虽然共用同一个标签名称，也不能互换。四种脂溶性维生素都需要同餐有脂肪，这也是复合维生素配黑咖啡吞下去时实际提供量少于成分表所示的原因。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。组成数据质量为高：核查把每个引用的 FDC ID 和 CoFID 代码都追溯到源数据集，描述、每 100 g 数值和分量重量精确吻合。有两点把本条拉低。支撑整个摄入不足论证的英国 NDNS 低于 LRNI 比例按引用方式无法核实，没有给出调查轮次、年龄组或表格，而写到小数点后一位却不带年份的数字是没法核对的。EFSA 的 600 ug/天 碘上限与通行的 SCF 2002 数字一致，但核查期间无法提取其原文。另有若干新增行采用惯例分量而非数据集分量（黑线鳕、蟹褐肉、盐渍鲭鱼、紫外线处理的褐色小蘑菇、强化涂抹油脂），每一处都已就地标注。

items.food_status_note: Oily fish supply EPA and DHA in gram quantities per ordinary portion, so this is one of the few supplement categories where food competes with capsules at physiological doses. One 143 g herring fillet or one 130 g salmon portion delivers 1.8-2.9 g EPA+DHA, roughly seven to twelve times a single day's EFSA Adequate Intake of 250 mg (EFSA Journal 2010;8(3):1461, DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2010.1461; EFSA DRVs summary 2017). The lower end of that range is deliberate: the USDA farmed-salmon entry reflects older analyses, and in over 3,000 Scottish farmed salmon EPA+DHA fell from 2.74 g to 1.36 g per 100 g wet weight between 2006 and 2015 as feed shifted from fish oil to vegetable oil (Sprague 2016, DOI 10.1038/srep21892), giving 1.8 g for the same 130 g portion. Treat the farmed-salmon figures below as an upper bound and roughly halve them for current farmed fish. The richest sources in the USDA database are not fillets at all: caviar carries 6,540 mg EPA+DHA per 100 g and mixed fish roe 2,343 mg, both above cooked herring.
items.dose_from_food_note: Two doses with two different answers. The physiological dose (EFSA AI 250 mg/day, evidence range 250-500 mg/day) is easily eaten: one 143 g herring fillet a week averages 410 mg/day, one 130 g farmed salmon portion 399 mg/day, one wild salmon portion 342 mg/day. Two mackerel fillets, two 92 g tins of sardines or two 45 g tins of anchovies a week give 258-302 mg/day. In portion terms 250-500 mg/day is 0.6-1.3 salmon portions, 0.6-1.2 herring fillets, 1.7-3.3 mackerel fillets, 1.9-3.9 tins of sardines, 1.9-3.8 tins of anchovies, 2.8-5.6 trout fillets, or 1.2-2.4 USDA 172 g cans of albacore per week. Tinned light tuna is the weakest realistic route at 370 mg per 165 g can, which is 5 cans a week for 250 mg/day and 9 cans a week for 500 mg/day. The pharmacological dose of 4 g/day used in trials and in prescription products (AHA Science Advisory, Circulation 2019, DOI 10.1161/CIR.0000000000000709; REDUCE-IT used 4 g icosapent ethyl) cannot be eaten. It requires 199 g/day of herring (1.4 kg/week), 186 g/day of farmed salmon on 2006-era composition or 294 g/day on 2015 composition (1.3-2.1 kg/week), 288 g/day of pickled herring, 333 g/day of mackerel (3.8 fillets a day), 407 g/day of sardines (4.4 tins a day), 195 g/day of anchovies (4.3 tins a day, with the sodium load that implies), 61 g/day of caviar (about four tablespoons a day), or 464 g/day of tinned albacore. Above roughly 1 g/day of EPA+DHA, supplements are the only realistic route.

items.form_caveat: Whole fish and fish oil are not interchangeable in the evidence base. VITAL randomised 25,871 adults to a 1 g/day capsule supplying 840 mg EPA+DHA (460 mg EPA, 380 mg DHA) and found no reduction in major cardiovascular events (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.80-1.06) or cancer incidence (HR 1.03) over 5.3 years (Manson 2019, PMID 30415637). The benefit at 4 g/day in REDUCE-IT came from purified prescription EPA rather than a food-equivalent mixture, and high-dose omega-3 carries an atrial fibrillation signal that eating fish does not. On contaminants, the direction of the tradeoff is clear but the numbers are weaker than they look: the FDA/EPA per-species mercury means quoted in the earlier draft (1.45 ppm Gulf of Mexico tilefish, 1.00 swordfish, 0.98 shark, 0.73 king mackerel, 0.35 albacore, 0.13 canned light tuna, 0.01-0.08 for sardine, salmon, anchovy, Atlantic mackerel, trout and herring) could not be retrieved from any live FDA or EPA page, so treat every one of them as indicative and unconfirmed. The tilefish figure in particular should be re-checked, since FDA's published Gulf of Mexico mean is usually cited as 1.123 ppm. What the surviving EPA page does confirm is the qualitative placement: anchovies, Atlantic mackerel, sardines and trout are all 'Best Choices'. Independent synthesis in Karimi 2012 (PMID 22732656) gives grand means of 0.882 ppm for shark and 0.883 ppm for tilefish, and 0.450 ppm for fresh or frozen tuna, which is not the canned product and should not be read as such. The earlier claim that high-mercury predators are also mediocre omega-3 sources has been withdrawn: it rested on a swordfish figure of 108 mg EPA per 85 g with no FDC ID that could not be traced, and an EPA-only figure understates a DHA-dominant fish. Dioxins run the other way, concentrating in the fat of oily fish. EFSA cut the tolerable weekly intake to 2 pg TEQ/kg body weight and reported it exceeded across all European age groups with fatty fish among the top contributors (EFSA Journal 2018;16(11):5333, DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2018.5333, document confirmed; the '5 to 15 fold' exceedance figure inside it was not independently verified). Refined fish oils must meet 1.75 pg WHO-TEQ/g fat for dioxins and 6.0 pg/g fat for dioxins plus dioxin-like PCBs under Regulation (EU) 2023/915 (limits not re-verified in this pass), so a purified concentrate can carry a lower contaminant load per gram of EPA+DHA than the fish it came from. One processing detail: draining oil-packed tuna pours away omega-3, and it takes both fatty acids with it. Canned white tuna in oil retains 66 mg EPA and 178 mg DHA per 100 g after draining, a total of 244 mg, against 233 mg EPA and 629 mg DHA (862 mg total) for the water-packed product, a 72% loss of total EPA+DHA (USDA FDC 175157 versus 175158, both confirmed).
items.bioavailability: Chemical form changes absorption measurably. Using natural triglyceride fish oil as the 100% reference, the bioavailability index was 124% for re-esterified triglyceride and 73% for ethyl ester (Dyerberg 2010, PMID 20638827, both values confirmed). The 91% figure for free fatty acid and the 3.1-3.6 g/day matched dose range are consistent with the paper as usually cited but were not independently confirmed. Most cheap concentrates are ethyl esters, which also depend more on a fat-containing meal for absorption, so a 1,000 mg ethyl-ester capsule taken on an empty stomach does not deliver what the label implies. Fish is delivered as natural triglyceride inside a fat and protein matrix and needs no such allowance. Preparation matters more than cooking method: canning in oil and then draining removes omega-3, whereas canning in water and draining does not.
items.data_confidence: HIGH. All eleven USDA composition rows resolved to exactly the described food with the stated EPA and DHA values, and roughly 60 dose-gap calculations recomputed correctly. The two defects were invented portion weights, now replaced with USDA's own measures. Confidence drops only on the peripheral material: the FDA/EPA per-species mercury means, the EU 2023/915 dioxin limits and the swordfish EPA figure are unconfirmed and are labelled as such.

items.food_status_note: The molecules krill oil delivers, EPA and DHA, are abundant in ordinary oily fish, and a 1-2 g/day krill oil dose is smaller than what a single tin of sardines provides. The phospholipid delivery form is also obtainable from food, which the earlier draft got wrong: fish roe and caviar are membrane-lipid tissues in which a large share of the EPA and DHA is phospholipid-bound, and in lean white fish such as cod most of the (small) EPA+DHA pool sits in phospholipid rather than triglyceride. The triglyceride generalisation holds for fatty fish flesh only. One tablespoon of caviar (16 g, 1,046 mg EPA+DHA) beats a 2 g krill oil dose on both quantity and form. Krill itself is close to a non-food: Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba) is eaten as okiami in Japan and to a small extent in Russia and the Philippines, but the global catch is largely rendered into meal and oil, and the shell carries a heavy fluoride load that has to be stripped before human consumption. Nobody reaches a krill oil dose by eating krill; they reach it by eating fish or roe, or by taking capsules.
items.dose_from_food_note: There is effectively no gap, which is the useful finding. Measured EPA plus DHA in 20 commercial krill oils from the Korean market spanned 14.2-34.8% of total fatty acids (Lee 2024, PMID 39233519, DOI 10.4014/jmb.2406.06026, range confirmed; the sampling is one national market). Converting that percentage to capsule mass overstates the content, because total fatty acids are less than capsule mass once phospholipid head groups, free sterols, astaxanthin and excipients are counted, so every figure that follows is a ceiling rather than a point estimate. A 1 g capsule carries at most roughly 140-350 mg EPA+DHA. Two capsules (2 g) deliver at most about 280-700 mg, which is matched or beaten by one 92 g tin of sardines (903 mg), one 45 g tin of anchovies (924 mg), one mackerel fillet (1,059 mg) or one tablespoon of caviar (1,046 mg). At the top of the trial range, 4 g/day of krill oil supplies at most roughly 570-1,400 mg, equal to at most 0.6-1.5 tins of sardines. Because these are ceilings, the real gap runs further in favour of fish than the raw numbers suggest. Going the other way, matching a krill oil dose by eating krill is not a real option: the catch is not sold as food outside a small Japanese and Russian market, and the shell must be removed for fluoride reasons.

items.form_caveat: Two things were previously claimed to separate krill oil from food, and both claims are weaker than stated. The phospholipid form is the product claim, and fish roe and caviar supply phospholipid-bound EPA and DHA in ordinary food, so the honest version is that krill oil offers a high phospholipid share conveniently, not uniquely. Krill oil is reported at roughly 39-81% phospholipid (Xie 2019, DOI 10.1111/1541-4337.12427); the citation is real and topically correct, but the range could not be traced to a page or table in the review, so treat it as indicative and unconfirmed, and do not read the original two-decimal precision as measured. Astaxanthin is the second claim, and 'no oily fish portion supplies it in comparable concentration' should not stand: wild sockeye and other red-fleshed Pacific salmon carry astaxanthin in flesh at roughly 25-40 mg/kg, so a 130 g portion supplies about 3-5 mg against the 0.1-1.5 mg per gram of oil typical of krill capsules. That concentration could not be re-verified, so it is a challenge to the claim rather than a settled figure, but the flat denial is gone. Neither the phospholipid form nor the astaxanthin has been shown to produce a clinical outcome that fish or fish oil does not. Against that, krill oil is the most expensive way to buy EPA and DHA per milligram, capsule doses are small enough that many products deliver less omega-3 than one tin of fish, it is a crustacean allergen, and whole krill or poorly processed krill meal carries the fluoride load of the exoskeleton. The fluoride figures usually quoted are about 4,260 mg F/kg fat-free dry matter in the carapace against 570 mg/kg in raw muscle; neither full text was retrievable, so both values are unconfirmed and should be attributed to whichever paper actually reports them (Soevik & Braekkan, Journal of the Fisheries Research Board of Canada 1979;36(11):1414-1416, DOI 10.1139/f79-204, which was not yet called the Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences in 1979; and Tou 2007, PMID 17345959). Sustainability is a genuine consideration given that Antarctic krill is the base of the Southern Ocean food web.
items.bioavailability: The phospholipid form does appear to be absorbed at least as well as triglyceride and better than ethyl ester. In a crossover trial in 12 healthy men at a matched 1,680 mg EPA+DHA dose, incorporation into plasma phospholipids by area under the curve over 0-72 h was 80.03 +/- 34.71 %*h for krill oil, 59.78 +/- 36.75 %*h for re-esterified triglyceride fish oil and 47.53 +/- 38.42 %*h for ethyl ester fish oil, with no statistically significant difference (EPA p = 0.057, DHA p = 0.246, EPA+DHA p = 0.119) (Schuchardt 2011, Lipids Health Dis, PMC3168413, all figures confirmed). Attributing that result to the phospholipid form is not the only reading: the same paper notes that 22% of the krill oil's EPA and 21% of its DHA were present as free fatty acids, which absorb readily and offer a plausible alternative explanation. The practical implication is modest either way, since a krill capsule contains so much less EPA and DHA than a portion of fish that absorption efficiency does not close the gap.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The comparator fish and roe composition is all traced to USDA records and the two human trials (Lee 2024, Schuchardt 2011) checked out exactly. The krill-specific claims are the weak part: the phospholipid percentage range, both fluoride values and the sockeye astaxanthin concentration are all unverified, and two of the three factual claims that justified the original classification turned out to be false.

items.food_status_note: Everything cod liver oil supplies is available from ordinary food: EPA and DHA from oily fish and roe, vitamin D from oily fish, vitamin A from any liver. Cod liver oil is itself a traditional food-grade oil with its own USDA composition entry, which is why it appears in the list below, and it is included as the reference product rather than as an alternative to itself. What makes it distinctive is concentration: one teaspoon (4.5 g) carries 806 mg EPA+DHA, 1,350 ug RAE of preformed vitamin A (4,500 IU) and 11.2 ug of vitamin D (450 IU). Two genuine food alternatives are named without figures because no authoritative per-portion composition value could be obtained in this pass: tinned cod liver, eaten in Nordic, Baltic and Russian cuisine, and liver as a vitamin A source. Rather than estimate them, no row is given.
items.dose_from_food_note: For the EPA and DHA at a traditional teaspoon dose there is no gap, and food matches it easily: 806 mg per teaspoon is a little under one 92 g tin of sardines (903 mg) and about a quarter of a herring fillet (2,873 mg). Cod liver oil is also efficient in the other direction: 250-500 mg/day of EPA+DHA needs only 1.4-2.8 g of oil, a third to two thirds of a teaspoon, carrying 419-838 ug RAE of vitamin A, comfortably inside the 3,000 ug/day UL. The gap that opens at pharmacological doses is a toxicity gap rather than a volume one. Reaching 4 g/day of EPA+DHA takes 22.3 g of cod liver oil, about 1.6 tablespoons, delivering 6,704 ug RAE of preformed vitamin A every day, 2.2 times the EFSA adult UL. Traditional cod liver oil therefore cannot be dose-escalated to the level used in triglyceride-lowering trials, and food cannot reach 4 g/day either (see the Omega-3 entry). That is what plain fish oil and purified concentrates exist for.

items.form_caveat: This is the clearest case in this group where the concentrated product is hazardous in a way the food behaviour does not suggest. The vitamin A is preformed retinol, so it accumulates and is teratogenic. Anyone already taking a multivitamin, or pregnant, can exceed the 3,000 ug RAE/day UL on one tablespoon alone (4,080 ug). Doubling up cod liver oil with a separate vitamin D supplement is the other common stacking error. Many modern products labelled cod liver oil are refined with the vitamin A and D partly stripped and re-standardised, so the USDA generic entry above describes traditional oil and not necessarily what is in a given bottle: the label governs. Contaminants concentrate in liver, which is why the EU sets a separate limit for fish liver and derived products (20.0 pg WHO-TEQ/g wet weight) alongside the 1.75 pg/g fat dioxin and 6.0 pg/g fat dioxin plus dioxin-like PCB limits for marine oils under Regulation (EU) 2023/915. Those limit values were not re-verified in this pass. Commercial cod liver oil is refined to meet them; home-rendered or artisanal liver oil is not.
items.bioavailability: Cod liver oil is a natural triglyceride and was one of the natural-triglyceride comparators assigned the 100% reference index in the Dyerberg comparison, against 124% for re-esterified triglyceride and 73% for ethyl ester (PMID 20638827, both comparator values confirmed). Its fat-soluble vitamins come dissolved in the oil, which is the ideal vehicle, and that is precisely why the vitamin A is so efficiently absorbed and why overdose is easy. There is no absorption advantage over eating oily fish for the EPA and DHA.
items.data_confidence: HIGH. The USDA cod liver oil record matched on every value including both household measures and both vitamin unit conversions, and the whole arithmetic block recomputed exactly (806 mg and 2,434 mg per portion, 322% of the AI, 45% and 136% of the vitamin A UL, 1.4-2.8 g for 250-500 mg carrying 419-838 ug RAE, 22.3 g for 4 g/day carrying 6,704 ug RAE). The EFSA vitamin A and D ULs and the EU 2023/915 limits are widely cited but were not confirmed in this pass, and they are load-bearing for the toxicity conclusion.
