items.form_caveat: The food is safe and useful; the supplement indication is the problem. Wheat bran is a genuinely effective faecal bulking agent, increasing stool by roughly 5 g per 1 g of bran consumed, at the top of the accepted 3-5.4 g range (DOI 10.3109/09637486.2012.687366), and it is a reasonable food for ordinary constipation and general fibre intake. In IBS it commonly worsens bloating, distension and pain, and it was the arm patients dropped out of. A less obvious caveat: wheat bran carries fructan (white wheat flour measures 0.75 g fructan/100 g, DOI 10.3389/fnut.2024.1446771), so bran-loading also raises FODMAP intake in exactly the patients least able to tolerate it. Insoluble-fibre supplements sold as 'IBS fibre' are marketing the wrong fibre class; the evidence in IBS favours the viscous, poorly fermented kind.
items.bioavailability: Not absorbed. The mechanism is mechanical bulking plus water-holding by arabinoxylan and cellulose, and the non-starch polysaccharide of the bran is 70% arabinoxylan, 24% cellulose and 6% beta-glucan (Stevenson et al., PMID 22716911, quotation verified). Bran accelerates small bowel transit and increases faecal weight dose-dependently. Particle size matters more than gram total, because coarse bran bulks and irritates while finely milled bran loses much of the effect, so two products with the same fibre label are not interchangeable. Only 1.5-4.0 g per 100 g is soluble, so bran contributes almost nothing to the viscous-gel effects on cholesterol, glycaemia and stool consistency that people often assume fibre delivers.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The core wheat values were confirmed against USDA legacy records (wheat bran 42.8, whole-wheat bread 6.0, whole-grain flour 10.7), as were the Stevenson NSP split and the Bijkerk trial narrative. Weaknesses: the bran flakes FDC ID could not be resolved, the whole-wheat bread slice weight is unconfirmed, and the corn bran, rice bran and all-bran figures come from the verification report's compiled values with conventional rather than sourced portion weights.
corrections_applied: Deleted the false superlative that wheat bran is 'one of the most fibre-dense foods in any composition table' and reframed it as one of the most fibre-dense ordinary cereal fractions, naming corn bran at 79 g/100 g as the USDA leader.
Added corn bran (79 g/100 g), rice bran (about 21 g/100 g) and extruded all-bran cereal (about 29-30 g/100 g) in rank order.
Corrected the bran flakes equivalence: 10 g of crude bran carries 4.28 g of fibre, which matches about 1 serving of bran flakes, not 2.
Recomputed whole-wheat bread on a 28 g slice: 2 slices = 56 g = 3.4 g fibre and 11% of the reference intake, replacing 3.8 g and 13%.
Flagged FDC 173002 (bran flakes) as an unconfirmed record identifier.
Limited the RICH grade to cereal-bran bases and stated that powdered/microcrystalline cellulose and methylcellulose have no dietary equivalent.
Flagged the unresolved discrepancy between Stevenson's 'wheat soluble fibre under 1% of dry weight' and the 1.5-4.0 g/100 g soluble figure quoted for bran.

items.food_status_note: This item bundles three substances with two different answers. Inulin and fructo-oligosaccharide (FOS) are RICH: chicory root at 15-20 g per 100 g fresh weight, Jerusalem artichoke at roughly 8-22 g, garlic at about 9-16 g, onion at about 2 g, with smaller amounts in globe artichoke, shallot, salsify, leek, asparagus, banana, wheat and rye. Beta-galacto-oligosaccharide (GOS) is SYNTHETIC and should not be carried under the same heading: the beta-GOS used in trials is manufactured enzymatically by transgalactosylation of lactose and has no meaningful presence in ordinary food. The galacto-oligosaccharides that do occur in legumes are alpha-galactosides (raffinose, stachyose, verbascose), a chemically different family with different bacterial targets. Habitual dietary intake of the fructan class is low: mean 1.6-1.7 g/day in a Slovenian survey (DOI 10.3389/fnut.2024.1446771) and median inulin 1.3 g/day in UK schoolchildren (PMID 40808333).
items.dose_from_food_note: For inulin and FOS the answer depends on which food. A 5 g/day dose is reachable from about 250 g of raw onion (two to three medium onions), about 10-19 cloves of garlic on the corrected 9-16 g/100 g range (the submission's 30 cloves was wrong by roughly 3x and contradicted its own food row), about 23-63 g of Jerusalem artichoke, or about 30 g of salsify on an unconfirmed figure. It is out of reach from banana (about 4.5 kg), leek (about 2.1 kg) and asparagus (roughly 1-5 kg, the range reflecting a fivefold uncertainty in the fresh-weight figure; the submission's flat 5 kg used the low end only). The tolerance ceiling is the more useful number than the dose: up to 10 g/day of native inulin and up to 5 g/day of oligofructose were well tolerated in a randomised crossover trial, while 10 g of oligofructose substantially increased symptoms, chiefly flatulence then bloating (Bonnema et al., PMID 20497775). One 150 g cup of Jerusalem artichoke delivers roughly 12-33 g of inulin, so between one and three times the tolerated daily ceiling in a single sitting. For GOS the answer is a flat no: the beta-GOS doses used in trials are made industrially and no ordinary food supplies them.

items.form_caveat: Chicory root is the classic textbook answer and a poor recommendation: it is the industrial source of inulin and is roasted as a coffee substitute rather than eaten as a vegetable, so its 15-20 g/100 g headline is not a dietary route. Dandelion greens, which are eaten as a vegetable, and burdock root and yacon are recognised high-inulin foods that answer that objection, though no confirmed figures for them were available here. Chicory also illustrates why fibre tables and fructan assays disagree, since USDA lists chicory root at only 1.5 g total dietary fibre per 100 g (FDC 169993). Purified inulin and oligofructose are safe as food ingredients, and concentration is what causes symptoms: the same molecule that is unremarkable spread across a day's vegetables provokes flatulence and bloating as a single 10 g bolus (PMID 20497775). Briet et al. (PMID 7588500) reported a symptom ladder for FOS (excess flatus above 30 g/day, borborygmi and bloating above 40 g, cramps and diarrhoea at 50 g, with no tolerance developing on chronic dosing); the citation is correct and on topic, but those specific thresholds could not be retrieved from the full text and are unconfirmed. The reverse caveat matters clinically: the 'eat more prebiotic vegetables' list (onion, garlic, leek, globe artichoke, Jerusalem artichoke, wheat, rye) is precisely the list a low-FODMAP diet removes, so in IBS the food route and the supplement route can both make things worse. Finally, do not treat legume alpha-GOS as a food form of supplemental beta-GOS; the reported contents in Phaseolus vulgaris (raffinose 0.8-7.4 mg/g, stachyose 20.0-30.9 mg/g, verbascose 0.3-1.3 mg/g, DOI 10.3390/foods15020391) come from a genuine and on-topic paper whose individual values could not be confirmed, and they are different molecules with a flatulence profile of their own.
items.bioavailability: Fructans are not absorbed at all, so the variable is where and how fast they ferment, and chain length decides that. Oligofructose (DP 2-8) ferments proximally and quickly, which is why its tolerated dose was half that of long-chain native inulin in the same trial, 5 g against 10 g (PMID 20497775). Assay and plant part also drive the numbers: onion measured 1.97 g/100 g and leek 0.24 g/100 g by AOAC 999.03 in one national survey (DOI 10.3389/fnut.2024.1446771), while an Australian survey using the Megazyme assay reported 1.2-17.4 g/100 g across high-fructan alliums including leek bulb (PMID 17625872). Storage matters too, since fructan is depolymerised during onion storage. Single figures should be read as indicative rather than exact. GOS is fermented similarly but is a distinct substrate: beta-GOS and legume alpha-galactosides are not interchangeable.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The Ferjancic fructan values (onion, leek, banana, bread, flour) and the Bonnema tolerance thresholds were verified verbatim, and the chicory contrast between 15-20 g inulin and a 1.5 g USDA fibre record holds. Against that: the garlic figure was a source misreading now corrected to a wide 9-16 g/100 g range, Jerusalem artichoke spans 8-22 g/100 g, the asparagus fresh-weight value is uncertain by fivefold, the Briet symptom ladder and the Phaseolus oligosaccharide values could not be confirmed, and the three added foods (salsify, globe artichoke, shallot) rest on group-level ranges rather than food-specific measurements.

Recomputed the Jerusalem artichoke dose equivalent to about 23-63 g on the wider range.

items.food_status_note: SYNTHETIC here means no dietary source, not an artificial molecule: a named probiotic strain is a live organism, a single clonal isolate held in a culture bank, grown in industrial fermenters, freeze-dried and encapsulated. No food contains it. Fermented foods do carry large numbers of live lactic acid bacteria, but the species and strains present are whichever organisms grow in that food and its starter, never the deposited trial strain. Because probiotic efficacy is demonstrated strain by strain, a food supplying a different strain of the same species is a different product. Live-organism loads for fermented foods are given under the generic multi-strain entry.
items.dose_from_food_note: The gap is categorical and no quantity of food closes it. Named-strain doses in trials run from about 1x10^8 to 1x10^10 CFU/day; Bifidobacterium longum 35624 (formerly classified as infantis) was effective at 1x10^8, a figure the source trial expressed as CFU/mL rather than CFU/day (PMID 16863564). A single cup of kefir at 2.5x10^8 CFU/mL supplies roughly 6x10^10 live lactic acid bacteria (DOI 10.3390/foods15101616), so the raw CFU total is easily exceeded by food. The fraction of those cells belonging to the trialled strain is zero, which makes the CFU comparison meaningless for a strain-specific claim.
items.form_caveat: This is the most important form caveat in the group. Clinical evidence for probiotics is strain-specific, and often formulation-specific and indication-specific on top of that. Yoghurt, kefir, sauerkraut, kimchi, miso, natto and tempeh do not contain the strains tested in the trials, so evidence generated with a named strain does not transfer to any fermented food, and does not transfer to a different strain of the same species either. Eating fermented food is a reasonable dietary habit with its own emerging evidence base, and it is a separate thing from taking a named strain at a defined dose for a specific clinical effect. Two practical points: heat kills the organisms, so a pasteurised or cooked ferment (canned sauerkraut, miso stirred into boiling soup, baked tempeh) delivers no live cells; and species-level labelling on a supplement such as 'contains Lactobacillus acidophilus' without a strain designation carries no more transferable evidence than a food does.
items.bioavailability: Survival of gastric acid and bile is strain-dependent, and the delivery matrix changes it: the fat and buffering capacity of a dairy food improves survival relative to a bare capsule, while enteric coating or microencapsulation is used to achieve the same in supplements. Dose is not monotonic, which is the clearest evidence that formulation matters as much as CFU count. In a 362-patient dose-ranging trial in primary-care IBS, B. infantis 35624 at 1x10^8 was significantly superior to placebo and to all other doses, while 1x10^6 and 1x10^10 were not; the paper attributes the failure of the highest dose to significant formulation problems (Whorwell et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2006;101:1581-1590, PMID 16863564). Two generalisability caveats the submission omitted: the trial enrolled women only, and doses were expressed as CFU/mL in the paper rather than CFU/day. A higher label CFU is therefore not better, and label CFU at manufacture is not the same as viable CFU at end of shelf life.
items.data_confidence: HIGH. The claim is categorical (no food contains a deposited trial strain) and the supporting trial was verified: 362 patients, doses 1x10^6, 1x10^8 and 1x10^10, with the 1x10^8 arm significantly superior to placebo and all other doses. The one detail that failed verification, the gelling mechanism for the top dose, has been removed and replaced with the paper's own wording.
corrections_applied: Added the note that SYNTHETIC here means no dietary source rather than an artificial molecule, since the same code is applied to genuinely manufactured products elsewhere in this group.
Replaced the unsourced 'capsule formulation gelled' mechanism with the paper's own 'significant formulation problems'.
Added the two omitted Whorwell caveats: the trial enrolled women only, and doses were expressed as CFU/mL, not CFU/day.

items.food_status_note: RICH applies to one endpoint only, and it is a redefined one: live lactic acid bacteria of common genera. On that endpoint several ordinary fermented foods match or exceed supplement label doses, with yoghurt surveyed at up to 10^9 CFU/g, kefir at 2.5x10^8 CFU/mL, unpasteurised sauerkraut at about 2x10^8 CFU/g, kimchi at 10^7.14 to 10^9.23 CFU/g and natto reported at roughly 10^8-10^9 CFU/g. On the endpoint that matters for a product claim, a defined blend of characterised strains at a stated dose, no food supplies it and the honest grade would be a flat no. A reader scanning this field should not read RICH as 'food replaces this product'. The named-strain entry in this same group states that a CFU comparison is meaningless for a strain-specific claim, and that remains true here.
items.dose_from_food_note: For total live cells there is no gap. The source review calculates that about 10^10 cells is the intake likely needed to affect the microbiota and that this is met by 100 g of a food carrying 10^8 cells/g (PMID 30197628). One cup of kefir, one cup of yoghurt, about 120 g of raw sauerkraut, a cup of kimchi or a cup of natto each clear that bar, and kimchi at the top of its measured range delivers more live organisms in one serving than most 50-billion-CFU capsules. The gap is qualitative: identity, characterisation and consistency. Fermented food counts vary across four to six orders of magnitude between products and batches (yoghurt below 10^4 to 10^9 CFU/g), the organisms are usually not identified to strain, and none of them are the strains on the label of the blend.

items.form_caveat: Fermented food is a reasonable dietary habit and a different proposition from a named strain at a defined dose. Even a generic blend tells you which species you are getting and roughly how many; a jar of sauerkraut tells you neither, and a pasteurised jar contains no live cells. The practical points that decide whether a food delivers anything: it must be labelled raw, unpasteurised or 'live cultures' and kept refrigerated; heat destroys the organisms, so miso added to boiling soup, cooked kimchi and baked tempeh contribute essentially nothing; and long-aged cheeses can be several orders of magnitude lower than young ones. Water kefir, kombucha, brine-fermented unpasteurised pickles, kvass, skyr, traditional buttermilk and young raw-milk cheeses belong on the same list, though no confirmed counts for them were available here. Conversely, a supplement claim of 50 billion CFU means little if the strains are unnamed, because probiotic effects are demonstrated strain by strain, and CFU counts on labels refer to manufacture rather than end of shelf life.
items.bioavailability: Gastric and bile survival is strain-dependent and matrix-dependent. Fermented dairy foods buffer stomach acid and their fat content improves transit survival, a genuine advantage of the food route over an uncoated capsule; supplements compensate with enteric coating or microencapsulation. Almost none of these organisms colonise permanently, so the effect is dose-dependent and ceases when intake stops, which applies equally to food and to capsules. The source review notes that many fermentation microbes are closely related to probiotic organisms and can share mechanisms, which is the honest basis for recommending fermented food, but relatedness is not equivalence and it does not license transferring a strain-specific trial result onto a jar of kimchi.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The Rezac counts for kimchi, sauerkraut, yoghurt, miso and tempeh were verified against Tables 5 and 6, as were the kefir counts and the 10^10-cells threshold. Two soft spots remain: the tempeh 9 log ceiling could not be sourced and has been removed, and the natto count is a literature range supplied by the verification report without a retrievable citation.

items.food_status_note: SYNTHETIC here means no dietary source, not an artificial molecule. The strain is a live organism isolated from the ileal mucosa of a healthy human donor and has since been reclassified from Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis to B. longum subsp. longum 35624 (PLOS One 2016;11:e0162983, PMC5033381). It is propagated industrially from a proprietary strain bank and freeze-dried. It is present in no food, no fermented food and no other supplement brand. Comparative genome analysis identified a 35624-specific gene cluster encoding biosynthesis of its exopolysaccharide EPS624, the kind of strain-level distinction that makes substitution unsound.
items.dose_from_food_note: No quantity of any food supplies this strain. The trial dose is small in absolute terms, 1x10^8 CFU, which is roughly the number of live bacteria in half a gram of unpasteurised sauerkraut at 8.3 log CFU/g, so the dose is not the obstacle and the identity is. Fermented foods can supply a thousand times more live cells than the effective dose of 35624 while supplying none of it. Note that the source trial expressed its doses as CFU/mL rather than CFU/day.
items.form_caveat: The dose-response data make the point better than any argument about food. In the 362-patient dose-ranging trial, 1x10^8 of B. infantis 35624 was significantly superior to placebo for abdominal pain, the composite score, bloating, bowel dysfunction and incomplete evacuation, while 1x10^6 and 1x10^10 were not, the paper attributing the highest dose's failure to significant formulation problems (Whorwell et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2006;101:1581-1590, PMID 16863564). The trial enrolled women only, which limits generalisation and which the submission did not state. If a tenfold change in dose of the same strain in the same capsule abolishes the effect, swapping the strain for a different Bifidobacterium in a yoghurt cannot be assumed to preserve it. Anyone advised to take 35624 should be told plainly that no diet reproduces it and that a generic bifidobacterium supplement is a different product.
items.bioavailability: The strain was selected partly for surviving gastrointestinal transit, and its documented actions are immunoregulatory and barrier-related rather than nutritional: enhanced gut barrier function, accelerated intestinal transit and reduced visceral hypersensitivity. It does not permanently colonise, so the effect depends on continued daily intake. Formulation dominates delivery: the failure of the 1x10^10 arm was a formulation problem rather than evidence against high cell numbers, and it illustrates that CFU on a label is not the active variable on its own. The specific gelling mechanism the submission gave for that failure is not in the source and has been removed.
items.data_confidence: HIGH. The strain's origin, reclassification, exopolysaccharide gene cluster and the dose-ranging trial results were all confirmed. The only failed detail was the gelling mechanism, now replaced with the paper's own wording, and the only additions are the women-only enrolment and the CFU/mL unit.
corrections_applied: Replaced 'having formed a gel in the capsule' with the paper's own 'significant formulation problems'.
Added the women-only enrolment as a generalisability caveat and noted that doses were expressed as CFU/mL rather than CFU/day.
Added the clarification that SYNTHETIC means no dietary source rather than chemically synthesised, since the strain is a live human-derived isolate.
Changed 'Infinite' in the dose-gap framing to a statement that identity rather than quantity is the obstacle, retaining the half-gram-of-sauerkraut comparison, which checks out at 8.3 log CFU/g.

items.food_status_note: Glutamine is one of the most abundant amino acids in ordinary dietary protein, so any protein-containing meal supplies it. One caveat governs every number below: USDA composition tables report 'glutamic acid', which after the acid hydrolysis used in amino acid analysis is the sum of glutamate and glutamine, because glutamine is converted to glutamate during hydrolysis. The figures are therefore the combined Glu plus Gln pool, and the glutamine share of that pool is roughly half in most animal proteins. Treat the values as an upper bound on glutamine content.
items.dose_from_food_note: The trial dose is 5 g three times daily, 15 g/day for 8 weeks, in post-infectious diarrhoea-predominant IBS with increased intestinal permeability (Zhou et al., Gut 2019;68:996-1002, PMID 30108163). On the combined Glu plus Gln figures, 15 g comes from about 50-60 g of vital wheat gluten, about 79-88 g of soy protein isolate, about 183 g of parmesan, about 323 g of cooked chicken breast, about 440 g of cod (about 2.5 fillets), about 450 g of natto (corrected from the submission's 865 g, which was wrong by 1.9x) or roughly 1.1 kg of cooked lentils. Correcting for the fact that only about half that pool is glutamine, matching 15 g of glutamine specifically needs roughly double: about 100-120 g of vital wheat gluten a day, or 600-700 g of cooked chicken breast. The baseline matters more than the ceiling. Glutamine is roughly 4-8% of food protein, so a diet supplying 80-100 g of protein delivers about 4-7 g/day, consistent with the conventional 3-6 g/day estimate. A 15 g/day supplement is therefore a three- to four-fold increase over habitual intake, not the doubling the submission claimed, which makes this a moderate gap rather than a small one. It is still nothing like creatine or NMN, where food cannot get close.

items.form_caveat: The difference is in the delivery rather than the amount. The trial gave 5 g of free crystalline L-glutamine three times a day on an empty-stomach schedule, producing a sharp luminal and plasma bolus; dietary glutamine arrives protein-bound, released slowly by digestion, and a large fraction is consumed by the enterocytes themselves on first pass. Whether the clinical effect depends on that bolus pattern has not been tested against a food-protein comparator, so 'just eat more protein' remains plausible and unproven. Two practical points: free glutamine is heat-labile and degrades in aqueous solution, so cooking and storage reduce free glutamine in food while leaving protein-bound glutamine intact; and glutamine supplementation is not risk-free in everyone, since it is a nitrogen donor and high doses warrant caution in hepatic or renal impairment, whereas the same amount arriving as ordinary food protein raises no comparable concern.
items.bioavailability: Absorbed as free amino acid and as di- and tripeptides, then extensively extracted by the small intestinal mucosa on first pass, which is the mechanistic argument for a gut-directed effect and also the reason plasma appearance underestimates delivery to the target tissue. Because USDA reports Glu and Gln as one pooled value, no composition table can give the true glutamine content of a food, and any per-food glutamine figure quoted to two decimal places should be treated with suspicion. In the trial, the measured mechanism was normalisation of an elevated urinary lactulose/mannitol ratio, so the endpoint was permeability rather than amino acid status; a food equivalent would have to reproduce the permeability effect, which has not been shown.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. Every USDA per-100 g glutamic acid value and every per-portion calculation in the original list was re-verified and stands. The weaknesses are structural and additive: the Glu plus Gln pooling means no table reports glutamine itself, the two densest rows (vital wheat gluten, soy protein isolate) are calculations from protein content and a literature glutamate fraction rather than direct composition records, and the corrected habitual baseline of 4-7 g/day rests on the conventional 3-6 g/day estimate rather than a measured survey.
corrections_applied: Corrected the habitual glutamine baseline from 8-12 g/day to about 4-7 g/day (90 g protein at glutamine's 4-8% share; conventional estimate 3-6 g/day), which converts the supplement from a doubling to a three- to four-fold increase and the entry's conclusion from a small gap to a moderate one.
Corrected the natto equivalent from 865 g to about 450 g (15/0.03337).
Deleted the false claim that parmesan is the densest ordinary food source and reframed it as the densest ordinary animal-food source.

Added vital wheat gluten (roughly 25-30 g Glu + Gln per 100 g) at the top of the list and soy protein isolate (roughly 17-19 g), both flagged as derived rather than directly measured, and added the 50-60 g gluten equivalent for a 15 g dose.
Reordered all rows by Glu + Gln per realistic portion.
Changed dose_from_food to PARTIAL to match the corrected baseline, keeping the food-route amounts explicit both on the pooled figure and after halving for glutamine specifically.

items.food_status_note: This item bundles two manufactured preparations with different answers, and the single SYNTHETIC code fits the products rather than the activities. Lactase: graded on the product it is SYNTHETIC, a microbial beta-galactosidase produced by fermentation of Aspergillus oryzae, A. niger or the yeast Kluyveromyces lactis and then purified, and the mammalian brush-border lactase it substitutes for is a membrane enzyme of the small intestinal epithelium present in no food; graded on the enzyme activity it is TRACE, because live yoghurt and kefir cultures carry microbial beta-galactosidase into the gut, which is why lactase-non-persistent people tolerate fermented dairy better than milk. Pancreatic enzyme replacement: NOT_FOOD. Pancreatin and pancrelipase are extracts of porcine pancreas glands, and the source review states that the preparations with demonstrated efficacy are porcine-derived (de la Iglesia et al., eClinicalMedicine 2026;94:103880, PMID 42011215). The nearest food is pancreas eaten as offal (sweetbread), which is not a realistic route.
items.dose_from_food_note: Pancreatic enzymes: absolute. Recommended dosing is a minimum of 40,000-50,000 units of lipase with main meals and 20,000-25,000 with snacks, taken with every meal for life (PMID 42011215). No food supplies active lipase in those quantities. Raw pancreas is the only tissue that contains the enzymes at all, it is not eaten raw in any normal diet, cooking denatures them, the delivered activity would be unmeasurable and uncontrolled, and without enteric protection gastric acid would destroy most of what survived. Lactase: there is one genuine partial route, since live yoghurt and kefir carry microbial beta-galactosidase into the gut, but that only handles the lactose in the fermented product itself and does not give a dose-adjustable enzyme to take with an arbitrary lactose-containing meal, which is the point of a lactase capsule. No peer-reviewed per-100 g beta-galactosidase activity figure for retail yoghurt was retrieved here, so no number is given; that is a sourcing gap in this dataset rather than an absence in the literature.
items.form_caveat: For pancreatin the caveats are pharmaceutical rather than dietary. Dose must be titrated to steatorrhoea, meal fat content and disease severity; the enzymes must be enteric-coated to survive gastric acid; the capsules are taken during the meal rather than before or after; and the porcine origin is a real issue for vegetarian, vegan, Muslim and Jewish patients and should be disclosed. Nothing sold as a plant-based or vegan pancreatic enzyme has demonstrated equivalence for pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, and treating a diagnosed insufficiency with a supermarket digestive enzyme blend risks continued fat malabsorption, weight loss and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency. For lactase the honest framing is that this is a targeted, cheap, low-risk aid rather than a nutrient: the alternative food strategy of hard cheese, live yoghurt and small lactose doses spread through the day works for many people, and lactase capsules matter mainly when the meal is unavoidable and the lactose dose is large.
items.bioavailability: Both are enzymes, so bioavailability means surviving intact and active to the site of action rather than being absorbed. Lactase works in the lumen of the upper small intestine and is itself digested, so timing relative to the lactose load determines the effect. Pancreatic lipase is irreversibly denatured below about pH 4, which is why uncoated pancreatin is largely wasted, why the field has moved to pH-sensitive enteric microspheres, and why an emerging approach adds bicarbonate to raise local pH around the pancreatin. Coadministered acid suppression is sometimes needed to make the enzymes work at all. None of this can be replicated by eating anything.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The PERT dosing figures and the porcine origin were confirmed against the cited review (PMID 42011215), and the manufacturing routes for microbial lactase are standard and uncontested. The lactase side is weaker: the fermented-dairy beta-galactosidase route is well established qualitatively but no per-100 g activity figure for retail yoghurt was retrieved, so the partial food route cannot be quantified or compared against a capsule dose.
corrections_applied: Split the bundled classification: stated that pancreatin is NOT_FOOD (porcine pancreas gland extract) while lactase is SYNTHETIC as a product and TRACE if graded on enzyme activity, resolving the contradiction between the SYNTHETIC label and the entry's own concession about live yoghurt and kefir.
Moved the fermented-dairy beta-galactosidase route out of the dose-gap narrative and into the food_status field, where the availability question is answered.
Split the dose_from_food prose so pancreatin (absolute gap) and lactase (partial, not dose-adjustable) each get their own statement rather than being averaged.
Labelled the missing yoghurt beta-galactosidase activity figure as a sourcing gap in this dataset rather than an absence in the literature.

items.food_status_note: Reclassified from NOT_FOOD, which was too strong and was contradicted by this entry's own form caveat. The plant proteases do occur in ordinary food: fruit bromelain is present in edible pineapple flesh and juice with real proteolytic activity, which is exactly why fresh pineapple stops gelatin setting and canned does not; papain occurs in unripe papaya flesh as well as in the latex that is the commercial source; and actinidin, a cysteine protease, is present in ordinary edible ripe green kiwifruit, with human data comparing green (actinidin-containing) against gold (actinidin-free) kiwifruit for gastric protein digestion. Ginger (zingibain), fig latex (ficin), malted barley (diastatic amylase) and raw honey (diastase) are further real dietary enzyme sources. What remains genuinely NOT_FOOD is the other half of these blends: the amylase, protease, lipase and lactase components are Aspergillus or yeast fermentation products with no dietary presence. TRACE rather than PARTIAL because the activity in edible flesh is present without any confirmed quantification, and the parts carrying the measured activity are not eaten.
items.dose_from_food_note: Bromelain supplements are dosed by activity, typically 500-2,000 mg of a preparation standardised to around 2,400 GDU/g, giving roughly 1,200-4,800 GDU per dose. On the activities reported for pineapple by-products, that is equivalent to about 0.41-1.65 g of basal stem or about 1.0-4.1 g of peel, and neither the basal stem nor the peel is eaten (those per-gram activity values are from a genuine, on-topic paper whose individual figures could not be retrieved, so treat them as unconfirmed). Expressed against food you would actually put in your mouth, the dose cannot be matched: the crown has no detectable activity, the core is usually discarded, and no sourced activity figure exists for the ripe flesh. Fresh pineapple and green kiwifruit do deliver active protease into the stomach, so the effect is not zero, but with no confirmed activity value for edible flesh there is no way to express a food equivalent of a GDU dose. For papain the source material is the latex of the unripe fruit, which is irritant and is not food. For the fungal amylase, protease and lipase components there is no food source at all.

foods.per_100g: contains actinidin, a cysteine protease; no per-100 g activity figure was retrieved in this pass
foods.per_portion: proteolytic activity present but unquantified here
foods.pct_rda_or_dose: not expressible against a GDU-standardised bromelain dose; the units and the enzyme differ and no activity value for the flesh was confirmed
foods.source: Human crossover data in healthy older adults compared green (actinidin-containing) against gold (actinidin-free) kiwifruit with beef meals for gastric protein digestion, with supporting in vitro work at gastric pH, as summarised in the verification report; no specific citation or activity value retrieved here, so the row is qualitative. This is the clearest food route for a swallowed protease and it is why the NOT_FOOD grade was withdrawn.

foods.per_100g: contains fruit bromelain (pI 4.6, distinct from stem bromelain at pI 9.5); no proteolytic activity value for the eaten flesh was retrieved in this pass
foods.per_portion: proteolytic activity present but unquantified here
foods.pct_rda_or_dose: not expressible; the measured GDU/g values in the literature belong to basal stem, peel and core rather than to flesh
foods.source: USDA FDC 169124 records the edible fruit but carries no enzyme activity value. Isoform distinction from the bromelain literature (DOI 10.3390/foods13040589). The absence of a flesh activity figure is a sourcing gap here rather than an absence in the literature.

items.form_caveat: The whole food is safe and the concentrate is not always. Fresh pineapple and papaya are ordinary fruit; concentrated bromelain has anticoagulant and antiplatelet activity and interacts with warfarin and antiplatelet drugs, and papain and chymopapain are recognised respiratory and contact allergens, which EFSA flags in its allergenicity assessments of the food enzyme (the specific identifier cited in the submission, DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2026.9950, could not be confirmed; EFSA does publish opinions on papain from papaya latex, so the substance of the point stands while that reference does not). The matrix also destroys the premise: these are proteins, so heat and gastric acid inactivate them. Canned and cooked pineapple has no meaningful proteolytic activity left, which is why canned pineapple does not stop gelatin setting while fresh pineapple does, and any orally swallowed enzyme without enteric protection meets pepsin and pH 2 before reaching the small intestine. The most important caveat is scope: these blends are not equivalent to pancreatic enzyme replacement and must not be substituted for it in diagnosed pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, where the requirement is 40,000-50,000 lipase units per meal in an enteric-coated porcine preparation (PMID 42011215). Nor is the plant-derived lactase in a blend interchangeable with a dose-standardised lactase product.
items.bioavailability: Enzymes are not absorbed and do not need to be; they act in the lumen, so what matters is surviving to the right pH and place. Stem bromelain and fruit bromelain differ even in isoelectric point (pI 9.5 against 4.6), which is why extraction pH determines which enzyme you actually get and why 'bromelain' on a label does not identify a single molecule. Activity rather than milligrams is the meaningful unit, and GDU, CDU, FIP and USP units are not interconvertible, so a milligram figure on a bottle says almost nothing about what it will do. Both bromelain and papain are irreversibly denatured by cooking and largely by gastric acid unless enterically protected, so an uncoated capsule and a bowl of fresh pineapple share the same delivery problem.
items.data_confidence: LOW. The quantitative core of this entry could not be verified. The pineapple by-product activities (2,909 GDU/g basal stem, 1,179 GDU/g peel, 694 GDU/g core, crown below detection) come from a genuine and on-topic paper (PMID 38397568) whose individual values were not retrieved, and every dose equivalence derives from them. The EFSA papain identifier could not be confirmed. The two food rows are qualitative because no activity figure for edible pineapple flesh or kiwifruit was retrieved. Only the supplement-side arithmetic (1,200-4,800 GDU per dose) and the bromelain isoform biochemistry check out.
corrections_applied: Reclassified from NOT_FOOD to TRACE and split the prose: fruit bromelain in edible pineapple flesh, papain in unripe papaya flesh and actinidin in green kiwifruit are real dietary proteases, while the fungal amylase, protease, lipase and lactase components remain NOT_FOOD.

Added kiwifruit (actinidin) and raw pineapple flesh as food rows, both qualitative because no confirmed activity figure exists for edible flesh; noted ginger, fig latex, malted barley and raw honey as further dietary enzyme sources.
Flagged the pineapple by-product GDU/g values as unconfirmed and retained the derived stem and peel equivalents only with that caveat attached.
Flagged the EFSA papain DOI as unconfirmed while keeping the allergenicity point, which does not depend on that identifier.
Reframed 'no proteolytic activity figure exists for the eaten flesh' as a sourcing gap in this dataset rather than an absence in the literature.
Set data_confidence to LOW because the entry's dose arithmetic rests entirely on values the verification pass could not trace.

items.food_status_note_zh: 洋车前子壳本身就是食品原料，是卵叶车前（Plantago ovata）种皮经研磨得到的产物，所以补充剂与食物是同一种材料，没有任何提取或浓缩步骤。在普通食物里，能与之对应的黏性成胶纤维是燕麦和大麦的 β-葡聚糖（beta-glucan），以及亚麻籽粉和奇亚籽的黏质；魔芋葡甘聚糖和瓜尔胶同样作为食品出售，黏度还要更高，但本次没有可确认的每份含量数据。豆类不属于同一类，已从该说法中删去：其可溶性纤维为 0.41-1.36 g/100 g，并且按本条自己的生物利用度部分所述，它在近端结肠发酵，在相同克数摄入下表现完全不同。β-葡聚糖在化学上也与洋车前子的阿拉伯木聚糖凝胶不同。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 在基层医疗 IBS 研究中优于安慰剂的 10 g/day 壳粉剂量（Bijkerk 2009, BMJ 339:b3154, PMID 19713235）大约是一满汤匙作为食品出售的产品，9 g 壳粉本身已提供 6.0 g 可溶性纤维，所以对洋车前子而言差距为零。用其他普通食物凑出这 6-7 g 可溶性纤维是另一回事：按 0.42 g/100 g 计算需要约 1.6 kg 煮好的燕麦粥（约 6.8 杯），罐装红腰豆按 1.36 g/100 g 计算需要约 493 g，即按每杯 177 g 折算的 2.8 杯（原稿写 3 杯，已更正）。这两个可溶性纤维分项都来自同一份无法调取的研究表格，因此这些千克级数字只能视为指示性。另一个更容易达到的目标是每天 3 g 燕麦或大麦 β-葡聚糖（beta-glucan），单靠吃就能实现：按 4-4.5% w/w 计约 67-75 g 干燕麦片，按 5.5-8% 计约 40-55 g 燕麦麸，或按 4% 计约 75 g 大麦。原稿写 40-50 g 干燕麦，是把燕麦麸水平的百分比套到整燕麦上，已更正。
items.form_caveat_zh: 洋车前子壳是未加工的植物材料，因此不存在提取物与食物之别的问题，但有三个真实的注意点。物理层面：服用时必须配一整杯液体，干吞成胶剂量可能堵塞食管或肠道。成分层面：标签上的“可溶性纤维”并非单一物质。洋车前子的阿拉伯木聚糖凝胶黏度高、难发酵，而菊粉挂着同样的可溶性纤维标签，却发酵快并产气，这与 IBS 患者的需求正好相反，按克数等量替换是个错误。加工层面：燕麦 β-葡聚糖（beta-glucan）的获益跟随黏度，而黏度取决于分子量，研磨、挤压膨化和长时间加热都会使其降解，所以标签克数相同的深加工燕麦产品并不等同于整粒燕麦片。
items.bioavailability_zh: 这里的物质都不被吸收，所以生物利用度指的是黏度、持水能力和可发酵性。洋车前子在整个结肠都能持水且产气量低，这是它对便秘和腹泻都有帮助的原因；豆类可溶性纤维和菊粉主要在近端结肠被发酵，在相同克数摄入下表现相差很大。分析方法是混乱的真实来源：AOAC 991.43 重量法测得的可溶性纤维值系统性高于英国食物成分表采用的酶化学法（Englyst/NSP）值，所以不同表格的可溶性纤维数字不应混用。头对头证据支持纤维类别之间的区分：同为 10 g 剂量，洋车前子在第一个月和第二个月均优于安慰剂，小麦麸则没有（PMID 19713235）。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。USDA 的总纤维值（燕麦麸 15.4，大麦 3.8）和 Bijkerk 试验细节已确认。仍有两处薄弱：洋车前子的主打成分数据依赖一份品牌厂家标签记录，而该记录自身的总纤维字段读数为 0 g；燕麦粥和豆类的所有可溶/不可溶分项都来自一份无法调取的 2002 年表格。新增的亚麻籽和奇亚籽数字取自核查报告自己给出的范围，并非可追溯的成分记录。

items.supplement: Wheat bran and insoluble fibre supplements for IBS
items.supplement_zh: 小麦麸与用于 IBS 的不可溶性纤维补充剂
items.food_status_note_zh: 小麦麸是食物，作为普通研磨谷物分层出售，每 100 g 含总膳食纤维 42.8 g（USDA FDC 169722），属于纤维密度最高的普通谷物分层之一。原稿称它是任何成分表中纤维最密集的食物之一，这一说法不成立，已删除：玉米麸 79 g/100 g 在约 4,000 种 USDA 食物中排第一，接近小麦麸的两倍，洋车前子壳约为 78 g/100 g。RICH 的判定专门适用于谷物麸皮类补充剂，因为只有这一类存在食物对照：小麦麸、玉米麸、米糠。另一类常见的不可溶性纤维补充剂基料，即粉状或微晶纤维素与甲基纤维素，属于人造材料，没有膳食对应物，RICH 等级不延伸到它们。这一产品类别的问题与可得性无关，问题出在适应证上。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 在 IBS 中与洋车前子和安慰剂对照的 10 g/day 麸皮（PMID 19713235）大约是 3 满汤匙普通小麦麸，含 4.28 g 膳食纤维。按纤维匹配，这相当于约 1 份麸皮薄片，原稿说的 2 份是错的：一份 29 g 提供 4.90 g，两份的纤维量超过试验剂量的两倍。一杯粗麸皮（58 g）按质量计是试验剂量的 5.8 倍。达到这个量不需要任何补充剂。试验的发现是达到了也没用：第一、二个月麸皮不优于安慰剂，第三个月的优势在最差情况分析下不成立，而且麸皮组的早期退出率最高，原因是 IBS 症状加重。一篇小麦麸文献综述得出同样结论，并引用官方指南指出不应向 IBS 患者推荐小麦麸（DOI 10.3109/09637486.2012.687366）。
items.form_caveat_zh: 食物本身安全且有用，问题在于补充剂的适应证。小麦麸确实是有效的粪便增容剂，每摄入 1 g 麸皮可使粪便增加约 5 g，处于公认 3-5.4 g 区间的上端（DOI 10.3109/09637486.2012.687366），对普通便秘和整体纤维摄入是合理的食物。在 IBS 中它常加重胀气、腹胀和疼痛，患者退出最多的正是这一组。一个不太明显的注意点：小麦麸带有果聚糖（白小麦面粉测得 0.75 g 果聚糖/100 g，DOI 10.3389/fnut.2024.1446771），所以加大麸皮摄入也会在最难耐受的那部分患者身上提高 FODMAP 摄入量。以“IBS 纤维”名义出售的不可溶性纤维补充剂推销的是错误的纤维类别，IBS 的证据支持的是黏性、难发酵的那一类。
items.bioavailability_zh: 不被吸收。机制是机械增容加上阿拉伯木聚糖与纤维素的持水作用，麸皮的非淀粉多糖组成为 70% 阿拉伯木聚糖、24% 纤维素和 6% β-葡聚糖（beta-glucan）（Stevenson et al., PMID 22716911，引文已核实）。麸皮加快小肠通过速度，并以剂量依赖方式增加粪便重量。颗粒大小比总克数更重要，粗麸皮既增容也造成刺激，细磨麸皮则丧失大部分效果，所以纤维标签相同的两种产品并不能互换。每 100 g 中只有 1.5-4.0 g 是可溶的，所以人们常以为纤维能带来的降胆固醇、控血糖和改善粪便质地的黏胶效应，麸皮几乎没有贡献。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。小麦相关的核心数值已对照 USDA legacy 记录确认（小麦麸 42.8，全麦面包 6.0，全麦面粉 10.7），Stevenson 的 NSP 组成拆分和 Bijkerk 试验叙述同样已确认。薄弱处：麸皮薄片的 FDC ID 无法确定，全麦面包的每片重量未获确认，玉米麸、米糠和全麸谷物的数字来自核查报告汇编的数值，份量重量为常规值而非取自来源记录。

items.supplement_zh: 益生元：菊粉、低聚果糖（FOS）、低聚半乳糖（GOS）
items.food_status_note_zh: 本条把三种物质打包在一起，而答案有两种。菊粉和低聚果糖（FOS）为 RICH：菊苣根按鲜重 15-20 g/100 g，洋姜约 8-22 g，蒜约 9-16 g，洋葱约 2 g，朝鲜蓟、红葱头、婆罗门参（salsify）、韭葱、芦笋、香蕉、小麦和黑麦中含量较少。β-低聚半乳糖（GOS）属于 SYNTHETIC，不应归在同一标题下：试验所用的 beta-GOS 由乳糖经酶法转半乳糖苷化制造，在普通食物中没有实质存在。豆类中确实存在的半乳寡糖是 α-半乳糖苷（棉子糖、水苏糖、毛蕊花糖），化学上属于另一族，作用的细菌靶标也不同。果聚糖这一类的习惯膳食摄入量偏低：斯洛文尼亚一项调查的均值为 1.6-1.7 g/day（DOI 10.3389/fnut.2024.1446771），英国学龄儿童菊粉摄入中位数为 1.3 g/day（PMID 40808333）。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 对菊粉和 FOS 来说，答案取决于选哪种食物。5 g/day 的剂量可以由约 250 g 生洋葱（两到三个中等大小洋葱）、按更正后的 9-16 g/100 g 范围计约 10-19 瓣蒜（原稿的 30 瓣偏差约 3 倍，并与其自己的食物行自相矛盾）、约 23-63 g 洋姜，或按一个未确认数值计约 30 g 婆罗门参达到。靠香蕉（约 4.5 kg）、韭葱（约 2.1 kg）和芦笋（约 1-5 kg，区间反映鲜重数值存在五倍不确定性；原稿写死 5 kg，只用了低端值）则达不到。比剂量更有用的数字是耐受上限：一项随机交叉试验中，天然菊粉每天最多 10 g、低聚果糖每天最多 5 g 耐受良好，而 10 g 低聚果糖显著加重症状，主要是排气，其次是腹胀（Bonnema et al., PMID 20497775）。一杯 150 g 洋姜提供约 12-33 g 菊粉，一顿就相当于每日耐受上限的一到三倍。对 GOS 的答案是明确的否：试验所用的 beta-GOS 剂量由工业制造，没有任何普通食物能提供。
items.form_caveat_zh: 菊苣根是教科书式的经典答案，也是个糟糕的推荐：它是菊粉的工业来源，通常烘烤后当咖啡替代品，并不作蔬菜食用，因此 15-20 g/100 g 这个亮眼数字不构成膳食途径。作为蔬菜食用的蒲公英叶，以及牛蒡根和雪莲果，是公认的高菊粉食物，可以回应这一质疑，但此处没有它们的可确认数据。菊苣还说明了纤维表与果聚糖测定为何会互相矛盾：USDA 把菊苣根列为每 100 g 仅 1.5 g 总膳食纤维（FDC 169993）。纯化菊粉和低聚果糖作为食品配料是安全的，引起症状的是浓度：同一种分子分散在一天的蔬菜里毫不起眼，一次性 10 g 冲击剂量却会引发排气和腹胀（PMID 20497775）。Briet et al.（PMID 7588500）报告了 FOS 的症状阶梯（每天超过 30 g 出现排气过多，超过 40 g 出现肠鸣和腹胀，50 g 时出现痉挛和腹泻，长期给药不产生耐受）；该引文本身正确且切题，但这些具体阈值无法从全文中调取，属未确认。反向的注意点具有临床意义：多吃益生元蔬菜的清单（洋葱、蒜、韭葱、朝鲜蓟、洋姜、小麦、黑麦）正是低 FODMAP 饮食要剔除的清单，所以在 IBS 中，食物途径和补充剂途径都有可能让情况变糟。最后，不要把豆类的 α-GOS 当作补充剂 beta-GOS 的食物形式；已报道的 Phaseolus vulgaris 含量（棉子糖 0.8-7.4 mg/g，水苏糖 20.0-30.9 mg/g，毛蕊花糖 0.3-1.3 mg/g，DOI 10.3390/foods15020391）出自一篇真实且切题的论文，但其中的单项数值无法确认，而且它们是不同的分子，有自己的产气特征。
items.bioavailability_zh: 果聚糖完全不被吸收，因此变量是在哪里发酵、发酵有多快，而这由链长决定。低聚果糖（DP 2-8）在近端快速发酵，这是它在同一试验中耐受剂量只有长链天然菊粉一半的原因，5 g 对 10 g（PMID 20497775）。测定方法和植物部位同样左右数字：某国家级调查用 AOAC 999.03 测得洋葱 1.97 g/100 g、韭葱 0.24 g/100 g（DOI 10.3389/fnut.2024.1446771），而澳大利亚一项使用 Megazyme 测定法的调查报告，包括韭葱鳞茎在内的高果聚糖葱属食物为 1.2-17.4 g/100 g（PMID 17625872）。储藏也有影响，洋葱储藏期间果聚糖会解聚。单一数字应当读作指示性数值，而非精确值。GOS 的发酵方式类似，但它是另一种底物：beta-GOS 与豆类 α-半乳糖苷不能互换。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。Ferjancic 的果聚糖数值（洋葱、韭葱、香蕉、面包、面粉）和 Bonnema 的耐受阈值已逐字核实，菊苣 15-20 g 菊粉与 USDA 1.5 g 纤维记录之间的反差也成立。另一面：蒜的数字原为来源误读，现更正为较宽的 9-16 g/100 g 范围；洋姜跨 8-22 g/100 g；芦笋鲜重值存在五倍不确定性；Briet 的症状阶梯和 Phaseolus 寡糖数值无法确认；新增的三种食物（婆罗门参、朝鲜蓟、红葱头）依据的是类别层面的范围，而非单一食物的实测值。

items.food_status_note_zh: 此处 SYNTHETIC 的含义是没有膳食来源。它并非人工合成的分子：一个指名益生菌菌株是活的生物体，是保藏在菌种库里的单一克隆分离株，在工业发酵罐中培养、冻干并装囊。没有任何食物含有它。发酵食品确实携带大量活的乳酸菌，但其中的菌种和菌株是能在该食物及其发酵剂中生长的那些微生物，从来不是保藏的试验菌株。由于益生菌的疗效是逐一菌株验证的，提供同一菌种不同菌株的食物属于另一种产品。发酵食品的活菌载量列在通用多菌株条目下。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 这个差距是类别性的，任何食物量都无法弥合。试验中指名菌株的剂量大致为 1x10^8 至 1x10^10 CFU/day；Bifidobacterium longum 35624（原归类为 infantis）在 1x10^8 有效，而原始试验把这个数字表述为 CFU/mL 而非 CFU/day（PMID 16863564）。一杯 2.5x10^8 CFU/mL 的开菲尔提供约 6x10^10 个活乳酸菌（DOI 10.3390/foods15101616），所以单看 CFU 总数，食物轻松超过。这些菌体中属于受试菌株的比例为零，这使得 CFU 比较对于菌株特异性的主张毫无意义。
items.form_caveat_zh: 这是本组中最重要的剂型注意点。益生菌的临床证据是菌株特异的，往往还叠加配方特异和适应证特异。酸奶、开菲尔、德式酸菜、韩式泡菜、味噌、纳豆和天贝都不含试验所用的菌株，所以用指名菌株得到的证据无法转移到任何发酵食品，也无法转移到同一菌种的另一个菌株。吃发酵食品是合理的饮食习惯，本身有正在积累的证据基础，这与为特定临床效果按确定剂量服用指名菌株是两件事。两个实用要点：加热会杀死这些微生物，因此经巴氏杀菌或加热烹调的发酵物（罐装德式酸菜、拌入沸汤的味噌、烤过的天贝）不提供活菌；补充剂上只标到菌种层面，例如“含嗜酸乳杆菌（Lactobacillus acidophilus）”而无菌株编号，其证据可转移性与食物无异。
items.bioavailability_zh: 对胃酸和胆汁的存活取决于菌株，递送基质也会改变它：乳制品的脂肪和缓冲能力使存活率优于裸胶囊，补充剂则用肠溶包衣或微囊化达到同样目的。剂量效应并非单调递增，这是配方与 CFU 数同等重要的最清晰证据。在一项纳入 362 例基层医疗 IBS 患者的剂量探索试验中，B. infantis 35624 在 1x10^8 显著优于安慰剂及其他所有剂量，1x10^6 和 1x10^10 则没有；论文把最高剂量失效归因于明显的配方问题（Whorwell et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2006;101:1581-1590, PMID 16863564）。原稿漏掉了两条外推性注意点：试验只纳入女性，论文中的剂量以 CFU/mL 而非 CFU/day 表述。因此标签 CFU 越高并不意味着越好，出厂时的标签 CFU 也不等于保质期末的活菌 CFU。
items.data_confidence_zh: 高。该主张是类别性的（没有食物含有保藏的试验菌株），支持性试验已核实：362 例患者，剂量为 1x10^6、1x10^8 和 1x10^10，其中 1x10^8 组显著优于安慰剂和其他所有剂量。唯一未通过核实的细节，即最高剂量的成胶机制，已删除并改用论文自身的表述。

items.supplement_zh: 通用多菌株益生菌复配产品
items.food_status_note_zh: RICH 只针对一个终点，而且是被重新定义过的终点：常见属的活乳酸菌。在这个终点上，若干普通发酵食品达到或超过补充剂的标签剂量，调查中酸奶最高达 10^9 CFU/g，开菲尔 2.5x10^8 CFU/mL，未经巴氏杀菌的德式酸菜约 2x10^8 CFU/g，韩式泡菜 10^7.14 至 10^9.23 CFU/g，纳豆据报约 10^8-10^9 CFU/g。而对产品主张真正重要的终点，即以确定剂量提供一组已表征菌株的确定配方，没有任何食物能提供，诚实的评级应当是明确的否。浏览本字段的读者不应把 RICH 读成食物可以替代这个产品。同一组中的指名菌株条目已指出，CFU 比较对菌株特异性主张毫无意义，这一点在此同样成立。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 就活菌总数而言不存在差距。原综述估算，可能影响菌群所需的摄入量约为 10^10 个菌体，而 100 g 含 10^8 菌体/g 的食物即可达到（PMID 30197628）。一杯开菲尔、一杯酸奶、约 120 g 生德式酸菜、一杯韩式泡菜或一杯纳豆都能越过这条线，处于实测区间上端的韩式泡菜一份提供的活菌数超过大多数标称 50 billion CFU 的胶囊。差距是定性的：身份、表征和一致性。发酵食品的菌数在不同产品和批次之间跨越四到六个数量级（酸奶从低于 10^4 到 10^9 CFU/g），其中的微生物通常没有鉴定到菌株层面，而且没有一个是复配产品标签上的菌株。
items.form_caveat_zh: 吃发酵食品是合理的饮食习惯，与按确定剂量服用指名菌株是两个不同的命题。即便是通用复配产品，也会告诉你拿到的是哪些菌种、大致多少数量；一罐德式酸菜两者都不告诉你，而经巴氏杀菌的罐装品根本没有活菌。决定一种食物是否真能提供活菌的实用要点：标签必须写生、未经巴氏杀菌或含活性菌种，并且全程冷藏；加热会破坏这些微生物，因此加进沸汤的味噌、炒熟的韩式泡菜和烤过的天贝基本没有贡献；长期陈化的奶酪可能比年轻奶酪低几个数量级。水开菲尔、康普茶、盐水发酵未杀菌腌菜、kvass 酸面包饮、skyr 酸奶、传统白脱牛奶和年轻生乳奶酪属于同一清单，但此处没有它们的可确认菌数。反过来说，如果菌株没有具名，补充剂标称 50 billion CFU 也说明不了什么，因为益生菌效应是逐一菌株验证的，而标签上的 CFU 数指的是出厂时而非保质期末。
items.bioavailability_zh: 在胃酸和胆汁中的存活既取决于菌株，也取决于基质。发酵乳制品能缓冲胃酸，其脂肪含量提高通过消化道的存活率，这是食物途径相对无包衣胶囊的真实优势；补充剂则用肠溶包衣或微囊化来弥补。这些微生物几乎都不会长期定植，所以效应是剂量依赖的，停止摄入即终止，这一点对食物和胶囊同样适用。原综述指出，许多发酵微生物与益生菌生物在亲缘上很近，可能共享作用机制，这是推荐发酵食品的诚实依据，但亲缘接近并不等于等效，也不允许把菌株特异的试验结果搬到一罐韩式泡菜上。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。Rezac 关于韩式泡菜、德式酸菜、酸奶、味噌和天贝的菌数已对照表 5 和表 6 核实，开菲尔菌数和 10^10 菌体阈值同样已核实。仍有两处软点：天贝 9 log 的上限找不到来源，已删除；纳豆菌数是核查报告给出的文献范围，没有可调取的引文。

items.food_status_note_zh: 此处 SYNTHETIC 的含义是没有膳食来源，它并非人工合成的分子。该菌株是活的生物体，分离自一名健康人类供体的回肠黏膜，此后已从 Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis 重新归类为 B. longum subsp. longum 35624（PLOS One 2016;11:e0162983, PMC5033381）。它从专有菌种库出发进行工业扩繁并冻干。任何食物、任何发酵食品、任何其他品牌的补充剂中都不存在它。比较基因组分析发现了一个 35624 特有的基因簇，编码其胞外多糖 EPS624 的生物合成，这类菌株层面的差异使替换缺乏依据。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 任何食物的任何摄入量都无法提供这个菌株。试验剂量在绝对值上很小，1x10^8 CFU，大致相当于 8.3 log CFU/g 的未杀菌德式酸菜半克中的活菌数，所以障碍与剂量无关，障碍在于身份。发酵食品能提供比 35624 有效剂量多一千倍的活菌，却一个 35624 都提供不了。请注意，原始试验把剂量表述为 CFU/mL 而非 CFU/day。
items.form_caveat_zh: 剂量反应数据比任何关于食物的论证都更能说明问题。在那项 362 例的剂量探索试验中，1x10^8 的 B. infantis 35624 在腹痛、复合评分、腹胀、排便功能障碍和排便不尽感上显著优于安慰剂，1x10^6 和 1x10^10 则没有，论文把最高剂量失效归因于明显的配方问题（Whorwell et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2006;101:1581-1590, PMID 16863564）。试验只纳入女性，这限制了外推，原稿没有说明。既然同一胶囊中同一菌株的剂量变动十倍就能让效应消失，那么把菌株换成酸奶里的另一种双歧杆菌，就不能假定效应还在。凡被建议服用 35624 的人都应被明确告知：没有任何饮食能复制它，通用双歧杆菌补充剂是另一种产品。
items.bioavailability_zh: 选择该菌株的部分理由是它能在胃肠道转运中存活，其有记录的作用属于免疫调节和屏障相关，与营养无关：增强肠道屏障功能、加快肠道转运、降低内脏高敏感性。它不会长期定植，所以效应依赖每天持续摄入。配方主导递送：1x10^10 组的失败是配方问题，并不构成反对高菌数的证据，它说明标签上的 CFU 单独并不是起作用的变量。原稿给出的那个具体成胶机制在来源文献中没有，已删除。
items.data_confidence_zh: 高。菌株来源、重新归类、胞外多糖基因簇和剂量探索试验结果均已确认。唯一未通过核实的细节是成胶机制，现已改用论文自身的表述；唯一的新增内容是只纳入女性这一点和 CFU/mL 单位。

items.supplement_zh: L-谷氨酰胺用于肠道修复
items.food_status_note_zh: 谷氨酰胺是普通膳食蛋白中含量最高的氨基酸之一，任何含蛋白的一餐都能提供。下面每一个数字都受一条限定条件约束：USDA 成分表报告的是“谷氨酸”，在氨基酸分析所用的酸水解之后，这个值是谷氨酸与谷氨酰胺之和，因为谷氨酰胺在水解过程中被转化为谷氨酸。因此这些数字是 Glu 加 Gln 的合并池，在多数动物蛋白中谷氨酰胺约占该池的一半。请把这些数值当作谷氨酰胺含量的上限。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 试验剂量为每次 5 g、每天三次，即 15 g/day，持续 8 周，用于伴肠道通透性升高的感染后腹泻型 IBS（Zhou et al., Gut 2019;68:996-1002, PMID 30108163）。按 Glu 加 Gln 合并值计算，15 g 来自约 50-60 g 谷朊粉（活性小麦面筋）、约 79-88 g 大豆分离蛋白、约 183 g 帕玛森奶酪、约 323 g 熟鸡胸肉、约 440 g 鳕鱼（约 2.5 片鱼柳）、约 450 g 纳豆（原稿写 865 g，偏差 1.9 倍，已更正），或约 1.1 kg 熟扁豆。考虑到该池中只有约一半是谷氨酰胺，要专门凑够 15 g 谷氨酰胺需要大约翻倍：每天约 100-120 g 谷朊粉，或 600-700 g 熟鸡胸肉。基线比上限更值得关注。谷氨酰胺约占食物蛋白的 4-8%，因此提供 80-100 g 蛋白的饮食可提供约 4-7 g/day，与常规估计的 3-6 g/day 一致。这样看，15 g/day 的补充剂相当于把习惯摄入量提高三到四倍，原稿说的翻倍并不成立，本条的差距因此从很小改判为中等。它仍然完全不同于肌酸或 NMN，那两者靠食物根本接近不了。
items.form_caveat_zh: 差别出在递送方式上，与总量无关。试验按空腹方案每天三次给予 5 g 游离结晶 L-谷氨酰胺，在肠腔和血浆中形成陡峭的冲击峰；膳食谷氨酰胺以蛋白结合形式进入，经消化缓慢释放，其中很大一部分在首过时就被肠上皮细胞自身消耗。临床效应是否依赖这种冲击式模式，尚未用食物蛋白作对照来检验，所以“多吃点蛋白就行”这种说法仍然只是合理推测，未被证实。两个实用要点：游离谷氨酰胺不耐热，在水溶液中会降解，因此烹调和储藏会减少食物中的游离谷氨酰胺，蛋白结合的谷氨酰胺不受影响；谷氨酰胺补充并非对所有人都没有风险，它是氮供体，肝功能或肾功能受损者用高剂量需谨慎，而同样的量以普通食物蛋白形式摄入则不引起可比的担忧。
items.bioavailability_zh: 以游离氨基酸以及二肽和三肽形式被吸收，随后在首过时被小肠黏膜大量摄取，这既是肠道定向效应的机制论据，也是血浆出现量低估靶组织递送量的原因。由于 USDA 把 Glu 和 Gln 报告为一个合并值，没有任何成分表能给出食物真实的谷氨酰胺含量，凡是精确到小数点后两位的单食物谷氨酰胺数字都应存疑。在该试验中，实测的机制是尿乳果糖/甘露醇比值升高后恢复正常，所以终点是通透性，与氨基酸营养状态无关；食物等效方案必须复现这个通透性效应，而这一点尚未被证明。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。原清单中每一个 USDA 每 100 g 谷氨酸值和每一项每份计算都已重新核实并成立。薄弱之处是结构性和新增性的：Glu 加 Gln 合并意味着没有任何表格报告谷氨酰胺本身；密度最高的两行（谷朊粉、大豆分离蛋白）是由蛋白含量与文献谷氨酸占比推算的，并非直接的成分记录；更正后的习惯摄入基线 4-7 g/day 依据的是常规估计 3-6 g/day，而非实测调查。

items.food_status_note_zh: 本条把两种人工制备的产品打包在一起，而它们的答案不同，单一的 SYNTHETIC 代码适用于产品，不适用于酶活性。乳糖酶：按产品评级为 SYNTHETIC，它是由 Aspergillus oryzae、A. niger 或酵母 Kluyveromyces lactis 发酵生产并纯化的微生物 β-半乳糖苷酶，而它所替代的哺乳动物刷状缘乳糖酶是小肠上皮的膜酶，任何食物中都不存在；按酶活性评级则为 TRACE，因为活性酸奶和开菲尔的菌种会把微生物 β-半乳糖苷酶带入肠道，这也是乳糖酶非持续型人群对发酵乳制品的耐受优于牛奶的原因。胰酶替代治疗：NOT_FOOD。胰酶（pancreatin）和胰脂肪酶制剂（pancrelipase）是猪胰腺的提取物，原综述指出，已证实有效的制剂均为猪源（de la Iglesia et al., eClinicalMedicine 2026;94:103880, PMID 42011215）。最接近的食物是作为内脏食用的胰腺（sweetbread），这不是现实可行的途径。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 胰酶：差距是绝对的。推荐剂量为主餐至少 40,000-50,000 单位脂肪酶，加餐 20,000-25,000 单位，终身随每餐服用（PMID 42011215）。没有任何食物能提供这个量级的活性脂肪酶。生胰腺是唯一含有这些酶的组织，正常饮食中没有人生吃，加热会使其变性，实际送达的活性无法测量也无法控制，而且没有肠溶保护，胃酸会摧毁存活下来的大部分。乳糖酶：确实存在一条部分可行的途径，活性酸奶和开菲尔会把微生物 β-半乳糖苷酶带入肠道，但那只能处理发酵产品自身所含的乳糖，无法提供一种可按剂量调整、随任意含乳糖餐食服用的酶，而后者正是乳糖酶胶囊的用途。此处没有检索到零售酸奶每 100 g β-半乳糖苷酶活性的同行评议数据，因此不给出数字；这是本数据集的取证缺口，并不代表文献中不存在。
items.form_caveat_zh: 对胰酶来说，注意点属于药学范畴，与膳食无关。剂量必须按脂肪泻程度、餐食脂肪含量和病情严重度滴定；酶必须做肠溶包衣才能在胃酸中存活；胶囊要在进餐过程中服用，不在餐前或餐后；猪源对素食者、纯素者、穆斯林和犹太患者是真实问题，应当披露。以植物基或纯素胰酶名义出售的产品，没有一种在胰腺外分泌不足上证明了等效性；用超市卖的消化酶复配产品去治疗已确诊的胰腺外分泌不足，可能导致脂肪吸收不良持续、体重下降和脂溶性维生素缺乏。对乳糖酶，诚实的定位是一种针对性强、便宜、低风险的辅助手段，它不构成营养素。替代的饮食策略（硬质奶酪、活性酸奶，把少量乳糖分散到一天里）对很多人有效，乳糖酶胶囊主要用在无法回避且乳糖负荷较大的那一餐。
items.bioavailability_zh: 两者都是酶，因此生物利用度指的是完整且有活性地到达作用部位，与被吸收无关。乳糖酶在上段小肠腔内起作用，本身也会被消化，所以相对于乳糖负荷的服用时机决定效果。胰脂肪酶在约 pH 4 以下不可逆变性，这就是无包衣胰酶大部分被浪费的原因，也是这一领域转向 pH 敏感肠溶微球的原因，还是近年出现的在胰酶周围加碳酸氢盐以提高局部 pH 这一思路的原因。有时还需要同时使用抑酸药，酶才能起作用。这些都无法靠吃任何东西复现。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。PERT 剂量数据和猪源已对照所引综述确认（PMID 42011215），微生物乳糖酶的生产路线是标准且无争议的。乳糖酶一侧较弱：发酵乳制品的 β-半乳糖苷酶途径在定性上确立良好，但没有检索到零售酸奶的每 100 g 活性数据，因此这条部分可行的食物途径无法定量，也无法与胶囊剂量比较。

items.supplement_zh: 非处方消化酶复配产品
items.food_status_note_zh: 原为 NOT_FOOD，判定过重，且与本条自己的剂型注意点自相矛盾，故重新分级。植物蛋白酶确实存在于普通食物中：果实菠萝蛋白酶存在于可食的菠萝果肉和果汁中，具有真实的蛋白水解活性，这正是新鲜菠萝会让明胶无法凝固而罐装菠萝不会的原因；木瓜蛋白酶除存在于作为商业来源的乳汁中，也存在于未熟木瓜的果肉里；猕猴桃蛋白酶（actinidin）是一种半胱氨酸蛋白酶，存在于普通可食的成熟绿肉猕猴桃中，并有人体数据用绿肉（含 actinidin）与金果（不含 actinidin）猕猴桃比较胃内蛋白消化。姜（zingibain）、无花果乳汁（ficin）、麦芽大麦（麦芽淀粉酶）和生蜂蜜（diastase）是另外几种真实的膳食酶来源。真正仍属 NOT_FOOD 的是这些复配产品的另一半：其中的淀粉酶、蛋白酶、脂肪酶和乳糖酶组分是 Aspergillus 或酵母发酵产物，在膳食中不存在。评为 TRACE 而未评 PARTIAL，原因是可食果肉中的活性虽然存在却没有任何经确认的定量，而携带已测活性的部位并不被食用。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 菠萝蛋白酶补充剂按活性给药，典型为 500-2,000 mg 标准化到约 2,400 GDU/g 的制剂，每次剂量约 1,200-4,800 GDU。按菠萝副产物报告的活性折算，这相当于约 0.41-1.65 g 茎基部或约 1.0-4.1 g 果皮，而茎基部和果皮都不会被吃掉（这些每克活性值出自一篇真实且切题的论文，其中的单项数字无法调取，应视为未确认）。若换成真正会放进嘴里的食物来表达，这个剂量无法匹配：冠芽检测不到活性，果心通常被丢弃，成熟果肉则没有有据可查的活性数据。新鲜菠萝和绿肉猕猴桃确实会把有活性的蛋白酶送进胃里，所以效果不为零，但在缺少可食果肉活性确认值的情况下，没有办法把 GDU 剂量换算成食物当量。木瓜蛋白酶的原料是未熟果实的乳汁，有刺激性，不属于食物。至于真菌来源的淀粉酶、蛋白酶和脂肪酶组分，根本没有食物来源。
items.form_caveat_zh: 整食是安全的，浓缩物未必。新鲜菠萝和木瓜是普通水果；浓缩菠萝蛋白酶有抗凝和抗血小板活性，与华法林及抗血小板药物存在相互作用，木瓜蛋白酶和木瓜凝乳蛋白酶（chymopapain）是公认的呼吸道和接触性致敏物，EFSA 在对该食品酶的致敏性评估中已提示这一点（原稿引用的具体标识 DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2026.9950 无法确认；EFSA 确实发布过关于木瓜乳汁来源木瓜蛋白酶的意见，因此论点本身成立，那个引用不成立）。基质本身也推翻了前提：这些是蛋白质，加热和胃酸会使其失活。罐装和加热过的菠萝已没有有意义的蛋白水解活性，这正是罐装菠萝不会阻止明胶凝固而新鲜菠萝会的原因；任何口服吞下且无肠溶保护的酶，在到达小肠之前都会遇到胃蛋白酶和 pH 2。最重要的注意点是适用范围：这些复配产品不等同于胰酶替代治疗，在已确诊的胰腺外分泌不足中绝不能用来替代，那里的要求是每餐 40,000-50,000 单位脂肪酶的肠溶包衣猪源制剂（PMID 42011215）。复配产品中植物来源的乳糖酶也不能与剂量标准化的乳糖酶产品互换。
items.bioavailability_zh: 酶不被吸收，也不需要被吸收；它们在肠腔内起作用，所以关键是能否在合适的 pH 和部位存活下来。茎菠萝蛋白酶与果实菠萝蛋白酶连等电点都不同（pI 9.5 对 4.6），这就是提取 pH 决定你实际拿到哪种酶的原因，也是标签上写菠萝蛋白酶并不指向单一分子的原因。有意义的单位是活性。GDU、CDU、FIP 和 USP 单位之间无法互换，所以瓶子上的毫克数几乎说明不了它能做什么。菠萝蛋白酶和木瓜蛋白酶都会因加热而不可逆变性，若无肠溶保护也大多被胃酸破坏，所以无包衣胶囊和一碗新鲜菠萝面对的是同一个递送问题。
items.data_confidence_zh: 低。本条的定量核心无法核实。菠萝副产物活性（茎基部 2,909 GDU/g，果皮 1,179 GDU/g，果心 694 GDU/g，冠芽低于检出限）出自一篇真实且切题的论文（PMID 38397568），但其中的单项数值未被调取，而所有剂量当量都由它们推导而来。EFSA 木瓜蛋白酶的标识无法确认。两个食物行只能定性，因为没有检索到可食菠萝果肉或猕猴桃的活性数据。只有补充剂一侧的算术（每次剂量 1,200-4,800 GDU）和菠萝蛋白酶同工型的生化特性经得起核对。

foods_zh.pct_zh: 无法与按 GDU 标准化的菠萝蛋白酶剂量对表；单位不同、酶也不同，且果肉活性值未获确认

foods_zh.portion_zh: 1 杯块状（约 165 g），常规份量
foods_zh.pct_zh: 无法表达；文献中实测的 GDU/g 数值属于茎基部、果皮和果心，不属于果肉

items.food_status_note: Turmeric is an ordinary culinary spice, the dried ground rhizome of Curcuma longa, and it carries curcumin at 3.14% by weight, so one level teaspoon delivers 94 mg. Measured against the JECFA/EFSA acceptable daily intake for curcumin of 3 mg/kg body weight (210 mg for a 70 kg adult), a single teaspoon supplies 45% of the ADI, which is a rich dietary source on any normal reading; the earlier TRACE label came from scoring food against a 1,000 mg capsule, which is the dose question and is answered separately below. Turmeric is effectively the only meaningful food source, and commercial curry powder is much weaker. Fresh turmeric rhizome is the same food in unprocessed form and is increasingly sold in UK and US supermarkets, but no verified composition figure for it is available here, so it gets no row.
items.dose_from_food_note: A 1,000 mg curcuminoid capsule equals about 21 to 32 g of turmeric powder every day: 32 g counting curcumin only at 3.14% w/w, about 21 g counting all three curcuminoids at roughly 4.7% (a conventional ratio the cited source does not establish). That is 7 to 11 level teaspoons, close to a third of a supermarket spice jar per day, and nobody eats that. A generous curry portion carries 1 to 2 g of turmeric, or 30 to 60 mg of curcumin, and a heavy South Asian intake of 2 to 2.5 g turmeric per day yields 63 to 79 mg of curcumin, so the capsule is about 13 to 16 times a heavy dietary intake on a curcumin basis, and about 8.5 to 11 times if the comparison is made on total curcuminoids. There is no eating route to the dose.

items.form_caveat: This is the single most important form gap in the whole list. Culinary turmeric has no liver-injury signal; 95% curcuminoid extracts, especially those boosted with piperine or reformulated as phytosomes, micelles or nanoparticles, are now a leading identified botanical cause of drug-induced liver injury in US and Australian case series, with a reported HLA-B*35:01 association. The EFSA/JECFA acceptable daily intake for curcumin (E 100) is 3 mg/kg body weight per day, 210 mg for a 70 kg adult: one teaspoon of turmeric in food (94 mg curcumin) sits at 45% of it, while a single 1,000 mg curcuminoid capsule is about five times over it. Concentrated extracts also inhibit CYP3A4 and UGT enzymes and interact with anticoagulants, which food-level turmeric does not. Second caveat cutting the other way: scaling up culinary turmeric is not a safe workaround either, because turmeric powder in some supply chains has been adulterated with lead chromate for colour (well documented in Bangladeshi turmeric), and gram-level daily dosing of spice-grade powder magnifies that exposure.
items.bioavailability: Curcumin is close to a worst case for oral absorption: poor solubility, extensive intestinal and hepatic glucuronidation and sulfation, and rapid biliary excretion leave systemic exposure at or below detection limits after dietary amounts. Co-administered piperine 20 mg raised curcumin bioavailability roughly 20-fold in humans (Shoba et al. 1998, PMID 9619120, verified as a 2000% increase), and modern phytosome, micellar and nanoparticle formulations claim 10 to 185-fold increases over unformulated powder. The practical consequence is that milligram equivalence between spice and supplement misleads in both directions: a formulated 500 mg extract can deliver more systemic curcumin than 30 g of raw powder, and the traditional practice of blooming turmeric in hot oil with black pepper is a crude version of the same trick.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The headline 3.14% curcumin figure, the two USDA portion weights, the per-teaspoon and per-tablespoon arithmetic, the 210 mg ADI and Shoba's 20-fold piperine effect all verified exactly. The curry powder range, the curcumin-to-total-curcuminoid ratio and the FDC ID could not be traced to their cited sources.

items.food_status_note: Green tea, matcha, white tea and gunpowder green tea all deliver EGCG at tens to over a hundred milligrams per cup or bowl from ordinary shop-bought products, so this is the one entry in the set where a normal beverage reaches the doses used in supplement trials. EFSA's exposure assessment puts mean adult intake at 86 to 321 mg EGCG/day across dietary surveys and high-level (95th percentile) intake at 308 to 866 mg/day, so the top of habitual tea drinking brushes the 800 mg supplement threshold. Oolong is often grouped in here, but no measured per-cup figure survived verification, so it gets no row; bottled ready-to-drink green tea is the commercially dominant form and is far weaker than anything listed, and it also lacks a verified figure here.
items.dose_from_food_note: 800 mg EGCG, the dose at which supplements produce measurable liver enzyme rises, is about 4 to 5 cups of green tea at EFSA's mean brewed concentration of 70.2 mg/100 mL, or 10 to 16 cups of more weakly brewed retail tea, or about 7 to 8 bowls of matcha at 2 g each. EFSA's high-level consumers already reach 308 to 866 mg/day from infusions alone, so the top of that range is at the supplement dose. What differs is the vehicle: the tea drinker's 800 mg arrives spread over a day in two to three litres of water, usually with food, while the supplement delivers it as a single fasted bolus.

items.form_caveat: State this plainly: the beverage carries no meaningful liver signal, the extract does. EFSA concluded that intake at or above 800 mg EGCG/day taken as a food supplement causes a statistically significant increase in serum transaminases, while catechins from green tea infusion prepared in the traditional way, and reconstituted drinks of equivalent composition, are in general considered safe. Same molecule, different product. Risk concentrates in high-dose, single-bolus, fasted dosing of concentrated extracts, and Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/2340 now prohibits supplements delivering 800 mg or more EGCG per day in the EU. Green tea extract is also the ingredient behind a large share of liver injury cases attributed to weight-loss and fat-burner blends, which is a warning about the extract rather than about tea.
items.bioavailability: Systemic bioavailability of EGCG is low, on the order of 0.1 to 1% of an oral dose as the unchanged compound, with heavy glucuronidation, sulfation and methylation plus colonic degradation. The critical modifier is food: fasted dosing raises EGCG Cmax severalfold compared with the same dose taken with a meal, and fasted administration is both the way extracts are typically taken and the condition associated with hepatotoxicity. Milk and food proteins bind catechins and blunt peak levels, so tea with milk is pharmacologically not tea on an empty stomach. Brewing extracts only part of the leaf's EGCG whereas matcha delivers the whole leaf. The corrected numbers support the point that matcha is no many-fold EGCG upgrade per gram of leaf: matcha measures 50.53 to 56.57 mg/g against gunpowder green tea at 70.22 mg/g in the same 15-product HPLC survey, which found no statistically significant EGCG difference across tea types.
items.data_confidence: HIGH. Every EFSA figure verified exactly (70.2 mg/100 mL from 100 samples across 12 references, 7,116 mg/100 g dry leaf, the intake ranges, the 800 mg transaminase conclusion), and the corrected matcha and gunpowder values come from an HPLC survey of 15 commercial products. The white tea row is the only indicative entry.

items.food_status_note: Resveratrol occurs in red wine, grapes, peanuts and some berries, at concentrations three to five orders of magnitude below trial doses; red wine averages 1.9 mg trans-resveratrol per litre, so a whole litre holds less than one capsule. Supplement resveratrol is not grape-derived: it is made synthetically or extracted from Japanese knotweed root (Polygonum cuspidatum). Knotweed is not entirely inedible, since young itadori shoots are eaten as a spring vegetable in Japan and foraged in the UK and North America and itadori tea is made from the plant, so the accurate statement is that it is not a food in Western diets, has no composition-table entry, and the root used for extraction is not the part anyone eats. Three sources that belong in the food picture carry no verified figure here and so get no row: peanut skins (the redskin testa, the richest stilbene fraction of the peanut, which is why the roasted-kernel value is explicitly for peanuts without seed coats), red and purple grape juice (the non-alcoholic route the ethanol argument implies), and the wider stilbene foods (muscadine grapes, bilberries, blueberries, cranberries, pistachios, cocoa), so the roughly 5 mg/day dietary ceiling rests on population intake studies rather than on rows built here.
items.dose_from_food_note: A 150 mg resveratrol dose equals 79 litres of average red wine (150 divided by 1.9 mg/L), about 105 standard 750 mL bottles or roughly 450 glasses, every day. Even at the top of the corroborated sample spread of 0.361 to 1.972 mg/L it is still 76 litres a day. From grapes it is 30 kg daily; from boiled peanuts 29 kg, and from roasted peanuts 2.7 tonnes. Trials commonly use 150 to 1,000 mg/day and the SRT501 cancer studies used up to 5 g/day, all of it manufactured. Measured population intakes sit far lower again (a Spanish study found a median of 100 ug/day and a mean of 933 ug/day for resveratrol plus piceid, and French wine consumption yields about 0.2 mg/day), and no plausible diet gets past about 5 mg/day.

items.form_caveat: Three separate mismatches. First, the supplement is not a food extract: commercial resveratrol is synthetic or comes from Polygonum cuspidatum root, which is not a Western food and not a composition-table food, so the grape imagery on the label is marketing rather than sourcing. Second, wine's stilbenes are mostly the glucoside trans-piceid, at about three times the aglycone concentration, arriving inside a large mixed polyphenol and ethanol matrix, so wine does not behave as a dilute resveratrol capsule. Third, and decisive: recommending wine as a resveratrol source is a bad recommendation regardless of dose, because ethanol is a Group 1 carcinogen and the alcohol harm arrives at one glass while the resveratrol dose would require a hundred bottles. Separately, high-dose resveratrol (2.5 to 5 g/day) causes diarrhoea and nausea and inhibits CYP3A4, CYP2C9 and sulfotransferases, giving it real interaction potential (warfarin, for example) that a glass of wine does not have.
items.bioavailability: Oral resveratrol is well absorbed (about 70% of the dose crosses the enterocyte) but systemic bioavailability of the unchanged aglycone is under 1 to 2% because of near-immediate intestinal and hepatic glucuronidation and sulfation; plasma peaks from dietary quantities sit in the low nanomolar range, while in vitro activity is generally demonstrated at micromolar concentrations. Piceid, the form dominant in grapes and much of wine, must be deglycosylated before absorption, adding another step. Gram doses are needed to reach micromolar plasma levels, which is precisely why the food route is closed.

The boiled peanut and peanut butter values sit behind a paywall and are indicative, and the wine maximum of 14.3 mg/L had to be removed as untraceable.

items.food_status_note: Astaxanthin is genuinely present at milligram levels in ordinary seafood, so this is the strongest food case in the set. Wild sockeye salmon carries 26 to 38 mg per kg of flesh, meaning one 140 g fillet supplies 3.6 to 5.3 mg, the same order of magnitude as a capsule. Several standard sources in the same literature carry no verified figure here and so get no row: salmon roe (ikura and sujiko), wild chinook, pink and chum salmon, Arctic char, red sea bream, and the shell-on preparations (crayfish, small crab, head-on prawns) where the pigment actually concentrates.
items.dose_from_food_note: A 12 mg daily dose, the commonest in the clinical literature, equals 315 to 460 g of wild sockeye salmon every day at 26 to 38 mg/kg, or about 550 g using the cited review's own dietary anchor of 3.6 mg per 165 g portion. From farmed Atlantic salmon it is 1.5 to 2.0 kg per day, from peeled shrimp meat about 1.4 kg, and from whole wet krill 1.2 to 1.5 kg. A single 140 g sockeye fillet already covers 30 to 44% of the dose, which no other entry here manages, so a meaningful fraction is reachable by eating while the full dose is not: sustaining 350 to 500 g of oily fish daily would push past standard advice on methylmercury and persistent organic pollutants.

items.form_caveat: Chemical form differs by source. Salmon astaxanthin is largely free or protein-bound; krill and Haematococcus astaxanthin is esterified with fatty acids; and much supplement and feed astaxanthin is synthetic astaxanthin dimethyldisuccinate, a different stereoisomer mixture from the natural 3S,3'S form. This matters for the safety arithmetic: EFSA's acceptable daily intake of 0.2 mg/kg body weight per day (14 mg for a 70 kg adult, established by the FEEDAP Panel in 2019 and replacing the earlier 0.034 mg/kg) was derived from a rat carcinogenicity study on the synthetic material and then applied to the algal form. On that ADI, a 12 mg capsule is 86% of the limit and sits just under it, doses of about 14 mg and above exceed it, and a 24 mg capsule is roughly 1.7 times over, while a salmon fillet stays well below. A safety review of 87 human studies, including 35 at 12 mg/day or more, found no safety concerns with natural astaxanthin and argues the synthetic-derived ADI should not govern it (Brendler & Williamson, Phytother Res 2019;33(12):3090-3111, PMID 31788888, DOI 10.1002/ptr.6514). One honest twist: the astaxanthin in farmed salmon is itself an added feed pigment, so eating farmed salmon for astaxanthin means eating a supplemented animal.
items.bioavailability: Astaxanthin is a lipophilic xanthophyll and absorption depends on fat and micelle formation: uptake from a lipid-based formulation or a fatty meal is severalfold higher than from a dry powder taken fasted, and esterified forms must first be hydrolysed by pancreatic lipase. Overall human bioavailability is low and highly variable (single-digit percentages), which cuts in favour of the food: salmon arrives pre-packaged with its own lipid and a food matrix, so the plasma difference between a 4 mg fillet and a 12 mg dry capsule is smaller than the milligram gap implies.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. Every salmonid figure verified exactly against its source (sockeye 26 to 38 mg/kg, Atlantic 6 to 8, trout 6 and 25, the 165 g / 3.6 mg anchor, retail sockeye 14.2 and coho 7.0 mg/kg), as did the EFSA ADI and the Brendler review. The salmonid values still rest on a compiled review figure, the shrimp span is paywalled and indicative, and the krill row is a wet-weight reconstruction rather than a measured food value.

items.supplement: Saffron, SAMe and other mood botanicals
items.food_status_note: This item bundles three different answers, so each gets its own sentence. Saffron is RICH: it is a supermarket spice with USDA composition and portion entries, its clinical dose is a cooking quantity, and it is listed under foods below, which is why the previous NOT_FOOD label on the group was the clearest error in the submission. SAMe has no dietary source: there is no meaningful preformed SAMe in food and no composition-table entry, the body synthesises it continuously from methionine and ATP by methionine adenosyltransferase, and the commercial material is made by Saccharomyces cerevisiae fermentation and stabilised as the tosylate disulfate or 1,4-butanedisulfonate salt, so it is biosynthetic in origin and the SYNTHETIC label holds in the sense of 'no dietary source' rather than 'chemically synthesised'. St John's wort aerial parts, rhodiola root, ashwagandha root and Griffonia simplicifolia seed (the source of 5-HTP) are NOT_FOOD: nobody eats them in any normal diet, they have no composition-table entry, and they have no portion size.
items.dose_from_food_note: For saffron the gap is zero or negative, which is the most useful finding in the set: the 30 mg/day used in the depression RCTs is about 15 threads at published thread weights near 2 mg, or about 6 to 9 threads if a thread weighs the 3 to 5 mg implied by the commonly quoted 20 to 30 threads per 0.1 g, which is under a generous culinary pinch, and one teaspoon of saffron in a paella is over twenty doses. The barrier is cost rather than physiology. For SAMe there is nothing to compute, because there is no food source: trials use 400 to 1,600 mg/day of a manufactured molecule, while the body's own SAMe turnover (on the order of grams per day) is fed by roughly 1 g/day of dietary methionine from protein foods, which is a different intervention from swallowing SAMe. For the remaining botanicals (St John's wort typically 300 mg three times daily of a 0.3% hypericin extract, rhodiola 200 to 600 mg, ashwagandha 300 to 600 mg root extract, 5-HTP 100 to 300 mg) the food gap is undefined because the source plants are not foods at any quantity.

foods.per_100g: 100 g of saffron is 3,333 clinical doses of 30 mg. The fluoxetine comparison belongs to a separate trial (Noorbala AA et al., J Ethnopharmacol 2005)

items.form_caveat: Saffron is the mildest food-versus-extract case in this whole set, since trials use either powdered stigma or a hydroalcoholic extract standardised to crocins and safranal, so kitchen saffron is close to the trial material. The caveat is at the top end: saffron is toxic at gram doses, with roughly 5 g reported as a toxic dose and 12 to 20 g as potentially lethal, and it is a traditional abortifacient, so scaling from a pinch to a spoonful is genuinely hazardous. Standardised extracts also concentrate crocins, so milligram for milligram an extract is not the spice. For the rest of the group the form gap is total: St John's wort is a potent CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inducer that has caused transplant rejection, contraceptive failure and serotonin syndrome with SSRIs; ashwagandha root extracts have accumulated a documented cluster of hepatotoxicity case reports, including in regulatory reviews, while traditional use was of small amounts of root powder in milk as medicine and never as a food; purified 5-HTP bypasses the rate-limiting tryptophan hydroxylase step that normally regulates serotonin synthesis, which is exactly why it carries serotonin syndrome risk with serotonergic drugs and why no food behaves like it.
items.bioavailability: Saffron's crocins are poorly absorbed intact and are hydrolysed in the gut to crocetin, which is what appears in plasma; safranal is volatile and is partly lost in long simmering, so a slow-cooked dish delivers a different apocarotenoid profile than a capsule taken cold, and blooming saffron in warm liquid before adding it is the culinary analogue of extraction. SAMe is chemically unstable and is degraded in gastric acid unless enterically coated, and oral bioavailability is only about 1% because of extensive first-pass metabolism, which is why oral doses are 400 to 1,600 mg while parenteral doses are far smaller. The classic bad recommendation in this space is 'eat turkey or eggs for 5-HTP': food supplies tryptophan, and dietary tryptophan competes with the other large neutral amino acids in the same protein meal for LAT1 transport across the blood-brain barrier, so a high-protein meal can lower rather than raise brain tryptophan availability. Food is a poor delivery route for this entire group.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The saffron portion weights, the 3,333-doses arithmetic and the trial's 30 mg/day for 6 weeks all verified exactly, and the trial's design has been corrected against the abstract. The apocarotenoid content figures could not be confirmed anywhere and have been removed, the thread-weight basis remains unsettled between two mutually inconsistent conventions, and the FDC ID is unconfirmed.

items.food_status_note: This category holds four different answers and the earlier single TRACE label hid the most important one. Caffeine is RICH and is the only component with a consistent thermogenic effect, available from coffee and tea by the cup. p-Synephrine is RICH as well: citrus juices carry up to 25 to 40 mg per quarter litre and Seville orange juice about 13 mg per 240 mL glass, which sits inside the clinical dose range, so the earlier NOT_FOOD label for bitter orange was wrong. Garcinia gummi-gutta rind (kodampuli, Malabar tamarind) is a genuine culinary souring agent in Kerala and parts of Southeast Asia, used in fish curry and asam laksa, and carries hydroxycitric acid at 10 to 30% of dry weight. The remainder splits differently: raspberry ketone is TRACE (up to 4.3 mg/kg in raspberries against 100 to 1,400 mg/day sold), green coffee chlorogenic acids come from unroasted beans that nobody eats, yohimbe bark and Coleus forskohlii root are NOT_FOOD, and higenamine and DMAA are synthetic with no food origin at all.
items.dose_from_food_note: Component by component. Caffeine: 200 mg is four to five 150 mL cups of filter coffee on the cited Brazilian table, or about two 240 mL US/UK mugs at roughly 95 mg each, or five cups of green tea, so this one is trivially reachable (guarana powder, yerba mate, cocoa and energy drinks belong in the same picture and appear in the same cited caffeine table, but no per-portion figure was verified here, so they get no row). p-Synephrine: a single 240 mL glass of Seville orange juice at about 13 mg already sits inside the 10 to 53 mg/day range used in the pooled overweight and obese subjects, whose individual study doses spanned 5.5 to 80 mg. Garcinia: 3 g of dried rind souring a pot for four carries 300 to 900 mg HCA at 10 to 30% w/w, about 75 to 225 mg per person against supplement doses of 72 to 900 mg HCA, and less again because HCA transfers only partly into the broth and the rind is fished out rather than eaten, so culinary use lands in the lower middle of the supplement range rather than at its top. Raspberry ketone: 100 mg, the smallest common dose, is about 23 kg of fresh raspberries at the highest natural concentration of 4.3 mg/kg, and the 1,400 mg top dose about 326 kg, so it is unreachable by three orders of magnitude, and the safety review notes even the lowest recommended dose is about 56 times the threshold of toxicological concern for its structural class. Green coffee: extracts standardised to 45 to 50% chlorogenic acids at 400 to 1,600 mg/day supply roughly 200 to 800 mg CGA, and the concentrated dose exists only because green beans are inedible; the cups-of-coffee comparison cannot be stated here, because the bean percentages it rested on were misattributed and have been withdrawn.
