foods.pct_rda_or_dose: 0.0003% of a 1 mg dose
foods.source: CUME+ study, J Hum Nutr Diet 2026, PMID 41588582, DOI 10.1111/jhn.70193; 0.015 ng/g = 15 pg/g sits inside the reviewed 14.45-18.41 pg/mL range (PMC5409706) and corresponds to daytime-milked milk. Night-milked milk runs several-fold higher and is sold commercially on that basis, so one value understates the range.

items.form_caveat: Food melatonin is not a smaller version of a tablet. Tart cherry juice concentrate measurably raises urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin and improved actigraphy-measured sleep efficiency at 2 x 30 mL/day (Howatson et al. Eur J Nutr 2012;51(8):909-916, PMID 22038497, verified), yet no melatonin content figure for the concentrate could be sourced here, so the one preparation with a positive human sleep outcome remains uncosted; the melatonin delivered is a fraction of a microgram, and most of the effect probably comes from the polyphenol matrix and tryptophan availability. Cultivar swamps everything: Montmorency and Balaton are the same species and differ 6.5-fold. Two melatonin-rich botanicals bear on this list for context: Scutellaria (huang-qin) at about 7,110 ng/g dry weight and St John's wort at about 4,490 ng/g dry weight, the latter classified NOT_FOOD in its own entry while being among the richest melatonin-bearing plants on record. On the pistachio dispute: one 2014 spectrofluorimetric paper reported roughly 233 ug/g dry weight, about 89,300 times the LC-MS/MS value, and it carries a published Expression of Concern (original PMID 24878439; EoC Spectrochim Acta A 2019;217:322, PMID 31027610). At that disputed figure 4.3 g of pistachios, about seven kernels, would supply 1 mg, which is exactly why the number should be treated as unconfirmed rather than as a food-based melatonin strategy. The Expression of Concern record lists only the four original authors and states no replication failure, so the submission's attribution of it to a German federal risk-assessment body has been removed. On the supplement side, doses commonly sold at 3-10 mg are ten to thirty times a physiological replacement dose, independent testing of commercial products has repeatedly found large deviations from label content plus occasional serotonin contamination, and melatonin is a prescription-only medicine in the UK and much of the EU while sold freely as a supplement in the US.
items.bioavailability: Absolute oral bioavailability of melatonin is low and highly variable, averaging about 15% (reported range roughly 9-33%, with individual values spanning a five-fold spread), because up to 85% is removed on first pass, mainly by hepatic CYP1A2. CYP1A2 modifiers therefore matter more than the source: caffeine raises plasma melatonin from a given dose, smoking lowers it. Nothing is known about whether the nanogram to low-microgram quantities in a food matrix follow the same kinetics, and at those quantities the question is close to academic. Anyone comparing natural melatonin in pistachios with a tablet is comparing a sub-microgram intake against a supra-physiological one.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The cherry values, the walnut value, the pistachio LC-MS/MS value, the milk value, the disputed 233 ug/g figure and the 89,300x ratio were all verified against primary sources, and the bioavailability figure matches the established literature. Against that, the entry's original anchor (goji) had to be replaced with a review value, the egg figure had to be re-based from dry solids to fresh weight, and the ten added rows all rest on a single compiled secondary review table (PMC5409706) whose primary measurements were not re-traced in this pass.
corrections_applied: Replaced the goji anchor: 1600.48 ng/g fresh weight (non-indexed journal, HPLC-FD, 15x to 100x outlier, exceeds the maximum of the 119-food CUME+ compilation by ~10x) swapped for the review value of 103 ng/g dry weight, and the row re-based to dried berries. The old 16%/32%-of-dose figures are void.

Fixed the egg moisture basis: 6.1 ng/g is egg dried solids, so fresh whole egg is about 1.5 ng/g. Per 100 g now 0.15 ug (was 0.61), per 50 g egg now 0.077 ug (was 0.31), now 0.008% of a 1 mg dose (was 0.031%).

Recomputed dose gaps: milk now about 64,500 L (was 67,000 L; kilograms had been treated as litres, correct at a density of 1.03 kg/L); egg now about 655-670 kg / 13,100-13,400 eggs (was 164 kg / 3,280 eggs); goji now about 9.7 kg dried (was 625 g fresh).
Restated the pistachio dose gap as a range rather than 383 kg, because the reported SD exceeds the mean.
Corrected two portion counts that were 1 oz counts relabelled as 30 g: about 52 pistachio kernels and about 15 walnut halves.

Dropped the claim that the Expression of Concern followed a German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment replication failure; the EoC record names only the four original authors and gives no replication attribution.
Withdrew the conclusion that goji berries are the one food a human could theoretically eat to a dose.
Added ten omitted food rows in rank order: roasted coffee, germinated lentils, red wine, germinated kidney beans, tomato, strawberry, white mustard seed, sunflower seed, fenugreek seed and almonds.
Added the walnut PMID (15979282) and the Reiter HPLC-plus-radioimmunoassay method caveat.
Noted that night-milked milk runs several-fold higher than the single daytime value given.
Split the label: TRACE now answers only whether melatonin occurs in food, and the note states separately that the commercial supplement is a synthetic manufactured article.

items.food_status_note: Berberine is an isoquinoline alkaloid from the roots, rhizomes and stem bark of medicinal plants: Berberis vulgaris (common barberry), B. aristata, B. asiatica and B. lycium, Coptis chinensis (huang lian) rhizome, Hydrastis canadensis (goldenseal), Mahonia aquifolium (Oregon grape) and Phellodendron amurense. None of these organs is eaten as food. Accumulation is highest in root tissue, 1.6-4.3% of dry weight across Berberis species, and B. vulgaris bark carries over 8% total alkaloids of which about 5% is berberine (Neag et al., Front Pharmacol 2018, PMC6111450, verified). Barberry fruit is the one part genuinely eaten, as zereshk in Iranian rice dishes, and it is the wrong organ: the whole-plant survey reporting up to 26,482 ug/g berberine in root and no detectable alkaloids in fruit pulp across 96 accessions was done on Berberis darwinii, the Chilean michay, which is a congener of the zereshk species rather than the same plant, and in that study leaves and seeds did carry detectable (lower) alkaloid levels, so only the pulp was non-detect (Molecules 2025;30(8):1849, PMID 40333914). The species question is closed by a separate group working directly on B. vulgaris fruit, which reports that the flowers, fruit pulp and seeds have little or no significant alkaloid content and describes their fruit extract as nearly devoid of berberine (Iran J Pharm Res 2011;10(1):97-104, PMID 24363687).
items.dose_from_food_note: Trials use 500 mg two or three times daily, 1000-1500 mg/day. At the 5% berberine content of B. vulgaris root bark that is 20-30 g of dried root bark per day, which is a herbal decoction rather than a meal. Via the edible fruit the gap is not a large number, it is undefined: berberine is below the limit of detection in barberry pulp, so no portion size reaches the dose at all. A generous serving of zereshk polow uses perhaps 30-50 g of dried berries spread across several people and contributes no measurable berberine. Coptis rhizome and goldenseal root would need 1-3 g of dried herb and neither is eaten as food.
items.form_caveat: This is the clearest case in the set where a food and its supplement share only a plant name. Eating zereshk supplies vitamin C, anthocyanins and organic acids, with no pharmacological berberine effect. The isolated alkaloid at 1000-1500 mg/day behaves like a drug: it inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 and is a P-glycoprotein substrate and inhibitor, so it can raise levels of co-administered medicines; it commonly causes constipation, cramping and diarrhoea; and it is contraindicated in pregnancy and in neonates because berberine displaces bilirubin from albumin and has been linked to kernicterus risk. Whole-plant root extracts also carry berbamine, palmatine and, in goldenseal, hydrastine, so a barberry root extract and a purified berberine HCl capsule are not the same product. Goldenseal is additionally a conservation concern and a frequent target of species adulteration.
items.bioavailability: Berberine's oral bioavailability is under 1%, measured at 0.36-0.68% in rats, with roughly 99.5% eliminated during gastrointestinal and hepatic first pass through poor solubility, self-aggregation in gastric acid, P-glycoprotein efflux and CYP-mediated intestinal metabolism (Expert Opin Drug Metab Toxicol 2023;19(3), PMID 37057922). Much of berberine's metabolic effect is thought to be exerted in the gut lumen and on the microbiome rather than systemically, so low bioavailability does not mean inactive. It does mean trace amounts from any food would be pharmacologically irrelevant, and it means formulation comparisons (plain salt, phytosome, micelle) can change exposure by an order of magnitude at the same labelled dose.
items.data_confidence: HIGH. Every quantitative claim in this entry was checked and matched its source verbatim: the 1.6-4.3% root range, the 8% total alkaloid / 5% berberine figure for B. vulgaris bark, the 26,482 ug/g root maximum, the 96-accession pulp non-detect, and the 20-30 g root-bark dose equivalent. The NOT_FOOD classification was challenged and upheld.
corrections_applied: Named the species mismatch the submission glossed over: the 96-accession non-detect result is from Berberis darwinii (Chilean michay), a congener of the zereshk species B. vulgaris, so the B. vulgaris fruit paper (PMID 24363687) is what actually closes the question for the eaten plant.
Added the refinement that leaves and seeds in that study did carry detectable, lower alkaloid levels, so only the fruit pulp was non-detect.

Split the label into the two questions: NOT_FOOD for the substance (a root and bark alkaloid), NO for the dose, with the note distinguishing the eaten organ (fruit) from the medicinal organ (root, rhizome, bark).
Kept the NOT_FOOD classification, which the verification pass challenged and upheld.
Kept every verified figure unchanged, including the 20-30 g root-bark dose equivalent.

items.food_status_note: Ashwagandha is the root, sometimes root plus leaf, of Withania somnifera, a small shrub in the Solanaceae. The root is a medicinal drug rather than a dietary item: bitter, taken as a churna or a decoction in milk, and present in no cuisine as an ingredient. The active steroidal lactones, withanolides such as withaferin A, withanolide A and withanone, occur in Withania and a few related genera and are absent from the food supply. The nightshades people actually eat, tomato, potato, aubergine, sweet and chilli peppers, contain a different class of steroidal compounds (glycoalkaloids such as tomatine and solanine), so botanical relatedness buys nothing here. A related species, Withania coagulans, has fruit used regionally as a vegetarian milk-clotting agent, which is a processing aid rather than a dietary source of withanolides.
items.dose_from_food_note: Trials use 300-600 mg/day of standardised root extract. KSM-66 is a root-only extract standardised to a minimum 5% withanolides, Sensoril is a root-and-leaf extract at 10%, and Shoden is standardised to 35% withanolide glycosides, so a typical daily dose is roughly 15-60 mg of withanolides. Traditional practice uses 3-6 g/day of dried root powder to reach a comparable place. No food quantity supplies this at any size, because no food plant contains withanolides. Quoting an equivalent weight of an ordinary food would require inventing a content value, so the honest answer is that the dietary route does not exist.
items.form_caveat: Plant part matters and so does the regulator's view. Root-only preparations have a better documented safety profile than preparations including leaf and aerial parts, which are richer in withaferin A, the most cytotoxic of the withanolides. Ashwagandha is banned in food supplements in Denmark, the Dutch national institute RIVM has published a risk assessment of Withania preparations (RIVM report 2024-0029), French authorities have advised against use in specific groups, the UK Food Standards Agency has logged rising incident reports and its committee reviewed associations with thyroid toxicity, hypoglycaemia and liver toxicity, and Australia's TGA issued a medicine safety update in July 2026 on continuing reports of ashwagandha-associated liver injury judged to be idiosyncratic. KSM-66's milk-based extraction is a marketing distinction rather than a safety one. Withanolide content also varies with chemotype, cultivation and plant part, so two products at the same milligram dose can differ several-fold in the compounds that matter.
items.bioavailability: Human pharmacokinetic data are thin and no standard bioavailability figure can be quoted with confidence. Withanolides are lipophilic and poorly water-soluble, which is why traditional preparation uses milk or ghee and why modern products add phospholipid or cyclodextrin carriers. Withanolide glycosides (withanosides) are more water-soluble and are the markers Shoden standardises on, so percent withanolides on two labels may refer to chemically different pools measured by different assays. Because there is no food form there is no food-versus-supplement absorption comparison to make; the meaningful comparison is between extract types, and it is not standardised.
items.data_confidence: HIGH for the food and dose determination. The NOT_FOOD call was challenged and upheld, the withanolide dose arithmetic (15-60 mg from 300-600 mg of extract at 5-10%) was verified as correct, and there are no food-composition figures in this entry to be wrong. The verification pass specifically endorsed the refusal to invent a withanolide food content value. The regulatory statements were outside the scope of the numeric verification.
corrections_applied: No numeric corrections were required; the verification pass found no errors in this entry.
Kept the NOT_FOOD classification, which was challenged and upheld.
Kept the verified 15-60 mg withanolide dose range and the 3-6 g dried-root traditional equivalent unchanged.
Split the label into the two questions: NOT_FOOD for the substance (a medicinal root), NO for the dose, retaining the explicit refusal to invent a food content figure.

items.food_status_note: The supplement is the rhizome and root of Rhodiola rosea (roseroot), an arctic-alpine succulent in the Crassulaceae, standardised on rosavins (rosavin, rosin, rosarin) and salidroside. The rhizome is a folk-medicine drug of Scandinavia and Russia and is not eaten as food. The plant is not entirely outside the food record: young leaves and shoots have been eaten raw or cooked like spinach and stems cooked like asparagus in Greenland, Alaska and northern North America, and Inuit use mixed leaves and buds with marine fat. That food use involves the aerial parts while rosavins are rhizome constituents, and composition data for the edible shoots are sparse, so the culinary history does not translate into a dietary source of the marker compounds. Rosavins are also close to unique to R. rosea, which is why species substitution is such a persistent problem.
items.dose_from_food_note: Typical dosing is 200-600 mg/day of extract standardised to 3% rosavins and 1% salidroside (the SHR-5 pattern), roughly 6-18 mg rosavins and 2-6 mg salidroside per day. The dried-rhizome equivalent depends entirely on the content assumed, and the 0.01-3.08% rosavin / 0.07-2.91% salidroside range cited here is COMMERCIAL PRODUCT content rather than measured rhizome, so raw-material content is not established from that source. Stating the assumption explicitly: at 1-3% rosavins, 0.2-1.8 g of dried rhizome carries a daily dose; at 0.1-0.5%, 1.2-18 g; at the 0.01% floor of the cited range, 60-180 g. The submission's flat 0.5-2 g figure silently assumed the top of the range and is optimistic by up to two orders of magnitude. On any assumption this is a herbal dose of a root and no food supplies it, and the edible young shoots cannot be costed at all because the composition work is on rhizome material.
items.form_caveat: Rhodiola has an unusually bad identity record. An analysis of US-market Rhodiola supplements found rosavin and salidroside contents ranging from 0.01% to 3.08% and 0.07% to 2.91% respectively, with substantial departures from label claims, alongside heavy metal and pesticide residue screening (The quality and safety of Rhodiola rosea supplements on the U.S. market, PLoS One 2026, PMC12810810, verified). Those are finished-product figures, not raw-material figures, a distinction the submission blurred. Rhodiola crenulata is a common substitute; it contains salidroside but little or no rosavin, so a product standardised only on salidroside can be a different species. Wild R. rosea is under harvesting pressure and CITES-listed in Appendix II. Field material varies enormously by clone and site, with inter-clonal variation of 92.8% reported for salidroside in Norwegian collections, so growing region and harvest season change the product more than the label does.
items.bioavailability: Salidroside is absorbed rapidly and hydrolysed to tyrosol, and rosavins are cinnamyl glycosides subject to gut microbial deglycosylation, so plasma exposure reflects metabolites rather than the labelled markers; controlled human pharmacokinetic data are limited and no reliable percentage figure can be given. Because there is no food form, the practical absorption question is the extraction solvent: hydroalcoholic extracts recover both rosavins and salidroside, while water infusions of the root recover the glycosides preferentially. Chewing raw shoots, the only genuinely food-like route, has never been characterised.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The NOT_FOOD classification was challenged and upheld and the cited biomarker ranges were verified as real and on-topic, but those ranges are commercial-product contents that the submission reused as raw-material contents, so the dried-rhizome dose equivalent is now given as a wide assumption-dependent range rather than a figure. No composition data exist for the edible aerial shoots, so that route cannot be quantified at all.
corrections_applied: Recomputed the dried-rhizome dose equivalent as a range with the assumed content stated: 0.2-1.8 g at 1-3% rosavins, 1.2-18 g at 0.1-0.5%, 60-180 g at the 0.01% floor. The submission's flat 0.5-2 g assumed the top of the cited range and was optimistic by up to two orders of magnitude.
Labelled the 0.01-3.08% and 0.07-2.91% ranges as commercial finished-product contents, correcting the submission's framing of them as measured rhizome-and-product content.
Kept the NOT_FOOD classification, which was challenged and upheld, including the organ distinction that the edible shoots are aerial parts while rosavins are rhizome constituents.
Split the label into the two questions: NOT_FOOD for the substance, NO for the dose.

items.food_status_note: Valerian is the root and rhizome of Valeriana officinalis, a European perennial. It is not a food in any cuisine; it is a bitter, strongly odorous drug taken as a tea, tincture or dried-extract capsule. The constituents credited with the sedative effect, valerenic acid and its relatives plus the flavonoids 6-methylapigenin, hesperidin and linarin, are found in Valeriana species and nowhere in the food supply. Valerian root has been used at low levels as a flavouring in some beverages, which puts trace amounts into a few products, and those are flavour levels, orders of magnitude below anything sedative. Nothing you would call a food supplies valerenic acid.
items.dose_from_food_note: Typical use is 400-900 mg of dried root extract before bed, or 2-3 g of dried root as an infusion. A quality target of at least 3 mg/g valerenic acid in the dried root has been recommended for commercial material and marketed extracts are sold around 0.8% valerenic acid, so a night's dose is roughly 3-8 mg of valerenic acid. No food at any portion size supplies measurable valerenic acid, so there is no achievable eating quantity to compute. The gap is total rather than large.
items.form_caveat: Valerian is the textbook example of a herb where the preparation determines the chemistry. Valerenic acid concentrations fall significantly during storage, with the greatest loss at 30 C in low humidity (Food Chemistry 2009, changes in valerenic acid content of valerian root during long-term storage), so an old capsule and a fresh one are different products. Valepotriates present in some preparations are unstable and degrade to baldrinals, and aqueous versus ethanolic extraction recovers quite different fractions, which is one reason valerian trials are so inconsistent. Practical cautions: additive sedation with alcohol, benzodiazepines and antihistamines; occasional paradoxical stimulation; rare hepatotoxicity reports, usually in multi-herb products. A valerian tea and a standardised extract capsule are not interchangeable at the same nominal gram amount.
items.bioavailability: Human data are limited. Valerenic acid is detectable in plasma after oral dosing with a short half-life of roughly one to two hours, which fits its use as a bedtime agent rather than a daytime one, and the flavonoid constituents undergo extensive glucuronidation. Because there is no food form there is no food-matrix comparison; the meaningful variable is extraction, since valerenic acid is lipophilic and is recovered far better by ethanol than by a water infusion, so a tea delivers a small and poorly characterised fraction of what a labelled milligram amount of extract implies.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The NOT_FOOD classification was challenged and upheld and the valerenic-acid dose arithmetic (3-8 mg per night) was verified as correct. The 3 mg/g quality target and the 0.8% extract figure each rest on a single secondary citation, and the storage-stability claim was not individually verified in the numeric pass.
corrections_applied: Corrected the nomenclature error: valepotinates is now valepotriates. The chemistry described, unstable and degrading to baldrinals, was already correct.
Kept the NOT_FOOD classification, which was challenged and upheld, including the point that flavouring-level use sits orders of magnitude below sedative doses.
Kept the verified 3-8 mg valerenic acid per night unchanged.
Split the label into the two questions: NOT_FOOD for the substance, NO for the dose.

items.food_status_note: The supplement is a concentrated leaf extract, and ginkgo leaf is not a food: it is processed with acetone-water into a standardised extract, of which EGb 761 is the reference, at a drug-to-extract ratio of 35-67:1 containing 22-27% flavone glycosides and 5-7% terpene lactones (2.8-3.4% ginkgolides A, B and C plus 2.6-3.2% bilobalide) with ginkgolic acids held below 5 ppm. The same species does have a real food form, and this is what a flat NOT_FOOD label conceals: ginkgo NUTS are eaten in Japanese chawanmushi, Chinese congee and Korean dishes, and they are chemically a different proposition from the leaf. Seeds carry ginkgotoxin (4'-O-methylpyridoxine and its 5'-glucoside), a vitamin B6 antagonist, at total mature-stage contents of 249-296 ug/g measured across three Chinese samples (249.30, 295.62 and 267.85 ug/g; Gong H et al., J Agric Food Chem 2018;66(30):7916-7922, PMID 29975518). Seeds do contain flavonoids and terpene trilactones occur in several tissues, but nothing in the seed approaches the 24%/6% standardised profile of a 50:1 leaf extract, so the edible organ does not supply the medicinal one.
items.dose_from_food_note: Clinical dosing is 120-240 mg/day of EGb 761. At a 35-67:1 drug-to-extract ratio that corresponds to 4.2-16 g of dried ginkgo leaf per day, and dried leaf is not something people eat; a leaf tea extracts only part of the terpene lactones and none of the concentration. Via the edible nut the gap cannot be closed at all, because the nut does not carry the leaf profile, and attempting it would be dangerous rather than merely futile: acute poisoning has been reported after 10-50 cooked seeds at one sitting, Hong Kong's Centre for Food Safety advises no more than 10 kernels a day for adults and three for children, and cooking does not destroy ginkgotoxin because it is heat-stable. Adult intoxication with seizures is documented (PMC7007935).
items.form_caveat: Two separate caveats, and both cut against food substitution. First, the safe food (the nut) and the studied medicine (the leaf extract) share no active profile; a bowl of ginkgo-nut congee is not a low dose of EGb 761. Second, the food itself has a hard ceiling: ginkgotoxin blocks pyridoxal-5'-phosphate-dependent enzymes including glutamate decarboxylase, so excess intake causes vomiting, irritability and convulsions, with children at much higher risk. Ginkgotoxin is present in leaf tissue as well, at far lower levels than in seed, and in a typical standardised leaf extract it sits below a 9 ppm limit of detection (Planta Med 2009, PMID 19288402; Toxicon 2021, PMID 34425140; J Nat Prod 2014, PMID 24432981); that 9 ppm figure supports the manufacturing argument better than the false absence claim it replaces. On the extract side, the concentration step is what makes standardisation possible and also what concentrates the hazards manufacturers must strip out: ginkgolic acids are strongly allergenic and are capped at 5 ppm, and unstandardised or adulterated ginkgo products (rutin or quercetin spiking to hit a flavonoid assay) are a recurring market problem. Ginkgo extract also inhibits platelet aggregation and interacts with anticoagulants, and lowers efavirenz and some other drug levels through CYP induction.
items.bioavailability: The two marker classes behave completely differently. Terpene lactones (ginkgolides A and B, bilobalide) are small, reasonably lipophilic and well absorbed after oral dosing of the standardised extract. The flavonol glycosides are not absorbed intact: gut microbiota hydrolyse them to quercetin, kaempferol and isorhamnetin aglycones, which are then heavily glucuronidated and sulfated, so plasma concentrations of the labelled compounds are very low and highly variable between people. This is the practical reason a leaf infusion is not a weak extract: hot water recovers a modest and inconsistent share of the terpene lactones, and the flavonoid fraction ends up as conjugated metabolites regardless. For the nut, the compound with real oral kinetics is ginkgotoxin, which is absorbed efficiently and has been measured in the serum of poisoning patients.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The EGb 761 specification and the derived 4.2-16 g/day dried-leaf equivalent were verified, as was the ginkgotoxin poisoning literature. Two of the entry's original factual claims failed verification and were corrected: the seed ginkgotoxin lower bound and the assertion that ginkgotoxin is absent from the leaf. A separate seed range of 170-404 ug/g could not be traced to the cited source and has been dropped rather than restated.
corrections_applied: Corrected the mature-stage seed ginkgotoxin range to 249-296 ug/g from the three measured values (249.30, 295.62, 267.85 ug/g). The submission's 187 ug/g lower bound understated the toxin ceiling its own nut-safety argument depends on by about 25%.
Dropped the separate 170-404 ug/g seed range, which is not in the cited source and could not be verified, rather than presenting it as sourced.

Corrected the factual error that ginkgotoxin is absent from the leaf: it is present in leaf tissue at far lower levels than in seed and sits below a 9 ppm limit of detection in typical standardised leaf extract (PMID 19288402, PMID 34425140, PMID 24432981).

Split the label into the two questions instead of a bare NOT_FOOD, so the entry now states plainly that the leaf extract is not a food while the seed is a genuine, widely eaten food carrying its own quantified intake ceiling.
Kept the verified EGb 761 specification and the 4.2-16 g/day dried-leaf equivalent unchanged.

items.food_status_note: Bacopa monnieri (brahmi, water hyssop) is a real leafy vegetable in parts of India, which makes it the exception among the herbal entries here. Ethnobotanical surveys in West Bengal's Terai-Dooars, Maharashtra, Assam and northeast India record it among wild edible greens gathered and cooked, with tender shoots and leaves eaten fresh, cooked as a green, or made into chutneys and raita, so bacosides genuinely enter the food supply in a way withanolides and valerenic acid do not. RICH here describes concentration, since a culinary serving reaches a fifth to a half of the clinical dose, and it is worth being explicit that this is one regional green rather than several ordinary foods: the availability is narrow and geographically limited, which is a different axis from concentration and is where the submission's TRACE label went wrong. Note the naming trap: in parts of India brahmi refers to Centella asiatica, a different plant with different actives (asiaticosides), and market material is frequently mixed.
items.dose_from_food_note: Trials use 300 mg/day of extract standardised to 50-55% bacosides, roughly 150-165 mg of bacosides. At the measured 6.54 mg/g for the two quantified bacoside constituents, that is about 23 g of dried brahmi herb per day, roughly eleven teaspoons of churna, which nobody eats in a day. A 2 g teaspoon of dried powder supplies 13.1 mg, about 9% of the dose. Converting to fresh greens requires a fresh-to-dry ratio the cited sources do not give, so only the dried figure is quoted: a realistic culinary serving of the fresh green, the quantity that goes into a thoran or a chutney, corresponds to single-digit grams of dry matter and therefore to a few tens of milligrams of bacosides, a fifth to a half of the trial dose. Eating brahmi as a vegetable is on the same scale as supplementing it without matching it, which is not true of anything else in this list except lion's mane. Total bacoside A also includes bacopasaponin C and a jujubogenin isomer that the cited analysis does not quantify, so the real herb content is somewhat higher than 6.54 mg/g and the gap correspondingly smaller.

foods.food: Bacopa monnieri (brahmi) dried aerial herb / churna powder, elite cultivar DBM-4
foods.per_100g: 654 mg of bacoside A3 plus bacopaside II (1.57 mg/g bacoside A3 and 4.97 mg/g bacopaside II in dry herbage)
foods.pct_rda_or_dose: about 9% of the roughly 150 mg of bacosides in a standard 300 mg dose of a 50-55% bacoside extract
foods.source: ICAR-Directorate of Medicinal and Aromatic Plants Research, Anand, variety release note for Bacopa monnieri DBM-4 (2020), https://icar.org.in/node/13442. Both figures, the DBM-4 designation and the CIM-Jagriti comparison were verified exactly; the verification pass called this the best-sourced food figure in the submission. Accession-level bacoside A survey in Industrial Crops and Products, PII S0926669021011134, gives the surrounding variation.

items.form_caveat: Bacoside content in the herb varies several-fold with accession, season and harvest, which is exactly why breeding programmes select elite lines such as DBM-4, so a wild-gathered green is an unpredictable dose. Extraction matters too: bacosides are saponins recovered by hydroalcoholic extraction, and boiling a green in water for a curry leaches an unknown fraction into cooking liquid that may be discarded. The best-studied products (CDRI-08, BacoMind) are specific standardised extracts and their cognitive trial results should not be read across to eating the plant. Bacopa also has real dose-dependent gastrointestinal effects, cramping, nausea and loose stools, more prominent with the concentrated extract than with the vegetable, and it has cholinergic activity that could matter alongside cholinesterase inhibitors. Watch for Centella asiatica sold as brahmi, and for heavy metal accumulation, since Bacopa is a wetland plant with documented capacity to take up metals from sediment.
items.bioavailability: Bacosides are large triterpenoid saponin glycosides with poor membrane permeability and low oral bioavailability; the pharmacologically relevant species are thought to be the deglycosylated sapogenins (jujubogenin and pseudojujubogenin derivatives) generated by gut hydrolysis, which is why supplement makers push phospholipid-complex and nanoparticle formulations. Eating the whole green delivers the same glycosides embedded in a fibrous matrix with fat from the cooking medium, and it has never been compared head to head with an extract in humans, so the fresh-vegetable route is plausible and uncharacterised. The saponins themselves also have surfactant behaviour in the gut, which is part of why higher doses cause GI upset.
items.data_confidence: HIGH. The ICAR DBM-4 bacoside figures were verified exactly against the cited release note, including the variety designation, and every derived step recomputed correctly (654 mg per 100 g, 13.1 mg per 2 g teaspoon, about 9% of dose, 23 g and about eleven teaspoons for 150 mg). The one soft spot is that no fresh-to-dry ratio is available in the cited sources, so the fresh-green serving is described qualitatively rather than given a number.
corrections_applied: Reclassified from TRACE to RICH. The submission's own arithmetic showed a culinary serving reaching a fifth to a half of the trial dose, which is a genuine source rather than a trace one; its stated reason for TRACE described narrowness of geographic availability, not trace concentration.

Separated the two axes the old label conflated: food_status RICH now answers concentration, dose_from_food PARTIAL answers reachability, and the narrow geographic availability is stated as a caveat in the note rather than smuggled into the classification.
Kept every figure unchanged, since all of them were verified: 6.54 mg/g, 654 mg per 100 g, 13.1 mg per teaspoon, 9% of dose, 23 g and eleven teaspoons for 150 mg.
Kept the single dried-herb row rather than inventing a fresh-green row, because the cited sources give no fresh-to-dry ratio.

items.food_status_note: This is the one entry whose supplement organism is an ordinary culinary food. Hericium erinaceus is sold fresh in Asian markets and increasingly in Western ones, cooked like scallops or shredded into stir-fries, and it is the same organism used to make the fruiting-body supplement. The best-known human trial used no exotic extract: Mori and colleagues gave 3 g/day of dried Hericium powder, four 250 mg tablets containing 96% dry powder three times daily, to older adults with mild cognitive impairment (Phytother Res 2009;23(3):367-372, PMID 18844328, verified). RICH describes this one species in its several presentations (fresh, dried powder, dried slices), which are one food rather than several independent sources. The important limit is by tissue: the newer and more mechanistically interesting trials use erinacine-A-enriched MYCELIUM, and no amount of the edible fruiting body supplies erinacines. Other edible Hericium species exist, notably H. coralloides and H. americanum, which matters here because the composition paper the submission cited was about H. coralloides rather than H. erinaceus.
items.dose_from_food_note: For the fruiting-body dose there is essentially no gap. At 8-11% dry matter, the 3 g/day of dried powder used in the Mori trial is about 27-38 g of fresh lion's mane, a small side portion, or 3 g of dried slices, or a rounded half-tablespoon of powder. A 100 g fresh portion supplies 8-11 g of dry matter, roughly 270-370% of that dose. The gap reappears with a concentrated extract: 3 g/day of a nominal 8:1 hot-water extract corresponds to about 24 g of dried mushroom, roughly 218-300 g of fresh mushroom a day, which is a lot of mushroom and still not absurd. For erinacine-A products the answer is NO at any portion size, because erinacines are mycelial and the fruiting body sold for cooking does not contain them at meaningful levels.

items.form_caveat: The compound classes split cleanly by tissue and by solvent, and this is where most consumer confusion lives. Hericenones C-H occur in the fruiting body; erinacines A-I occur in the mycelium, with erinacine biosynthesis genes consistently downregulated in fruiting-body tissue and no detectable erinacine production there (Fungal Biol Biotechnol 2025, PMC11969743, verified). The Taiwanese trials in early Alzheimer's disease and in depression used erinacine-A-enriched mycelium capsules at around 5 mg/g erinacine A, three 350 mg capsules a day giving 1,050 mg mycelia and about 5.25 mg erinacine A over 49 weeks (PMC7283924, verified), so their results cannot be transferred to eating the mushroom, and equally the Mori fruiting-body result cannot be transferred to a mycelium product. Solvent matters as much as tissue: hericenones are lipophilic and are recovered by ethanol while hot-water extraction recovers polysaccharides, so a dual extract and a hot-water extract deliver different chemistry at the same milligram figure. The specific polysaccharide numbers the submission used to make that point (4.85-5.68% of dry weight for the fruiting body and 3.62% beta-glucan for a hot-water extract) are withdrawn here, because neither is present in the paper cited for them. Many cheap US supplements are mycelium grown on grain and sold with the substrate included, so a large fraction of the capsule weight is starch; a starch assay or a low beta-glucan number relative to labelled polysaccharide is the tell. Safety is good for a food, with occasional contact dermatitis and respiratory allergy reports, and scattered case reports of skin reactions with supplement use.
items.bioavailability: The fungal beta-glucans are not absorbed intact; a water-soluble 1-3/1-6 beta-glucan of about 13.3 kDa has been characterised from the fruiting body, and such polymers act on gut and gut-associated immune receptors rather than entering circulation, so how much reaches the blood is the wrong question for the polysaccharide fraction. The small molecules are the ones with systemic potential: erinacine A is lipophilic, crosses the blood-brain barrier in rodents and is the compound behind the neurotrophic claims, while hericenones are also lipophilic and their human absorption is poorly characterised. Practically, fat in the pan helps the hericenone fraction, a water-based soup extracts the polysaccharides, and the raw mushroom is not the right comparator for either since chitinous cell walls need heat to break down. The relevant food-versus-supplement difference here is which molecules are present at all rather than absorption efficiency.
items.data_confidence: LOW. Every composition figure in this entry traces to one paper that turned out to be about a different species: J Fungi 2025;11(11):785 analysed only Hericium coralloides, and the submission truncated its title to Hericium. The 91.68% moisture that generated every dose-gap number was an H. coralloides measurement, the H. erinaceus proximate values appear in that paper only as an untraced quotation from its reference [29], and the 4.85-5.68% polysaccharide range is absent from the paper altogether. The replacement moisture figure used here is the published 89-92% band rather than a specific re-traced H. erinaceus measurement. What is solid is the dose side: the Mori 3 g/day protocol, the 4 x 250 mg x 3 arithmetic, the 5 mg/g erinacine A figure and the tissue-partition claim were all verified.
corrections_applied: Fixed the species misattribution at the foundation of the entry: 91.68% moisture is a measured H. coralloides value, so it has been replaced with the published H. erinaceus band of 89-92% and flagged as indicative rather than re-traced.

Recomputed every figure that depended on it: 100 g fresh now gives 8-11 g dry matter and 270-370% of dose (was 8.3 g and 275%); 3 g dried now equals 27-38 g fresh (was 36 g); an 8:1 extract at 3 g/day now equals 218-300 g fresh per day (was about 290 g).

Fixed the provenance of the proximate values: they are H. erinaceus figures quoted from reference [29] of PMC12653868 rather than measured there, and the paper's own H. coralloides measurements are named separately so the two are no longer silently mixed.
Consolidated the three table rows into two, since fresh, powder and dried slices are one food in three presentations and the three-row layout made RICH look like multiple independent sources.
Kept RICH but scoped it explicitly: it holds against the Mori fruiting-body dose and cannot cover erinacine-A mycelium products, and dose_from_food YES now carries that exception in the note.

Kept the verified dose-side figures unchanged: 3 g/day Mori dose, 4 x 250 mg x 3, 5 mg/g erinacine A, 1,050 mg mycelia and 5.25 mg erinacine A per day, and the 167%/333% dried-portion percentages.

items.food_status_note: St John's wort is the dried flowering aerial parts of Hypericum perforatum, a European meadow plant with no culinary use anywhere. It is consumed only as a medicine: tea, tincture, oil macerate or standardised dry extract. The two constituents that define it, hypericin (a naphthodianthrone) and hyperforin (a prenylated phloroglucinol), are confined to Hypericum species and are absent from the food supply, so there is no food route at any dose. Pharmacopoeial and commercial standards specify 0.3% hypericin, and the well-studied extract WS 5570 is an 80% ethanolic extract at a drug-to-extract ratio of 3:1 to 7:1 containing 0.12-0.28% hypericin and 5-6% hyperforin. One point worth carrying across from the melatonin entry: Hypericum perforatum is itself among the richest melatonin-bearing botanicals on record at roughly 4,490 ng/g dry weight, which is a curiosity about the plant rather than a reason to eat it.
items.dose_from_food_note: Standard antidepressant dosing is 300 mg of standardised extract three times daily, 900 mg/day, delivering roughly 1.1-2.5 mg of hypericin (900 mg x 0.12-0.28%) and 45-54 mg of hyperforin. At a 3:1 to 7:1 drug-to-extract ratio that corresponds to about 2.7-6.3 g of dried herb per day. There is no food equivalent to compute at any portion size, because hypericin and hyperforin do not occur in foods. This is a complete absence rather than a large multiplier.
items.form_caveat: The most consequential caveat in the whole set, and it runs opposite to the usual pattern: here the concentrated product is the dangerous one and there is no safe whole-food version to fall back on. Hyperforin is a potent activator of the pregnane X receptor and therefore a strong inducer of CYP3A4, CYP2C19 and P-glycoprotein. It lowers plasma levels of combined oral contraceptives (breakthrough bleeding and contraceptive failure are documented), ciclosporin and tacrolimus (with reported transplant rejection, including graft loss), warfarin, digoxin, HIV protease inhibitors and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, irinotecan and imatinib, and several anticonvulsants. Combined with SSRIs, SNRIs, triptans or tramadol it can precipitate serotonin syndrome. Hypericin causes dose-dependent photosensitisation. Preparation type changes the risk profile substantially: hyperforin is lipophilic and unstable, so a water infusion delivers far less of it than an ethanolic extract, and low-hyperforin extracts were developed specifically to reduce interactions. A tea, a tincture and a capsule labelled with the same herb weight are not interchangeable, and treating this plant as a gentle food-adjacent botanical is the central error.
items.bioavailability: Hyperforin is well absorbed from oil-containing or ethanolic preparations, has a long elimination half-life on the order of nine hours and accumulates with three-times-daily dosing, which is why enzyme induction builds over one to two weeks and takes a similar period to wash out after stopping. Hypericin absorption is slow, low and variable, with a much longer half-life still. Both are lipophilic, so an aqueous tea extracts a small and inconsistent share, particularly of hyperforin, and hypericin is light-sensitive and degrades in poorly stored material. Since there is no food form, the practical absorption question is preparation rather than matrix, and the answer is that interaction risk tracks hyperforin exposure rather than the labelled hypericin percentage most products still advertise.
items.data_confidence: MEDIUM. The NOT_FOOD classification was challenged and upheld, and the hyperforin dose (45-54 mg/day) and dried-herb equivalent (2.7-6.3 g/day) both recompute correctly. The hypericin figure had to be corrected by recomputation from the entry's own specification, and the only quantitative composition figure in the original entry carried no citation at all and has been withdrawn, so the entry now rests entirely on the extract specification rather than on any measured plant-material content.
corrections_applied: Corrected the hypericin delivered by 900 mg/day to 1.1-2.5 mg (900 mg x 0.12-0.28% = 1.08-2.52 mg). The submission's 0.9-2.7 mg came from a 0.1-0.3% assumption that contradicted the WS 5570 specification it quoted two sentences earlier.

Withdrew the claim that dried Hypericum leaf material measures around 5.1 mg/g total hypericins. It carried no citation in the submission and none could be located, and it was the entry's only quantitative composition figure.
Kept the verified figures unchanged: hyperforin 45-54 mg/day and the 2.7-6.3 g/day dried-herb equivalent.
Kept the NOT_FOOD classification, which was challenged and upheld.
Added the point flagged by the verification pass that Hypericum perforatum is itself among the richest melatonin-bearing botanicals recorded, at about 4,490 ng/g dry weight.
Split the label into the two questions: NOT_FOOD for the substance, NO for the dose.

items.food_status_note: 5-hydroxytryptophan is not a dietary constituent. In living tissue it exists only as a transient intracellular intermediate between tryptophan and serotonin, immediately decarboxylated by aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase, so it does not accumulate in any food at measurable levels. The commercial article is a purified single molecule, either extracted from the seeds of Griffonia simplicifolia, a West African climbing shrub whose seeds are an unusual botanical accumulator at 156 mg/g dry weight (about 16%) in a chemically characterised reference sample against literature concentrations of 10-20%, or, increasingly, produced by microbial or enzymatic biosynthesis. Griffonia seed is a pharmaceutical raw material rather than a food, which is why SYNTHETIC fits better than the NOT_FOOD label used for botanical drugs such as valerian or ashwagandha. The foods listed below are tryptophan sources, a different molecule one step upstream, scored against the WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 adult requirement of 4 mg tryptophan per kg per day (280 mg/day for a 70 kg adult) rather than against any 5-HTP dose.
items.dose_from_food_note: For 5-HTP itself the gap is absolute: no food contains it in measurable quantity, so no eating quantity reproduces the 50-300 mg/day used in trials. From the manufacturing raw material, 100 mg of 5-HTP sits in about 0.64 g of Griffonia seed at 156 mg/g, a striking number and irrelevant to eating, since Griffonia seed is not a food and carries other constituents. Via the dietary precursor the arithmetic runs deceptively the other way. An ordinary mixed diet supplies roughly 900-1000 mg of tryptophan a day, three to twenty times a 5-HTP dose by mass, and a single chicken breast supplies 434 mg, yet that intake does not act like 5-HTP for three reasons. Over 95% of tryptophan is degraded down the kynurenine pathway by TDO and IDO, with only about 1-2% passing through tryptophan hydroxylase to serotonin (PMC5398323; PMC9292703). Tryptophan competes with the other large neutral amino acids, leucine, isoleucine, valine, phenylalanine and tyrosine, for the LAT1 transporter at the blood-brain barrier, and every protein food raises tryptophan and its competitors together, so a high-protein meal can leave the brain tryptophan ratio flat or lower. And tryptophan hydroxylase is the regulated rate-limiting step, so raising substrate does little. 5-HTP sidesteps all three: it is past the rate-limiting hydroxylation and is decarboxylated by ubiquitous AADC. Adding 300 mg of tryptophan to a meal is therefore not equivalent to 300 mg of 5-HTP, and no realistic quantity of food makes it so.

items.form_caveat: Bypassing the pathway's regulation is what makes 5-HTP a drug rather than a nutrient. AADC is present throughout peripheral tissues, so much of an oral 5-HTP dose is converted to serotonin outside the central nervous system, which produces the characteristic nausea and is why clinical protocols historically paired 5-HTP with a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor such as carbidopa. Combined with SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs, tramadol, triptans or linezolid, 5-HTP carries a genuine serotonin syndrome risk that no amount of dietary tryptophan does. There is also a contamination history worth naming: the 1989 eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome epidemic was traced to a contaminant in bacterially produced L-tryptophan, and a related peak X impurity has been detected in some 5-HTP preparations, so purity of a purified plant extract or fermentation product is not a given. Note also that commercial 98% 5-HTP claims are computed on identified compounds rather than on seed weight, and one commercial extract labelled 95% assayed at about 65%. Griffonia seed should not be eaten as a food substitute; the whole seed carries other constituents and is not characterised for dietary safety. Nothing about the tryptophan-rich foods above raises comparable concerns; they are food, and the warm-milk folklore is folklore. Separately, the food table here is narrower than it should be: it contains no legume, no plant-protein concentrate and no cheese richer than cheddar, and dried spirulina, soybeans and soy protein isolate, Parmesan, sesame seeds, turkey, tuna, oats and peanuts are all absent. No figures for them could be verified in this pass, so they are named rather than tabulated, but their absence makes the requirement look harder to meet than it is.
items.bioavailability: The whole point of 5-HTP is that its absorption route differs from its precursor's. 5-HTP is absorbed from the small intestine and crosses the blood-brain barrier without competing significantly for the LAT1 large-neutral-amino-acid carrier, so plasma and brain 5-HTP rise roughly in proportion to dose, unlike tryptophan whose brain entry depends on the tryptophan-to-LNAA ratio rather than on absolute intake. Dietary tryptophan absorption from protein foods is efficient at the gut level, over 90%, and the losses that matter are metabolic rather than absorptive: hepatic TDO is induced by cortisol and by tryptophan itself, and IDO is induced by inflammation, so illness, stress and high-protein intake all divert precursor toward kynurenine. This is why the classic dietary manoeuvre for raising brain tryptophan is a carbohydrate load with little protein, using an insulin-driven fall in circulating branched-chain amino acids to improve the ratio, an effect measured in single-digit percentage changes and nothing like a 100 mg 5-HTP capsule.
items.data_confidence: HIGH for what remains. All six USDA tryptophan values were confirmed against SR Legacy with no errors, all six per-portion and percent-of-requirement figures recompute correctly against the verified WHO/FAO/UNU denominator of 280 mg/day, and the Griffonia 156 mg/g figure and the 0.64 g per 100 mg calculation were verified against full text. Two Griffonia figures that could not be found in their cited source have been withdrawn rather than restated, and the cheddar value carries the verifier's caveat that the USDA number is probably an imputation artefact.
corrections_applied: Withdrew the Griffonia figures of 111 mg/g for yellow-endosperm seeds and 70 mg/g for discoloured ones. Two full-text passes over the cited source (PMC6472197) found no seed-appearance stratification; the paper analysed a single non-stratified batch.
Corrected the Griffonia literature range from 10-18% to 10-20% of dry weight, matching the cited paper.

The commercial article is a purified or fermented single molecule, either extracted from a pharmaceutical raw material or biosynthesised, which is a different situation from the botanical drugs (valerian, ashwagandha) that NOT_FOOD describes.

Used the two-field split to resolve the label sitting awkwardly over a six-row food table: food_status now describes 5-HTP itself, and the prose states separately that the tabulated foods are tryptophan sources for a different molecule scored against a nutrient requirement rather than a supplement dose.

items.food_status_note_zh: 褪黑素确实广泛存在于各类植物性和动物性食物中，其中含量最高的并不是人们常提到的那些水果和坚果：烘焙咖啡、红葡萄酒和发芽豆类的含量远高于酸樱桃或核桃。即便如此，任何现实份量都比 0.5-5 mg 的补充剂剂量低一到四个数量级。补充剂与膳食中的这种物质属于两回事：市售褪黑素为化学合成产物，并非从食物中提取，所以标着“天然褪黑素”出售的产品其实是人工制造的分子；如果本字段描述的是药片而非物质本身，标签应为 SYNTHETIC。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 要摄入 1 mg，大约需要 104 g 烘焙咖啡粉，这是所有食物中最接近的，而咖啡粉不会被整份吃下（冲泡时转入杯中的比例未经表征）；或 7.7 L 红葡萄酒；或约 918 g 干物质计的发芽扁豆；或 1.9 kg 干物质计的发芽菜豆；或 5.3 kg 白芥子；或按综述值 103 ng/g 干重计算的 9.7 kg 干枸杞；或 23 kg 葫芦巴籽、34 kg 葵花籽、42 kg 番茄、74 kg Montmorency 酸樱桃、89 kg 草莓、286 kg 核桃、485 kg Balaton 酸樱桃、818 kg 杏仁、约 655-670 kg 鸡蛋（13,100-13,400 个）以及约 64,500 L 牛奶。开心果无法给出单一数值：点估计为 383 kg，但报告的标准差（3096 pg/g）超过均值（2609 pg/g），因此真实需求量在两个方向上都有约一个数量级的不确定性。0.5 mg 剂量把上述数字减半，5 mg 剂量乘以五。原稿的核心结论称枸杞是人类理论上唯一能吃到剂量的食物，经修正后不成立，因为它依赖一个未被重复验证的离群值；按权威值计算，表中没有任何食物能在可食用的份量内达到补充剂剂量。
items.form_caveat_zh: 食物中的褪黑素并不等于一片药的缩小版。酸樱桃浓缩汁按每天 2 x 30 mL 服用，可测量地升高尿中 6-硫酸氧褪黑素，并改善了活动记录仪测得的睡眠效率（Howatson 等，Eur J Nutr 2012;51(8):909-916, PMID 22038497，已核实），但本次未能找到该浓缩汁的褪黑素含量数据，所以唯一在人体睡眠终点上取得阳性结果的制剂仍无法折算；它提供的褪黑素不足一微克，效应大部分可能来自多酚基质和色氨酸的可得性。品种差异盖过其他一切因素：Montmorency 和 Balaton 属同一物种，含量相差 6.5 倍。两种富含褪黑素的药用植物可作参照：黄芩约 7,110 ng/g 干重，圣约翰草约 4,490 ng/g 干重，后者在自己的条目中归为 NOT_FOOD，同时又属于已记录的褪黑素含量最高的植物之列。关于开心果的争议：2014 年一篇荧光分光法论文报告约 233 µg/g 干重，约为 LC-MS/MS 值的 89,300 倍，该文已被公开发表关注声明（原文 PMID 24878439；关注声明见 Spectrochim Acta A 2019;217:322, PMID 31027610）。按这个存疑数值，4.3 g 开心果（约七粒）就能提供 1 mg，正因如此，这个数字应被视为未经确认，不能当成靠食物补充褪黑素的方案。关注声明记录只列出四位原作者，也没有提到任何重复实验失败，因此原稿把它归因于德国联邦风险评估机构的说法已被删除。补充剂一侧：常见售卖的 3-10 mg 剂量是生理替代剂量的十到三十倍；对市售产品的独立检测多次发现含量与标签严重偏离，并偶有血清素污染；褪黑素在英国和欧盟大部分地区属处方药，在美国则作为补充剂自由销售。
items.bioavailability_zh: 褪黑素的口服绝对生物利用度低且个体差异极大，平均约 15%（报告范围大致 9-33%，个体值相差可达五倍），原因是最多 85% 在首过过程中被清除，主要经肝脏 CYP1A2。因此影响 CYP1A2 的因素比来源更重要：咖啡因会提高同等剂量下的血浆褪黑素，吸烟则会降低。食物基质中纳克到低微克级的量是否遵循同样的动力学，目前一无所知，而在这个量级上该问题几乎只有学术意义。把开心果里的“天然褪黑素”和药片相比，等于拿亚微克级的摄入量去比一个超生理剂量。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。樱桃数值、核桃数值、开心果的 LC-MS/MS 数值、牛奶数值、存疑的 233 µg/g 数值以及 89,300 倍的比值均已对照原始文献核实，生物利用度数字也与既有文献一致。另一方面，本条目原来的锚点（枸杞）不得不换成综述值，鸡蛋数值不得不从干固形物基准改算为鲜重基准，而新增的十行全部依赖一份汇编性的二手综述表格（PMC5409706），本轮未回溯其原始测定。

items.food_status_note_zh: 小檗碱是一种异喹啉类生物碱，来自多种药用植物的根、根茎和茎皮：欧洲小檗（Berberis vulgaris，刺檗）、B. aristata、B. asiatica 和 B. lycium，黄连（Coptis chinensis）根茎，北美黄连（Hydrastis canadensis，goldenseal），俄勒冈葡萄（Mahonia aquifolium）以及黄檗（Phellodendron amurense）。这些器官都不作为食物食用。蓄积以根组织最高，小檗属各物种为干重的 1.6-4.3%，欧洲小檗树皮总生物碱超过 8%，其中约 5% 是小檗碱（Neag 等，Front Pharmacol 2018, PMC6111450，已核实）。小檗果实是真正被吃的部分，即伊朗米饭菜里的 zereshk（干酸浆果），而它属于另一个器官：那项在 96 个种质中报告根部小檗碱高达 26,482 µg/g、果肉未检出生物碱的全株调查，用的是达尔文小檗（Berberis darwinii，智利 michay），它是 zereshk 所属物种的同属近缘种，并非同一种植物；而且在该研究中叶和种子确实含有可检出的（较低的）生物碱水平，只有果肉为未检出（Molecules 2025;30(8):1849, PMID 40333914）。物种问题由另一组直接研究 B. vulgaris 果实的工作作了结：该研究报告花、果肉和种子几乎不含或不含有意义量的生物碱，并把其果实提取物描述为几乎不含小檗碱（Iran J Pharm Res 2011;10(1):97-104, PMID 24363687）。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 试验用量为每次 500 mg、每天两到三次，即 1000-1500 mg/天。按欧洲小檗根皮 5% 的小檗碱含量计算，相当于每天 20-30 g 干根皮，这属于草药煎剂的范畴，不是一餐饭。走可食用果实这条路，差距无法用一个倍数表示，它是未定义的：小檗碱在小檗果肉中低于检出限，任何份量都达不到剂量。一份量足的 zereshk polow（酸浆果抓饭）大约用 30-50 g 干果，还要分给好几个人，提供的小檗碱不可测。黄连根茎和北美黄连根需要 1-3 g 干药材，而两者都不作为食物食用。
items.form_caveat_zh: 本组数据中，食物与其补充剂只共享一个植物名的情况，这一条最为典型。吃 zereshk 得到的是维生素 C、花青素和有机酸，没有小檗碱的药理作用。分离出的生物碱在 1000-1500 mg/天的用量下表现如同药物：它抑制 CYP3A4 和 CYP2D6，同时是 P-糖蛋白的底物和抑制剂，因而可能升高同服药物的浓度；常见不良反应为便秘、腹部绞痛和腹泻；孕妇和新生儿禁用，因为小檗碱会把胆红素从白蛋白上置换下来，并与核黄疸风险相关。全株根提取物还含小檗胺和巴马汀，北美黄连中另含北美黄连碱（hydrastine），所以小檗根提取物和纯化的盐酸小檗碱胶囊是两种不同产品。北美黄连另外还涉及物种保护问题，也是物种掺假的常见对象。
items.bioavailability_zh: 小檗碱的口服生物利用度低于 1%，在大鼠中测得 0.36-0.68%，约 99.5% 在胃肠道和肝脏首过过程中被清除，机制包括溶解性差、在胃酸中自聚集、P-糖蛋白外排以及 CYP 介导的肠道代谢（Expert Opin Drug Metab Toxicol 2023;19(3), PMID 37057922）。一般认为小檗碱的代谢效应大部分发挥在肠腔内和对微生物组的作用上，而非全身性作用，所以生物利用度低并不等于没有活性。它确实意味着食物中的任何微量在药理上都无关紧要，也意味着剂型比较（普通盐、磷脂复合物、胶束）在同一标注剂量下可使暴露量相差一个数量级。
items.data_confidence_zh: 高。本条目中每一项定量说法都经过核对并与来源逐字相符：1.6-4.3% 的根部含量范围、欧洲小檗树皮总生物碱 8% 与小檗碱约 5% 的数据、根部最高 26,482 µg/g、96 个种质的果肉未检出，以及 20-30 g 根皮的剂量等效量。NOT_FOOD 分类经过质疑后仍然维持。

items.food_status_note_zh: 南非醉茄是 Withania somnifera 的根，有时是根加叶，该植物是茄科的一种小灌木。这个根属于药材，不属于膳食成分：味苦，通常做成 churna 药粉或用牛奶煎煮服用，任何菜系都不把它当配料。其活性成分是甾体内酯类，即睡茄内酯（withanolides），如 withaferin A、withanolide A 和 withanone，只见于醉茄属及少数近缘属，在食物供应链中不存在。人们真正吃的茄科作物，番茄、马铃薯、茄子、甜椒和辣椒，含的是另一类甾体化合物（番茄苷、茄碱等糖苷生物碱），所以植物学上的亲缘关系在这里没有帮助。近缘种 Withania coagulans 的果实在一些地区用作素食凝乳剂，那是加工助剂，并不构成睡茄内酯的膳食来源。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 试验用量为标准化根提取物 300-600 mg/天。KSM-66 是仅用根的提取物，标准化到至少 5% 睡茄内酯；Sensoril 是根加叶提取物，含量 10%；Shoden 标准化到 35% 睡茄内酯糖苷。因此典型每日剂量约相当于 15-60 mg 睡茄内酯。传统做法用 3-6 g/天的干根粉达到大致相当的水平。任何份量的食物都无法提供这个量，因为没有食用植物含睡茄内酯。要给出某种普通食物的等效重量，就必须凭空编一个含量值，所以诚实的答案是：膳食途径不存在。
items.form_caveat_zh: 用哪个部位很关键，监管机构的态度同样关键。只用根的制剂，安全性资料比含叶和地上部分的制剂更完整，后者 withaferin A 含量更高，而它是睡茄内酯中细胞毒性最强的一个。丹麦禁止在食品补充剂中使用南非醉茄；荷兰国家研究院 RIVM 发布了醉茄属制剂的风险评估（RIVM 报告 2024-0029）；法国主管部门建议特定人群不要使用；英国食品标准局记录到不良事件报告上升，其专家委员会审查了与甲状腺毒性、低血糖和肝毒性的关联；澳大利亚 TGA 在 2026 年 7 月发布药品安全通报，指出与南非醉茄相关的肝损伤报告持续出现，判定为特异质性反应。KSM-66 的牛奶提取工艺是营销上的区别，谈不上安全性上的区别。睡茄内酯含量还随化学型、栽培条件和植物部位变化，所以同样毫克剂量的两个产品，在真正起作用的成分上可能相差数倍。
items.bioavailability_zh: 人体药代动力学数据薄弱，无法有把握地给出标准生物利用度数值。睡茄内酯亲脂、水溶性差，这也是传统制备用牛奶或酥油、现代产品加磷脂或环糊精载体的原因。睡茄内酯糖苷（withanosides）水溶性更好，是 Shoden 标准化所用的标志物，因此两个标签上的“睡茄内酯百分比”可能指化学上不同的成分池，并由不同方法测定。由于没有食物形式，也就无从比较食物与补充剂的吸收；有意义的比较是不同提取物类型之间的比较，而这一点并未标准化。
items.data_confidence_zh: 食物与剂量判定为高。NOT_FOOD 判定经质疑后维持，睡茄内酯剂量的算术（300-600 mg 提取物按 5-10% 计得 15-60 mg）核实无误，本条目也没有可能出错的食物成分数值。核查环节明确认可了拒绝编造睡茄内酯食物含量值的做法。监管方面的陈述不在数值核查范围内。

items.food_status_note_zh: 补充剂用的是红景天（Rhodiola rosea，roseroot）的根茎和根，它是景天科的一种北极高山肉质植物，以 rosavins（rosavin、rosin、rosarin）和红景天苷（salidroside）为标准化指标。这个根茎是斯堪的纳维亚和俄罗斯的民间药材，不作为食物食用。这种植物并非完全不见于食物记录：在格陵兰、阿拉斯加和北美北部，嫩叶和嫩芽被生食或像菠菜一样煮食，茎则像芦笋一样烹煮，因纽特人会把叶和芽混着海生动物脂肪一起吃。那种食用涉及的是地上部分，而 rosavins 是根茎成分，加上可食嫩芽的成分数据很少，所以这段饮食史无法转化为标志物成分的膳食来源。rosavins 还几乎只见于 R. rosea，这正是物种替代问题长期存在的原因。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 典型用量为 200-600 mg/天的提取物，标准化到 3% rosavins 和 1% salidroside（SHR-5 模式），约合每天 6-18 mg rosavins 和 2-6 mg salidroside。干根茎的等效量完全取决于假定的含量，而这里引用的 0.01-3.08% rosavin 与 0.07-2.91% salidroside 范围是市售成品的含量，不是实测的根茎含量，因此原料含量无法由该来源确定。把假定明确写出来：按 1-3% rosavins 计，0.2-1.8 g 干根茎含一日剂量；按 0.1-0.5% 计为 1.2-18 g；按所引范围的下限 0.01% 计为 60-180 g。原稿一律给 0.5-2 g，暗中采用了范围上限，乐观程度最多达两个数量级。无论采用哪个假定，这都是一种根类草药的剂量，没有食物能提供；可食的嫩芽则根本无法折算，因为成分研究做的是根茎材料。
items.form_caveat_zh: 红景天的品种真实性记录尤其糟糕。一项对美国市场红景天补充剂的分析发现，rosavin 含量在 0.01% 到 3.08% 之间，salidroside 在 0.07% 到 2.91% 之间，与标签声称有很大偏差，同时还做了重金属和农药残留筛查（The quality and safety of Rhodiola rosea supplements on the U.S. market, PLoS One 2026, PMC12810810，已核实）。这些是成品数据，不是原料数据，原稿把这一区别模糊掉了。Rhodiola crenulata（大花红景天）是常见的替代品，它含 salidroside 但几乎不含 rosavin，所以只按 salidroside 标准化的产品可能是另一个物种。野生 R. rosea 面临采挖压力，已列入 CITES 附录二。田间材料随克隆株和产地差异极大，挪威采集材料中 salidroside 的克隆间变异达到 92.8%，因此产地和采收季节对产品的影响比标签更大。
items.bioavailability_zh: salidroside 吸收迅速并水解为酪醇（tyrosol），rosavins 属肉桂醇糖苷，会被肠道菌群脱糖基，所以血浆暴露反映的是代谢产物，而不是标签上的标志物；受控的人体药代动力学数据有限，无法给出可靠的百分比数值。由于没有食物形式，实际的吸收问题变成了提取溶剂：水醇提取物能同时回收 rosavins 和 salidroside，而根的水浸提液优先回收糖苷。咀嚼生嫩芽是唯一真正接近食物的途径，它从未被表征过。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。NOT_FOOD 分类经质疑后维持，所引的标志物含量范围也核实为真实且切题，但那些范围是市售成品的含量，原稿把它们当成了原料含量，因此干根茎的剂量等效量现在给出的是一个依赖假定的宽区间，不再是一个确定数字。可食用的地上嫩芽没有成分数据，这条途径完全无法量化。

items.food_status_note_zh: 缬草是欧洲多年生植物 Valeriana officinalis 的根和根茎。它在任何菜系里都不是食物；它是一种味苦、气味强烈的药材，以茶、酊剂或干提取物胶囊的形式服用。被认为产生镇静作用的成分，缬草酸（valerenic acid）及其同系物，加上黄酮类 6-methylapigenin、橙皮苷（hesperidin）和 linarin，只见于缬草属植物，在食物供应链中没有。缬草根曾以低水平用作某些饮料的香味成分，这让少数产品中含有微量，那属于香料级用量，比任何有镇静作用的量低几个数量级。称得上食物的东西没有一种能提供缬草酸。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 典型用法是睡前 400-900 mg 干根提取物，或 2-3 g 干根泡饮。商业原料的质量目标建议干根中缬草酸不低于 3 mg/g，市售提取物按约 0.8% 缬草酸销售，所以一晚的剂量大致相当于 3-8 mg 缬草酸。任何份量的食物都不能提供可测量的缬草酸，所以没有可以计算的进食量。这里的差距是彻底的缺失，不是一个大倍数。
items.form_caveat_zh: 缬草是“制备方式决定化学成分”的教科书式例子。缬草酸浓度在储存期间明显下降，在 30 C 低湿条件下损失最大（Food Chemistry 2009, changes in valerenic acid content of valerian root during long-term storage），所以一瓶放久的胶囊和一瓶新的是不同的产品。某些制剂中的缬草素（valepotriates）不稳定，会降解为 baldrinals；水提和乙醇提取回收的组分差别很大，这也是缬草临床试验结果如此不一致的原因之一。实用注意事项：与酒精、苯二氮类和抗组胺药有叠加镇静作用；偶见反常性兴奋；有罕见的肝毒性报告，通常出现在多草药复方产品中。同样标注克数的缬草茶和标准化提取物胶囊并不能互换。
items.bioavailability_zh: 人体数据有限。口服后血浆中可检出缬草酸，半衰期约一到两小时，这符合它作为睡前用药而非日间用药的定位；黄酮类成分会经历大量葡萄糖醛酸化。由于没有食物形式，也就没有食物基质的比较可做；有意义的变量是提取方式，缬草酸亲脂，乙醇的回收率远高于水浸，所以一杯茶提供的量只是标注毫克数的提取物所暗示量的一小部分，而且难以表征。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。NOT_FOOD 分类经质疑后维持，缬草酸剂量的算术（每晚 3-8 mg）核实无误。3 mg/g 的质量目标和 0.8% 的提取物含量各自只有一条二手引用支撑，储存稳定性的说法在数值核查中未逐项验证。

items.food_status_note_zh: 补充剂是浓缩的叶提取物，而银杏叶不是食物：它用丙酮-水体系加工成标准化提取物，EGb 761 是其参照品，药材与提取物比为 35-67:1，含 22-27% 黄酮苷和 5-7% 萜类内酯（2.8-3.4% 银杏内酯 A、B、C 加 2.6-3.2% 白果内酯），银杏酸控制在 5 ppm 以下。同一物种确实有真实的食物形式，这也是笼统的 NOT_FOOD 标签会掩盖的事情：白果（银杏种子）出现在日本茶碗蒸、中国粥品和韩国菜里，它在化学上与叶完全是另一回事。种子含银杏毒素（ginkgotoxin，即 4'-O-甲基吡哆醇及其 5'-葡萄糖苷），一种维生素 B6 拮抗剂，三份中国样品在成熟期测得的总含量为 249-296 µg/g（249.30、295.62 和 267.85 µg/g；Gong H 等，J Agric Food Chem 2018;66(30):7916-7922, PMID 29975518）。种子确实含黄酮类，萜类三内酯也存在于多个组织中，但种子里没有任何成分接近 50:1 叶提取物 24%/6% 的标准化谱型，所以可食的器官无法提供药用的那个器官。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 临床用量为 EGb 761 120-240 mg/天。按 35-67:1 的药材提取物比，相当于每天 4.2-16 g 干银杏叶，而干叶不是人们会吃的东西；叶茶只能提取出一部分萜类内酯，也完全没有浓缩效果。走可食用的白果这条路，差距根本无法弥补，因为白果不含叶的成分谱，而且尝试这么做是危险的，并非只是徒劳：一次吃 10-50 颗熟白果已有急性中毒报告，香港食物安全中心建议成人每天不超过 10 颗、儿童不超过 3 颗，而烹煮不能破坏银杏毒素，因为它耐热。成人中毒伴惊厥已有记录（PMC7007935）。
items.form_caveat_zh: 这里有两条独立的警告，都不利于用食物替代。第一，安全的食物（白果）和被研究的药物（叶提取物）没有共同的活性谱；一碗白果粥不是小剂量的 EGb 761。第二，这个食物本身有硬性上限：银杏毒素会阻断依赖 5'-磷酸吡哆醛的酶，包括谷氨酸脱羧酶，因此摄入过量会引起呕吐、易激惹和抽搐，儿童风险高得多。银杏毒素在叶组织中同样存在，水平远低于种子，在典型的标准化叶提取物中低于 9 ppm 的检出限（Planta Med 2009, PMID 19288402；Toxicon 2021, PMID 34425140；J Nat Prod 2014, PMID 24432981）；这个 9 ppm 的数字比它所取代的“叶中不含”的错误说法更能支持工艺层面的论证。提取物一侧，浓缩这一步既让标准化成为可能，也把厂家必须去除的危害一起浓缩了：银杏酸致敏性强，限量为 5 ppm，而未标准化或掺假的银杏产品（用芦丁或槲皮素掺入以凑够黄酮测定值）是市场上反复出现的问题。银杏提取物还抑制血小板聚集，与抗凝药有相互作用，并通过诱导 CYP 降低依非韦伦等一些药物的血药浓度。
items.bioavailability_zh: 两类标志物的行为完全不同。萜类内酯（银杏内酯 A 和 B、白果内酯）分子小、亲脂性适中，口服标准化提取物后吸收良好。黄酮醇糖苷不会以原形吸收：肠道菌群把它们水解为槲皮素、山奈酚和异鼠李素苷元，随后大量葡萄糖醛酸化和硫酸化，所以标签成分的血浆浓度很低且个体间差异很大。这正是叶泡水不能算作弱提取物的实际原因：热水只回收出一部分萜类内酯，比例还不稳定，而黄酮组分无论如何最终都变成结合型代谢物。对白果来说，真正有口服动力学意义的化合物是银杏毒素，它吸收效率高，并已在中毒患者血清中被测出。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。EGb 761 的规格及由此推出的 4.2-16 g/天干叶等效量均已核实，银杏毒素中毒文献同样核实。本条目原有的两项事实性说法未通过核查并已更正：种子银杏毒素的下限，以及银杏毒素不存在于叶中的断言。另一个 170-404 µg/g 的种子范围无法追溯到所引来源，已删除而未重述。

items.food_status_note_zh: Bacopa monnieri（brahmi，假马齿苋）在印度部分地区是真正的叶菜，这让它成为本组草药条目中的例外。西孟加拉 Terai-Dooars 地区、马哈拉施特拉、阿萨姆和印度东北部的民族植物学调查记录它属于采集后烹食的野生食用绿叶菜，嫩梢和叶被鲜食、当青菜炒煮，或做成酸辣酱（chutney）和 raita，所以假马齿苋皂苷（bacosides）确实以睡茄内酯和缬草酸做不到的方式进入了食物供应。这里的 RICH 描述的是浓度，因为一份普通菜量就能达到临床剂量的五分之一到一半；有必要明确的是，这只是一种地方性绿叶菜，而非若干常见食物：可获得性狭窄且地域受限，那是与浓度不同的另一个维度，也正是原稿 TRACE 标签出错的地方。注意名称陷阱：在印度部分地区，brahmi 指的是积雪草（Centella asiatica），那是另一种植物，活性成分不同（积雪草苷类，asiaticosides），市场上的原料经常混用。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 试验用量为 300 mg/天、标准化到 50-55% bacosides 的提取物，约合 150-165 mg bacosides。按实测的两种 bacoside 成分合计 6.54 mg/g 计算，相当于每天约 23 g 干 brahmi 药材，约合十一茶匙 churna 药粉，没有人一天吃这么多。一茶匙 2 g 干粉提供 13.1 mg，约为剂量的 9%。换算成新鲜绿叶需要所引来源没有给出的鲜干比，所以这里只列干重数据：一份现实的鲜菜量，也就是做 thoran 或 chutney 会用的分量，对应个位数克的干物质，因而是几十毫克的 bacosides，即试验剂量的五分之一到一半。把 brahmi 当菜吃，量级上与吃补充剂接近，只是达不到同等水平，这在本列表中除猴头菇外没有别的例子。此外，bacoside A 总量还包括所引分析未定量的 bacopasaponin C 和一个 jujubogenin 异构体，所以药材的真实含量比 6.54 mg/g 更高一些，差距也相应更小。
items.form_caveat_zh: 药材中的 bacoside 含量随种质、季节和采收期变化数倍，这正是育种项目要选育 DBM-4 这类优良品系的原因，所以野采的绿叶菜是一个不可预测的剂量。提取方式同样重要：bacosides 是皂苷，靠水醇提取回收，而把青菜在水里煮成菜肴时，会有不确定比例浸入可能被倒掉的汤汁。研究最充分的产品（CDRI-08、BacoMind）是特定的标准化提取物，其认知功能试验结果不应照搬到吃这种植物上。假马齿苋还有明确的剂量依赖性胃肠道反应，绞痛、恶心和稀便，浓缩提取物比蔬菜更明显；它具有胆碱能活性，与胆碱酯酶抑制剂同用时可能需要注意。要留意积雪草被当作 brahmi 出售，也要留意重金属蓄积，因为假马齿苋是湿地植物，有从底泥中吸收金属的明确能力。
items.bioavailability_zh: bacosides 是大分子三萜皂苷糖苷，膜通透性差，口服生物利用度低；一般认为具药理意义的形式是肠道水解生成的脱糖基皂苷元（jujubogenin 和 pseudojujubogenin 衍生物），这也是补充剂厂家推磷脂复合物和纳米制剂的原因。整棵菜吃下去，提供的是同样的糖苷，只是嵌在纤维基质中并伴随烹调油脂，而它从未在人体上与提取物做过头对头比较，所以鲜菜途径可行但未被表征。皂苷本身在肠道内还有表面活性行为，这也是高剂量引起胃肠不适的部分原因。
items.data_confidence_zh: 高。ICAR 的 DBM-4 bacoside 数据已逐项对照所引品种发布说明核实，包括品种名称，各步推导也重算无误（每 100 g 654 mg、每 2 g 茶匙 13.1 mg、约为剂量的 9%、150 mg 需 23 g 和约十一茶匙）。唯一的薄弱处是所引来源没有鲜干比，所以鲜菜份量只作定性描述，没有给出数字。

foods_zh.food_zh: 假马齿苋（brahmi）干地上部药材 / churna 药粉，优良品种 DBM-4
foods_zh.pct_zh: 约为标准剂量（50-55% bacoside 提取物 300 mg 中约 150 mg bacosides）的 9%

items.food_status_note_zh: 这是唯一一条补充剂原生物本身就是普通食用食材的条目。Hericium erinaceus（猴头菇）在亚洲市场有鲜品出售，西方市场也越来越多，做法像干贝一样烹调或撕成丝炒菜，它与制作子实体补充剂用的是同一种生物。最著名的人体试验没有用什么特殊提取物：Mori 等人给轻度认知障碍的老年人每天 3 g 猴头菇干粉，即每次四片 250 mg（含 96% 干粉）、每天三次（Phytother Res 2009;23(3):367-372, PMID 18844328，已核实）。RICH 描述的是这一个物种的几种形态（鲜品、干粉、干片），它们属于同一种食物，并非几个独立来源。重要的限制按组织划分：更新、机制上更有意思的那些试验用的是富含 erinacine A 的菌丝体，而供食用的子实体无论吃多少都不含 erinacines。还存在其他可食的猴头菌属物种，尤其是 H. coralloides 和 H. americanum，这一点在此很重要，因为原稿引用的成分论文研究的是 H. coralloides，并非 H. erinaceus。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 就子实体剂量而言基本没有差距。按 8-11% 干物质计，Mori 试验用的 3 g/天干粉相当于约 27-38 g 鲜猴头菇，一小份配菜的量，或 3 g 干片，或略满的半汤匙干粉。100 g 鲜品提供 8-11 g 干物质，约为该剂量的 270-370%。换成浓缩提取物，差距就回来了：标称 8:1 的热水提取物 3 g/天相当于约 24 g 干菇，即每天约 218-300 g 鲜菇，量不小但仍不算荒唐。对于 erinacine A 类产品，答案在任何份量下都是 NO，因为 erinacines 存在于菌丝体，供烹调出售的子实体不含有意义量的 erinacines。
items.form_caveat_zh: 化合物类别按组织和溶剂清晰分开，消费者的困惑大多出在这里。Hericenones C-H 存在于子实体；erinacines A-I 存在于菌丝体，erinacine 生物合成基因在子实体组织中一致下调，该组织中检测不到 erinacine 生成（Fungal Biol Biotechnol 2025, PMC11969743，已核实）。台湾在早期阿尔茨海默病和抑郁症中的试验用的是富含 erinacine A 的菌丝体胶囊，erinacine A 约 5 mg/g，每天三粒 350 mg 胶囊，即 1,050 mg 菌丝体、约 5.25 mg erinacine A，持续 49 周（PMC7283924，已核实），所以它们的结果不能转用到吃这种菇上；同样，Mori 的子实体结果也不能转用到菌丝体产品上。溶剂和组织同等重要：hericenones 亲脂，靠乙醇回收，而热水提取回收的是多糖，所以在相同毫克数下，双提取物和热水提取物提供的化学成分不同。原稿用来支持这一点的具体多糖数值（子实体干重的 4.85-5.68%，以及热水提取物 3.62% 的 β-葡聚糖）在此撤回，因为所引论文中没有这两个数据。美国许多便宜补充剂是在谷物上培养的菌丝体，连培养基一起出售，所以胶囊重量里有很大一部分是淀粉；淀粉检测，或 β-葡聚糖数值相对标注多糖含量偏低，都是识别线索。作为食物，它的安全性良好，偶有接触性皮炎和呼吸道过敏报告，服用补充剂后也有零星皮肤反应的个案报告。
items.bioavailability_zh: 真菌 β-葡聚糖不会以原形吸收；已从子实体中表征出一种约 13.3 kDa 的水溶性 1-3/1-6 β-葡聚糖，这类聚合物作用于肠道及肠道相关免疫受体，并不进入循环，所以对多糖组分来说，“有多少进入血液”是个提错的问题。有全身作用潜力的是小分子：erinacine A 亲脂，在啮齿类中可穿过血脑屏障，是神经营养相关说法背后的化合物；hericenones 也亲脂，其人体吸收情况表征很差。实际操作上，锅里的油脂有助于 hericenone 组分，水基汤品提取的是多糖，而生菇对两者都不是合适的参照，因为几丁质细胞壁需要加热才能破坏。这里食物与补充剂的真正差别是哪些分子存在，吸收效率是次要问题。
items.data_confidence_zh: 低。本条目的每个成分数值都追溯到同一篇论文，而那篇论文研究的是另一个物种：J Fungi 2025;11(11):785 只分析了 Hericium coralloides，原稿把它的标题截短成了 Hericium。生成全部剂量差距数字的 91.68% 水分是 H. coralloides 的测定值；H. erinaceus 的常规成分值在该论文中只是引自其参考文献 [29] 的未追溯引用；4.85-5.68% 的多糖范围在该论文中完全不存在。这里采用的替代水分数值是已发表的 89-92% 区间，并非重新追溯的某个 H. erinaceus 具体测定值。可靠的是剂量一侧：Mori 的 3 g/天方案、4 x 250 mg x 3 的算术、5 mg/g erinacine A 的数据以及组织分布的说法均已核实。

foods_zh.food_zh: 猴头菇（Hericium erinaceus），新鲜子实体，烹调前的生品
foods_zh.portion_zh: 100 g，一份量足的配菜，或约三分之一个中等大小的子实体
foods_zh.pct_zh: 约为 Mori 轻度认知障碍试验所用 3 g/天干粉剂量的 270-370%

foods_zh.food_zh: 猴头菇（Hericium erinaceus），干粉或干片，同一种食物的脱水形式
foods_zh.portion_zh: 1 汤匙干粉（5 g），或 10 g 干片（复水后约 100 g）

items.food_status_note_zh: 圣约翰草是贯叶连翘（Hypericum perforatum）的干燥开花地上部分，这是一种欧洲草地植物，任何地方都没有烹饪用途。它只作为药物使用：茶、酊剂、油浸剂或标准化干提取物。定义它的两个成分，金丝桃素（hypericin，一种双蒽酮）和贯叶金丝桃素（hyperforin，一种异戊烯基间苯三酚类化合物），只存在于金丝桃属物种，食物供应链中没有，所以任何剂量下都不存在食物途径。药典和商业标准规定 0.3% 金丝桃素，研究充分的提取物 WS 5570 是 80% 乙醇提取物，药材与提取物比为 3:1 至 7:1，含 0.12-0.28% 金丝桃素和 5-6% 贯叶金丝桃素。有一点可以从褪黑素条目带过来：贯叶连翘本身是已记录含褪黑素最丰富的植物之一，约 4,490 ng/g 干重，这属于关于这种植物的趣闻，不构成吃它的理由。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 标准抗抑郁用量为标准化提取物 300 mg、每天三次，即 900 mg/天，提供约 1.1-2.5 mg 金丝桃素（900 mg x 0.12-0.28%）和 45-54 mg 贯叶金丝桃素。按 3:1 至 7:1 的药材提取物比，相当于每天约 2.7-6.3 g 干药材。任何份量都没有食物等效量可算，因为金丝桃素和贯叶金丝桃素不存在于食物中。这是完全的缺失，不是一个大倍数。
items.form_caveat_zh: 这是整组数据中后果最严重的一条警告，而且方向与常见情况相反：这里危险的是浓缩产品，也没有安全的全食物版本可以退守。贯叶金丝桃素是孕烷 X 受体的强效激动剂，因此是 CYP3A4、CYP2C19 和 P-糖蛋白的强诱导剂。它会降低复方口服避孕药（已有突破性出血和避孕失败的记录）、环孢素和他克莫司（有移植排斥报告，包括移植物失功）、华法林、地高辛、HIV 蛋白酶抑制剂和非核苷类逆转录酶抑制剂、伊立替康和伊马替尼，以及若干抗惊厥药的血药浓度。与 SSRI、SNRI、曲普坦类或曲马多合用时，可诱发血清素综合征。金丝桃素会引起剂量依赖性光敏反应。制备类型对风险谱影响很大：贯叶金丝桃素亲脂且不稳定，水浸提液提供的量远低于乙醇提取物，低贯叶金丝桃素提取物就是专为减少相互作用而开发的。标注同样药材克数的茶、酊剂和胶囊不能互换，而把这种植物当成温和、接近食物的植物制品，正是核心错误。
items.bioavailability_zh: 贯叶金丝桃素在含油或乙醇制剂中吸收良好，消除半衰期约九小时，每天三次给药会累积，所以酶诱导在一到两周内逐步建立，停药后也需要相似时间才能消退。金丝桃素吸收缓慢、量低且波动大，半衰期更长得多。两者都亲脂，所以水煮的茶只提取出很小且不稳定的一部分，尤其是贯叶金丝桃素；金丝桃素对光敏感，在储存不当的材料中会降解。由于没有食物形式，实际的吸收问题是制备方式而非基质，答案是相互作用风险跟随贯叶金丝桃素暴露量，而不是跟随多数产品至今仍在宣传的金丝桃素百分比。
items.data_confidence_zh: 中。NOT_FOOD 分类经质疑后维持，贯叶金丝桃素剂量（45-54 mg/天）和干药材等效量（2.7-6.3 g/天）重算均无误。金丝桃素数值需按本条目自身的规格重新计算才得到更正，而原条目中唯一的定量成分数据完全没有引文，已被撤回，所以本条目现在完全依赖提取物规格，不依赖任何实测的植物材料含量。

items.food_status_note_zh: 5-羟基色氨酸不是膳食成分。在活体组织中，它只作为色氨酸到血清素之间的瞬时细胞内中间体存在，会被芳香族 L-氨基酸脱羧酶立即脱羧，因此不会在任何食物中蓄积到可测量的水平。市售产品是纯化的单一分子，或从 Griffonia simplicifolia（西非一种攀缘灌木）的种子中提取，该种子是不寻常的植物蓄积体，一份经化学表征的参照样品达 156 mg/g 干重（约 16%），文献浓度为 10-20%；或者越来越多地由微生物或酶法生物合成得到。Griffonia 种子是药用原料，不是食物，这就是 SYNTHETIC 比用于缬草、南非醉茄这类植物药的 NOT_FOOD 标签更贴合的原因。下面列出的食物是色氨酸来源，那是上游一步的另一个分子，评分依据是 WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 年成人需要量每公斤体重每天 4 mg 色氨酸（70 kg 成人 280 mg/天），而非任何 5-HTP 剂量。
items.dose_from_food_note_zh: 就 5-HTP 本身而言，差距是绝对的：没有食物含有可测量的量，所以没有任何进食量能重现试验所用的 50-300 mg/天。从生产原料看，按 156 mg/g 计算，100 mg 5-HTP 存在于约 0.64 g Griffonia 种子中，这个数字很惊人，与吃东西无关，因为 Griffonia 种子不是食物，还含有其他成分。走膳食前体这条路，算术的方向反而具有欺骗性。普通混合膳食每天提供约 900-1000 mg 色氨酸，按质量计是 5-HTP 剂量的三到二十倍，单块鸡胸肉就提供 434 mg，但这种摄入不会像 5-HTP 那样起作用，原因有三。超过 95% 的色氨酸经 TDO 和 IDO 沿犬尿氨酸通路降解，只有约 1-2% 经色氨酸羟化酶转向血清素（PMC5398323；PMC9292703）。色氨酸要与其他大分子中性氨基酸（亮氨酸、异亮氨酸、缬氨酸、苯丙氨酸和酪氨酸）竞争血脑屏障上的 LAT1 转运体，而每种蛋白质食物都会同时提高色氨酸和它的竞争者，所以一顿高蛋白餐可能让脑内色氨酸比值持平甚至下降。而色氨酸羟化酶是受调控的限速步骤，提高底物作用很小。5-HTP 绕开了这三点：它已越过限速的羟化步骤，并由普遍存在的 AADC 脱羧。因此在一餐中加 300 mg 色氨酸并不等于 300 mg 5-HTP，任何现实的食物量都做不到这一点。
items.form_caveat_zh: 绕过该通路的调控，正是 5-HTP 成为药物而非营养素的原因。AADC 遍布外周组织，所以口服 5-HTP 的很大一部分在中枢神经系统之外被转化为血清素，这产生了典型的恶心反应，也是临床方案历来把 5-HTP 与卡比多巴等外周脱羧酶抑制剂配伍使用的原因。与 SSRI、SNRI、MAOI、曲马多、曲普坦类或利奈唑胺合用时，5-HTP 有真实的血清素综合征风险，而膳食色氨酸无论多少都没有这种风险。还有一段值得点明的污染史：1989 年嗜酸性粒细胞增多-肌痛综合征的暴发被追溯到细菌法生产的 L-色氨酸中的一种污染物，某些 5-HTP 制剂中也检出过相关的 peak X 杂质，所以纯化植物提取物或发酵产品的纯度并非理所当然。另外，市售 98% 5-HTP 的说法是按已鉴定化合物计算的，不按种子重量计算；一份标称 95% 的市售提取物实测约 65%。Griffonia 种子不应当作食物替代品食用；整粒种子含有其他成分，膳食安全性未经表征。上面那些富含色氨酸的食物没有类似问题，它们就是食物，而睡前热牛奶的说法只是民间说法。还有一点：这里的食物表比应有的范围窄，其中没有豆类、没有植物蛋白浓缩物，也没有比切达更高的奶酪，干螺旋藻、大豆和大豆分离蛋白、帕玛森奶酪、芝麻、火鸡肉、金枪鱼、燕麦和花生全部缺失。本轮无法核实它们的数据，因此只点名不入表，但它们的缺席让需要量看起来比实际更难达到。
items.bioavailability_zh: 5-HTP 的关键在于它的吸收路径与前体不同。5-HTP 在小肠吸收，穿过血脑屏障时不与 LAT1 大分子中性氨基酸载体发生显著竞争，所以血浆和脑内 5-HTP 大致随剂量成比例上升；色氨酸进入脑内则取决于色氨酸与其他大分子中性氨基酸的比值，与绝对摄入量无关。蛋白质食物中的膳食色氨酸在肠道层面吸收效率高，超过 90%，真正重要的损失是代谢性的：肝脏 TDO 受皮质醇和色氨酸自身诱导，IDO 受炎症诱导，所以疾病、应激和高蛋白摄入都会把前体转向犬尿氨酸。这就是提高脑内色氨酸的经典膳食手段是低蛋白的高碳水负荷的原因，它借助胰岛素引起的循环支链氨基酸下降来改善比值，效应量以个位数百分比计，与一粒 100 mg 5-HTP 胶囊完全不在同一量级。
items.data_confidence_zh: 就保留下来的内容而言为高。六项 USDA 色氨酸数值全部对照 SR Legacy 确认无误，六个每份含量和占需要量百分比的数字按核实过的 WHO/FAO/UNU 分母 280 mg/天重算均正确，Griffonia 的 156 mg/g 数据和 100 mg 对应 0.64 g 的计算已对照全文核实。两个在所引来源中找不到的 Griffonia 数据已撤回而未重述，切达奶酪数值带有核查者的提示，即该 USDA 数字很可能是插补产物。
